title: assert() with a runtime-false condition is silently dropped instead of aborting
close_reason: Closed

title: (EPIC) Correctness fixes
description:
## Why
Beyond idiomization gaps (ugly-but-correct Rust), differential testing can surface actual semantic divergences between the C source and the generated Rust: cases where baseline lowering silently drops or misrepresents a side effect. These are correctness bugs, not readability work, and belong in a separate top-level epic so they never get deprioritized behind fixup/idiomization backlog.

## What to do
- Track and fix confirmed semantic divergences between C and generated Rust behavior (differing stdout, differing exit code, differing abort/panic behavior) discovered during any exploration, fixture audit, or fuzzing session.
- Each child bug must include a minimal C repro, the actual C binary behavior (stdout/exit code), and the actual generated Rust behavior, demonstrating the divergence concretely.
- Fixes must restore differential equivalence and land with a fixture under tests/fixtures/ that would have caught the regression.

## Success Criteria
- Every confirmed divergence has a landed fix plus a differential fixture pinning the corrected behavior.
- No open P0 bug lingers without an assigned root cause investigation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each child bug closes with a fixture demonstrating C/Rust equivalence restored.
- cargo nextest r --release passes with the new fixture included.

title: Thread proven function identity through lowering and semantic passes
description:
Why: every consumer that currently infers libc behavior from a function name can independently recreate the miscompile even after provenance exists in the frontend and AST types. Proven identity must become the sole authorization for idiomization and semantic summaries throughout Slate.

Scope:
- Thread typed function identity through baseline lowering, symbol tables, facts collection, fixup analysis, rewrite passes, effects summaries and interpreter models, and unused-extern pruning.
- Replace or gate every name-only standard-function classifier, including string_libc, call semantics, effect purity and summaries, allocation and I/O handling, and extern removal.
- Preserve ordinary call behavior for unknown, project-defined, indirect, aliased, or otherwise unproven functions.
- Add diagnostics or fact-debug output explaining why a same-name call was accepted or rejected where useful.
- Add end-to-end differential and effects regression coverage for trusted and adversarial same-name functions.
- Update provenance guarantee documentation and its link-time/runtime interposition boundary.
design: Downstream code may inspect symbol spelling for rendering and diagnostics, but semantic rewrites and summaries must require the typed proven identity. Remove compatibility adapters introduced by the type-system child once all consumers migrate. Default branches preserve baseline calls rather than assuming libc behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The epic reproducer translates and prints 5, with no constant strlen substitution. Trusted <string.h> strlen calls retain current valid idiomizations. Project strings.h declarations, project definitions, shadow headers, indirect calls, aliases, and unknown provenance never receive libc rewrites or effects. Project functions named like allocation, memory, string, and I/O APIs are not assigned standard semantics or pruned as unused externs. Repository search finds no semantic libc classification based only on callee string names unless it is explicitly limited to rendering or diagnostics. cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Rename KnownLibc to Known and expand it across all supported external standard APIs. Use one consolidated adversarial fixture covering every supported function, with exit last. Runtime interposition such as LD_PRELOAD is explicitly unsupported because it changes semantics out of band.
close_reason: Threaded Known function provenance through lowering, fixups, effects, and extern pruning; consolidated adversarial differential/effects fixture; documented interposition boundary; all gates pass

title: Represent external function provenance in the typed AST model
description:
Why: plugin evidence is useless if lowering collapses every callee to an untyped symbol name. The internal model needs an exhaustive distinction between proven standard functions and ordinary or unknown functions before any fixup can consume libc semantics.

Scope:
- Define typed identities for proven external functions, including an explicit unknown or ordinary classification.
- Add provenance-bearing call or callee nodes to the compact Clang AST facts and Rust AST instead of parallel string maps.
- Define the source-location join that attaches plugin call-site evidence to the corresponding Clang AST and CIR operation.
- Preserve direct versus indirect call identity and canonical signatures.
- Make printers, walkers, equality helpers, effects inputs, and test builders exhaustive over the new representation.

This child changes representation and transport boundaries only. Downstream passes may continue using compatibility adapters until the next child removes name-only behavior.
design: Use a strongly typed enum or equivalent AST node owned by the call/callee representation. Keep spelling and semantic identity separate: the source symbol remains available for baseline emission while optional proven semantics carry KnownLibc variants. Unknown must be the default, and constructing a known identity must require plugin evidence rather than a matching string.
acceptance_criteria: The compact Clang AST and Rust AST can represent two calls spelled strlen with distinct identities: KnownLibc::StrLen and unknown project function. Plugin facts join to calls by physical source location without assigning identity to unrelated same-name calls. Direct and indirect calls remain distinguishable. AST walkers and renderers compile exhaustively, baseline Rust emission is unchanged when provenance is unknown, and focused representation/join regression tests pass.
close_reason: Added typed call provenance to compact and Rust ASTs, joined plugin evidence through CIR source locations, distinguished direct and indirect calls, and added the differential strlen collision fixture.

title: Extract trusted function provenance in the Clang plugin
description:
Why: CIR and the rendered Rust AST retain external symbol names but not enough information to distinguish a standard-library declaration from a project declaration with the same name. Provenance must be captured while Clang still has the preprocessor include graph, physical file identities, declaration bindings, and redeclaration chains.

Scope:
- Extend the existing out-of-tree macro-dump plugin with PPCallbacks::InclusionDirective data for resolved physical FileEntryRef identities, include edges, written header names, angle-versus-quote form, and Clang header characteristics.
- Add an ASTConsumer that inspects direct CallExpr bindings, FunctionDecl canonical declarations and redeclarations, declaration expansion locations, bodies, and symbol-changing attributes.
- Establish a conservative trust policy for toolchain standard-header instances, including internal-header forwarding and project wrapper headers, without trusting basename or isInSystemHeader alone.
- Emit stable machine-readable call-site provenance facts keyed by physical source file and offset for later AST/CIR joining.
- Treat indirect calls and incomplete evidence as unknown.

The plugin gathers evidence only. It must not assign Rust fixup behavior or perform source rewriting.
design: Share one provenance collector between PPCallbacks and the translation-unit ASTConsumer. Build the resolved include graph during preprocessing, classify declaration chains after parsing, and emit call-site records only when the exact direct callee and trusted declaration ancestry are proven. Keep raw evidence distinguishable from semantic classification so diagnostics and future policies can explain rejection.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin output distinguishes a libc strlen declared through the toolchain-resolved <string.h> from a project-defined or project-header-declared strlen. Tests cover direct trusted calls, the epic reproducer with a project definition, an independent project strings.h declaration, a wrapper that includes trusted <string.h>, a shadow string.h on a normal project include path, internal libc header forwarding, macro-generated declarations, compatible redeclarations, symbol-changing attributes, and indirect calls. Unknown cases emit no trusted-function classification. The plugin builds against the configured CIR-enabled Clang and its output is deterministic.
close_reason: Implemented Clang plugin include/function provenance with physical header identities, AST redeclaration evidence, conservative rejection reasons, and 13 integration regressions. Verified plugin rebuild, cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo nextest r --release (736 passed). Merged into main as 44bf4c7.

title: Guarantee provenance for idiomized external functions
description:
Why: Slate currently assigns libc semantics and performs fixups by function name. A project-owned function with a reserved-looking name can therefore be replaced as though it were the standard-library function. The demonstrated case defines size_t strlen(const char *s) { return 5; }, but Slate folds strlen("hello world") to 11. This violates the projects correctness requirement and can affect string, memory, allocation, I/O, effects, and extern-pruning logic.

Scope:
- Establish trusted-header identity from the exact Clang invocation using an out-of-tree plugin and PPCallbacks::InclusionDirective. Record resolved physical file identity and include ancestry rather than trusting basename, angle-bracket spelling, or isInSystemHeader alone.
- Use Clang AST binding for direct calls and referenced declarations. Correlate CallExpr::getDirectCallee, canonical declarations, and redeclaration chains with trusted include provenance.
- Define conservative known-function identities such as KnownLibc::StrLen and preserve them through Clang AST extraction, CIR/source-location joining, baseline Rust AST lowering, fixup facts, effects summaries, and unused-extern pruning.
- Replace name-only semantic classification throughout the pipeline. Unknown, indirect, project-defined, aliased, weak, ifunc, asm-labeled, or otherwise unproven callees must retain ordinary external or project-call behavior.
- Document the guarantee boundary: source-level declaration provenance under the selected toolchain and normal libc linkage. Header provenance alone does not prove the link-time or runtime implementation under symbol interposition.
- Cover standard headers that re-export declarations through internal headers and project wrapper headers that include trusted standard headers.

Reproducer:
#include <stdio.h>
size_t strlen(const char *s) { return 5; }
int main() { printf("%ld\n", strlen("hello world")); }

Current wrong result: generated Rust replaces the project call with the known literal length 11 instead of calling the project strlen and printing 5.
design: Treat function semantics as typed provenance established before lowering, never as a property inferred from a rendered symbol name. InclusionDirective supplies resolved include identity; the completed Clang AST supplies call-to-declaration binding. Classify only direct calls whose compatible redeclaration chain contains a declaration exported through a trusted standard-header instance and contains no untrusted definition or symbol-changing attribute. Emit call-site facts keyed by physical source location so the CIR/AST join can carry the semantic identity into Rust AST nodes. Default to Unknown and decline idiomization whenever proof is incomplete.
acceptance_criteria: The reproducer prints 5 after translation and the generated Rust does not substitute strlen("hello world") with 11. A project header named strings.h that independently declares strlen is not classified as libc. A project wrapper header that includes the toolchain-resolved <string.h> preserves libc classification. A shadow string.h from an ordinary project include path is not trusted. Compatible redeclarations, macro-generated declarations, internal libc header forwarding, and direct versus indirect calls have differential regression coverage. All name-only libc semantic matching in fixups, effects, and extern pruning is removed or gated by typed known-function provenance. Unknown provenance always preserves baseline call semantics. cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.

title: Compile generated libyaml crate
description: Objective: make the Rust crate generated from ~/libyaml by translate-project --lib pass cargo check and then cargo build as a library crate. Regenerate the crate with the required libyaml include/version SLATE_CLANG_ARGS, fix each child root cause, and file new children only for new cargo check failures that appear after these are resolved. Passing libyaml's runtime tests is out of scope for this epic unless needed to validate compilation fixes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add library-mode project translation CLI
description: Objective: make Slate run against the libyaml library sources cloned at ~/libyaml. Add a library-mode project translation CLI path for C projects without a main translation unit, so libyaml can be translated as a library rooted at lib.rs instead of failing because translate-project requires main. The immediate bar is that the command runs properly over ~/libyaml and produces the library-shaped Rust output; it does not need to pass libyaml's tests or fully compile/link yet. File follow-up beads from the resulting failures and gaps.
close_reason: Implemented translate-project --lib to initialize a Cargo lib crate, translate library C sources into src modules, write src/lib.rs, and translate project tests into tests/*.rs. Verified with cargo test --test cross_tu, cargo nextest r --release, and a run against /home/takashi/libyaml generating /tmp/slate-libyaml-crate.

title: Lower generic CIR scalar op spellings
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.binop and cir.unary as P0 unsupported generic scalar spellings that can block ordinary C emitted by newer/different CIR producers.

What to do:
- Add parsing/lowering for cir.binop and cir.unary spellings.
- Reuse existing scalar arithmetic, bitwise, logical, and unary lowering semantics where possible.
- Add differential fixtures that force these spellings.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md when the ops are supported.
close_reason: cir.binop/cir.unary are incubator-only generic spellings; upstream ClangIR (our producer) emits split named ops (cir.add, cir.minus, ...) instead and never emits these, so they can't be differentially tested. Not implementing. Documented in docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.

title: Lower low-level CIR branch variants
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.brcond and cir.switch.flat as P0 unsupported control-flow variants. Slate supports structured branch/switch forms, but these lower-level forms can appear and should not block ordinary C.

What to do:
- Add parser and lowerer support for cir.brcond.
- Add parser and lowerer support for cir.switch.flat.
- Prefer structured Rust output when the CFG shape permits it; use conservative state-machine style only when needed.
- Add differential fixtures and update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: cir.brcond/cir.switch.flat come only from --cir-flatten-cfg, which Slate never runs. Verified: if/else, ternary, &&, ||, for, while, do-while, switch, goto all stay structured through Slate's emit pipeline (0 brcond/switch.flat). Supporting them would be untestable dead code. Documented in docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.

title: Complete MSVC cross-target verification and support documentation
description:
Turn the accumulated MSVC implementation into a stable completion gate for the parent epic. Consolidate the supported-header manifest, xwin oracle probes, fixture coverage, generated Rust checks, and COFF inspection into maintainable tests.

Audit every generated use of libc::FILE, libc::mbstate_t, libc::timespec, pthread types, and other host-libc assumptions. Replace or target-gate them so MSVC output uses correct generated types or core::ffi primitives. Verify conditional multi-target output where the same portable C declaration differs between MSVC and glibc or musl.

Document the supported architectures, UCRT/SDK and toolset versions, header surface, intentionally unsupported Windows SDK areas, version-update procedure, and the rule that users remain responsible for import libraries and final linking.
design: Use a manifest-driven verification matrix: libc-shim compilation proves declarations are self-consistent, pinned xwin probes prove ABI agreement, fixture translation proves Slate preserves it, cargo check proves valid Rust for installed MSVC targets, and llvm-readobj or llvm-nm proves COFF symbol identity. None of these layers substitutes for another.
acceptance_criteria: The documented MSVC manifest has automated libc-shim compilation, xwin signature/layout comparison, fixture translation, cargo check for each claimed Rust MSVC target, and COFF symbol inspection; generated code contains no incompatible Linux libc type assumptions; portable multi-target fixtures select correct MSVC versus glibc/musl declarations; all parent-epic acceptance criteria are met; cargo fmt, cargo clippy, focused tests, and cargo nextest r --release pass; documentation precisely states supported versions, architectures, headers, exclusions, and user linking responsibility.

title: Preserve MSVC calling conventions, imports, and exports
description:
Carry MSVC ABI metadata from Clang/CIR through Slate into generated Rust instead of hardcoding every foreign declaration and exported definition to an undifferentiated C ABI.

For the initial x86_64 target, verify ordinary C declarations, variadics, imported data accessors, dllimport, dllexport, explicit assembler or link names, and exported definitions. Add an internal representation that can later distinguish __cdecl, __stdcall, __fastcall, and __vectorcall, then exercise the distinctions with i686 reference probes before claiming 32-bit support. Verify ARM64 behavior before enabling that architecture.

Do not select import libraries or link the program. The output requirement is correct Rust ABI spelling, no_mangle/export behavior, link_name metadata, and COFF symbol identity.
design: Represent calling convention and import/export identity as first-class function or declaration metadata sourced from CIR and the Clang AST. Map to Rust extern C, extern system, or another supported Rust ABI only when that mapping is verified for the selected target. Keep unsupported conventions explicit rather than erasing them.
acceptance_criteria: Generated Rust preserves verified x86_64 MSVC foreign and export ABI metadata, symbol names, variadics, and data/function distinctions; COFF object inspection confirms representative import and export names without final linking; the lowering model can represent x86 calling-convention distinctions and rejects any convention without a correct Rust mapping; i686 and ARM64 are enabled only after dedicated probes pass; existing ELF and Mach-O behavior is unchanged.

title: Model UCRT macro redirects and imported symbol identities
description:
Make MSVC source spellings lower to the actual UCRT declarations and symbols used by generated Rust. Compilation against plausible prototypes is insufficient when a header macro or inline wrapper redirects the call.

Cover errno through _errno(), stdin/stdout/stderr through __acrt_iob_func(), time and stat selection macros, formatted-I/O common helpers, secure CRT wrappers, underscore-prefixed functions, locale-sensitive variants, intrinsic or inline substitutions that escape into CIR, and aliases selected by feature macros. Preserve source provenance through the macro-dump path where needed and emit explicit link names when the Rust identifier differs from the imported symbol.

Use object or AST probes against the pinned xwin headers to establish the post-preprocessing declaration and symbol identity for every supported redirect.
design: Treat macro-to-symbol identity as ABI data owned by the libc profile. Keep the public source spelling available to fixups while recording the concrete foreign identity that Rust must import. Do not hardcode UCRT redirects as global libc behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures for errno, standard streams, time/stat variants, formatted I/O, secure CRT functions, and representative inline redirects emit the same effective signatures and foreign symbol names as pinned xwin probes; generated Rust contains no invented extern data symbols or unresolved public-spelling functions where UCRT uses an accessor/helper; link-name rendering is structurally tested without requiring final linking; prior MSVC and Linux tests remain green.

title: Complete the public UCRT C header and type surface
description:
Expand the basic MSVC profile to the public ISO C and UCRT declaration surface required by the MSVC epic. Work header-family by header-family from failing C fixtures and pinned xwin comparison probes.

Model FILE and stream-related types, fpos_t, mbstate_t, locale handles, errno_t, rsize_t, time_t and clock types, div structures, signal types, process and environment declarations, math and floating-environment types, wide-character interfaces, time and stat variants, and other aggregates exposed by supported headers. Keep implementation-private objects opaque unless source code can observe their layout; reproduce exact layout whenever code may allocate, embed, initialize, pass by value, or access fields.

Partition declarations so Linux/POSIX extensions remain independent. Record which UCRT headers are supported and add separate follow-up beads for any header family that proves too large for this ticket.
design: Use the real xwin CRT and UCRT trees as an oracle and maintain clean declaration-only equivalents in libc-shim. Prefer shared ISO declarations with target-selected type definitions, but keep UCRT extensions and layouts in an MSVC overlay. Every new public type or function begins with a C fixture.
acceptance_criteria: Every header in the agreed public UCRT C manifest compiles through libc-shim for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc; fixtures exercise all exposed aggregate categories and divergent signatures; sizes, alignments, offsets, canonical parameter types, and return types agree with pinned xwin probes; unsupported headers are explicitly excluded or tracked; no Linux-only ABI leaks into MSVC; existing libc tests and the full release suite remain green.

title: Establish basic x86_64 MSVC libc-shim support
description:
Create the smallest correctness-checked MSVC libc profile that lets Slate parse and lower representative ISO C programs for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. Use the xwin sysroot only as an external oracle; all Slate compilation continues through declaration-only libc-shim headers.

Add an MSVC-specific supported-header manifest instead of feeding the existing Linux all-header list to Clang. Correct the fundamental LLP64 model: pointer-sized types are 64-bit while long is 32-bit, wchar_t is 16-bit, and long double follows the MSVC target ABI. Cover the core freestanding and hosted ISO C headers needed for simple programs, including stddef, stdint, stdarg, limits, float, assert, errno, ctype, string, stdlib, and minimal stdio declarations.

Ensure target feature selection accepts x86_64-pc-windows-msvc without exposing pthread, ioctl, fork, Linux sockets, or other POSIX/Linux declarations. Add C fixtures before implementation that demonstrate the current failures and verify generated Rust primitive types and ordinary extern C declarations.
design: Introduce a target-specific header surface manifest plus MSVC ABI branches in shared bits headers. Use compiler builtin type macros where they accurately encode the target. This milestone intentionally supports a narrow ISO C/UCRT subset and must diagnose or omit unsupported headers rather than guessing Linux-compatible declarations.
acceptance_criteria: With SLATE_TARGET=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, the focused MSVC header test compiles the documented basic manifest against libc-shim; representative C fixtures translate successfully; size_t, ptrdiff_t, intptr_t, uintptr_t, wchar_t, long, long long, and long double lower according to the MSVC LLP64 ABI; ordinary imported functions emit correct extern C signatures; Linux-only declarations are absent; comparison probes against the pinned xwin reference agree; existing glibc and musl header tests and the full release suite remain green; the supported basic surface and known omissions are documented.
close_reason: Implemented and validated the basic x86_64 MSVC libc-shim profile, LLP64 lowering, focused manifest, xwin probes, explicit Linux-header rejection, fixture coverage, and documentation

title: Bootstrap a pinned xwin MSVC reference sysroot under target
description:
Add a repository script that obtains a pinned xwin release and uses it to materialize the Microsoft CRT and Windows SDK reference sysroot under target/. The sysroot is an external test oracle and must remain ignored rather than being copied into libc-shim or committed.

The script must use repository-local paths for both the xwin executable/cache and the resulting sysroot, support at least x86_64, expose explicit CRT and SDK version pins, be safe to rerun, and fail with an actionable message when the Microsoft license has not been accepted. License acceptance must be explicit through an argument or environment variable rather than silently implied.

The resulting layout must make the CRT include directory and Windows SDK ucrt include directory easy for tests and developers to discover. Document the exact setup command, output paths, version-update procedure, and cleanup behavior. Do not add Windows UM, WinRT, libraries, or linking setup beyond what xwin necessarily downloads.
design: Prefer a tools/ script that installs or invokes a pinned xwin in target/msvc-tools, stores downloads in target/msvc-xwin-cache, and writes the splatted reference tree to target/msvc-sysroot. Keep all downloaded Microsoft artifacts beneath target/. Print or persist machine-readable include-root information for later tests without introducing tracked generated files.
acceptance_criteria: One documented command, after explicit license acceptance, creates a pinned and reproducible x86_64 MSVC reference sysroot under target/ containing crt/include and sdk/include/ucrt; no global xwin installation is required; a second invocation is idempotent; version pins are visible and updateable; failure modes explain missing cargo/network/license prerequisites; all downloaded or unpacked artifacts remain ignored; a smoke probe using the configured CIR Clang can include representative CRT and UCRT headers with target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.
close_reason: Added and validated pinned repository-local xwin MSVC header sysroot bootstrap and documentation

title: Support the MSVC libc ABI in libc-shim and generated Rust
description:
Objective

Allow Slate to translate C intended for the MSVC environment by using declaration-only headers that accurately describe the MSVC/UCRT ABI and by emitting compatible Rust foreign declarations. Slate does not link the result; library selection and final linking remain the responsibility of the user.

Initial scope

Start with x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and the ISO C plus core UCRT surface. Support source declarations, type layouts, macros that select runtime symbols, imported functions and data accessors, exported C definitions, and ordinary x86_64 Windows C calling convention behavior.

Required work

1. Replace the current LP64-versus-32-bit assumption with a data-model-aware type layer. MSVC x86_64 is LLP64: pointers and size_t are 64-bit while long remains 32-bit. Define correct size_t, ptrdiff_t, intptr_t, uintptr_t, wchar_t, time_t, clock_t, off_t variants, intmax types, long double behavior, and va_list behavior. Prefer Clang target builtin type macros where they express the ABI directly.

2. Separate public header surfaces by target libc and kernel. Common ISO C declarations may be shared, but Linux/POSIX declarations such as pthread, ioctl, fork, and Linux socket structures must not be advertised for MSVC. Add MSVC-specific bits headers or target-conditioned declarations without duplicating the entire include tree.

3. Model UCRT types and layouts needed by user-visible signatures, including FILE, fpos_t, mbstate_t, locale handles, errno_t, rsize_t, time and stat families, and other aggregate types encountered by supported headers. Keep types opaque when only pointer identity is observable; provide exact layout whenever C may allocate, embed, initialize, or access the object.

4. Add accurate UCRT declarations and macro behavior. In particular, model interfaces whose source spelling does not equal the imported symbol, such as errno through _errno(), standard streams through __acrt_iob_func(), time/stat selection macros, formatted I/O wrappers, underscore-prefixed CRT functions, and secure CRT functions. Generated Rust must reference the actual runtime symbol and signature rather than a declaration that merely parses.

5. Preserve foreign ABI and symbol identity. For the initial x86_64 UCRT scope, ordinary extern "C" is generally sufficient. The design must leave room for __cdecl, __stdcall, __fastcall, __vectorcall, decorated x86 names, dllimport, dllexport, and explicit link names when i686 or broader Windows API support is added. C definitions exported by the input must retain a public C ABI and stable export name in Rust.

6. Remove generated-code assumptions that libc crate Linux types are universally valid. Uses such as libc::FILE, libc::pthread_attr_t, libc::timespec, and libc::mbstate_t must either be restricted to compatible targets or replaced with generated target-specific types or core::ffi primitives.

7. Build a clean declaration-only shim from trustworthy references. Actual UCRT/MSVC headers used through clang-cl and official Microsoft ABI documentation are authoritative. MinGW headers may be used for comparison but are not an MSVC ABI reference. Do not vendor proprietary SDK headers.

Verification

Add MSVC-specific header manifests rather than compiling every Linux header. Compile supported headers with Clang targeting x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. Add C fixtures for each introduced signature, aggregate layout, macro-to-symbol mapping, import, and export. Verify generated Rust structurally, run cargo check for the MSVC Rust target without linking, and inspect generated COFF objects with LLVM tools where symbol spelling or export behavior matters. Use C static assertions or compiler record-layout output for sizes, alignments, and offsets.

Out of scope for the initial milestone

Windows SDK APIs, Winsock, COM, C++, SEH, compiler intrinsics beyond those required by UCRT declarations, i686-specific calling conventions and decoration, ARM64 Windows, import-library selection, final linking, and execution on Windows.
design: Use one common ISO C declaration layer with target-selected ABI and libc overlays. Do not make the existing all-public-headers Linux test pretend to represent MSVC; create a target surface manifest so unsupported headers are absent rather than silently exposing incompatible declarations. Treat compile success as necessary but insufficient: every declaration that can reach Rust needs signature, layout, symbol-identity, and calling-convention verification. Deliver x86_64 UCRT support first, then expand architecture and Windows SDK scope through child issues.
acceptance_criteria: For x86_64-pc-windows-msvc: Slate can parse and lower representative programs using every declared header in the supported ISO C/UCRT manifest; fundamental and exposed aggregate types match the MSVC LLP64/UCRT ABI; macro-backed interfaces lower to the correct imported symbols; generated foreign declarations preserve signatures and symbol names; exported input definitions retain the correct public C ABI; generated Rust passes cargo check for the MSVC target without linking; COFF symbol inspection tests pass where applicable; Linux glibc and musl header and differential tests remain green; documentation states the exact supported MSVC surface and exclusions. The epic is complete only after its child issues cover type modeling, header partitioning, UCRT declarations, symbol and calling-convention lowering, generated-type portability, and cross-target verification.

title: Fix libc-shim header compilation errors across targets
description: The ignored header_compilation test fails while compiling libc-shim headers for supported target triples. Fix all compilation errors, leaving warnings for later, with changes confined to libc-shim.
acceptance_criteria: cargo nextest r header_compilation --no-capture --run-ignored only passes for every target; all tracked edits are under libc-shim; cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and the full release suite pass.
close_reason: All 12 supported architecture/libc header compilations pass.

title: Scope SalsaFacts::sync to actually-touched functions via TouchedItems
description: slate-kby1.1's benchmark (src/fixups/salsa.rs::temp_bench, kept, do not delete) showed SalsaFacts::sync's current unconditional re-set of every function's body/bindings on every call forecloses all backdating benefit: full unconditional re-sync of 60 functions took ~1.06ms, versus ~170us when only 1 of 60 functions was actually touched (bypassing sync() and setting just that one FunctionInput directly) -- a ~6x loss from not scoping sync to what actually changed. Thread the plan's TouchedItems (src/fixups/query/plan.rs, already computed by plan.apply() and already consumed by IncrementalFacts::mark_touched) into SalsaFacts::sync so it only calls set_body/set_bindings for functions in touched.in_place, drops touched.removed entries from the registry, and only does a full whole-program sync when touched.unbounded is set or the registry is empty (first call / bootstrap - matches IncrementalFacts's own Dirty::Everything/Clean semantics, see docs/salsa-migration.md 'Bridging Program <-> salsa inputs'). Rewire the two DeadLocals call sites in fixups/mod.rs that currently call salsa_facts.sync(&program, &facts) unconditionally to pass the actual touched set instead.
acceptance_criteria: SalsaFacts::sync takes a touched-scope argument (or equivalent) and only mutates salsa inputs for functions that actually changed, removed, or are new; the registry stays complete after every sync call (every function in FixupFacts::functions has a corresponding, up-to-date FunctionInput), including on first bootstrap and after an unbounded/full sync; def_use/effect lookups for any function remain correct (no stale-cache regressions) -- verified by full nextest r --release staying green; the kept temp_bench harness (or an extension of it) demonstrates the live DeadLocals pipeline usage realizing a measurable speedup over today's unconditional-resync baseline, not just the isolated single-call measurement from kby1.1; cargo fmt/clippy clean.
close_reason: SalsaFacts::sync split into sync_all (full, safe bootstrap) and sync_touched (scoped to TouchedItems.in_place/removed). Both DeadLocals pipeline occurrences now: sync_all on their own first loop iteration (handles staleness from untracked intervening passes), sync_touched using the *previous* iteration's touched set paired with the *freshly re-resolved* facts/program on later iterations of the same fixpoint loop. Found and fixed a real correctness bug during implementation: an earlier version called sync_touched right after plan.apply() using that iteration's pre-edit facts for bindings against the already-mutated post-edit program body -- a body/bindings mismatch that broke buffer_pointer_cursor_uses_safe_array_indexes (dead_locals under-fired, cascading into a buffer_cursor match failure) and chibicc_supported_tests_match_c. Root cause: bindings are function-local derived facts that must come from the same (fresh) FixupFacts snapshot as the body being read, not from whatever pre_edit_facts happened to be in scope at the sync call site. Fixed by always pairing sync_touched's facts argument with a body read from the matching program snapshot. Full nextest r --release 221/221 green (full suite, not just the previously-failing tests) after the fix. title: heap_ownership.rs converted use-after-free to well-defined Box code, hiding UB
description: heap_uses_are_owned's linear scan recorded the free() call's position but never checked that later reads/writes in the same body occurred BEFORE it -- any heap_use matched after free was already recorded got silently appended to uses just like a pre-free use. Combined with fuse_scalar_box_initializers folding the first matching scalar write into Box::new(...), a C program with a use-after-free (malloc; free(x); *x = 4; printf(...);) got converted straight to 'let x: Box<i32> = Box::new(4);' -- turning a real memory-safety bug in the source C into clean, well-defined Rust. Differential testing didn't catch it because glibc doesn't scrub/unmap tiny freed allocations immediately, so both the buggy C and the 'fixed' Rust happened to print the same output.
close_reason:
Fixed. src/fixups/facts/heap_ownership.rs's heap_uses_are_owned loop recorded
free()'s position but never enforced that it comes last: once `free` was set,
subsequent realloc_at/pointer_alias_temp_from_any/heap_use matches on the same
pointer were still accepted and appended to `uses` with no ordering check.
Added `if free.is_some() { return None; }` guards to all three match arms
(realloc, alias, heap_use) right after the free-call arm, so any read, write,
realloc, or aliasing of the pointer found after its free() now rejects the
whole ownership candidate -- it falls back to baseline raw *mut T Rust
(preserving the same UB the C had, rather than silently resolving it).

Added tests/fixtures/heap_box_use_after_free_bailout.c (malloc; free(x);
*x = 4; printf(...);) and a matching structural-assertion test
(heap_owner_bails_out_when_a_use_follows_the_free_call in
tests/differential.rs) asserting the pointer stays raw and free() stays as an
explicit unsafe call. Verified all pre-existing heap_ownership fixtures
(heap_box_delayed_store, heap_vec_malloc/calloc/realloc, heap_box_fixup) still
convert correctly -- the fix only rejects candidates with a genuine
post-free use, not the ordinary allocate-use-then-free-last shape those cover.
Full cargo fmt / cargo clippy --release --all-targets /
cargo nextest r --release (216 passed, 2 skipped) all green.

Found while investigating an unrelated report against slate-04q.83.4's
Option<Box<T>> pass; this bug lives entirely in the pre-existing, separately
shipped heap_ownership.rs and has no other relation to that ticket.

title: fenv_t/femode_t are x86-64-only glibc layouts; wrong struct shape on ARM/RISC-V
description: libc-shim/include/fenv.h's fenv_t and femode_t are hardcoded to real glibc's x86-64 layout: an x87 FPU control/status/tag-word block plus an MXCSR field (see the struct's own fields: __control_word, __status_word, __tags, __eip, __cs_selector, __opcode, __data_offset, __data_selector, __mxcsr). This is not a sizing problem like the pthread types were — it is a fundamentally different STRUCT SHAPE per CPU family. ARM's floating-point environment is a single FPSCR register; RISC-V's is a single fcsr register; neither has an x87-style multi-field FSAVE block, MXCSR, or segment selectors. fegetenv/fesetenv/feholdexcept/feupdateenv/fegetmode/fesetmode are real libc symbols that read and write this memory directly by pointer, so on any non-x86 target today, Slate parses a struct with completely the wrong layout and real libc calls into it are memory-unsafe (reading/writing fields that don't correspond to anything the real function expects).
design: Fix per the epic's methodology: for each architecture Slate should support (x86_64, i686, aarch64, arm32, riscv64 at minimum — riscv32 has no real glibc target per the epic notes), get that architecture's REAL fenv_t/femode_t field layout (via the Debian-sysroot-download technique for glibc, or musl's arch/<arch>/bits/fenv.h source for musl) and give each its own #if-gated definition keyed on that architecture's predefined macro (__x86_64__, __aarch64__, __arm__, __riscv + __riscv_xlen for 32 vs 64-bit). Do not attempt a shared/superset layout — the field sets are genuinely incompatible across CPU families, unlike the pthread opaque-blob cases.
acceptance_criteria: fenv_t and femode_t have real, field-accurate (or correctly-sized/aligned opaque, if a field-accurate port isn't practical) definitions for each supported architecture, verified against real glibc/musl headers per the epic's methodology, not assumed. fegetenv/fesetenv-family differential fixtures (if any exist beyond tests/stdlib/fenv/) pass under each supported SLATE_TARGET.

title: Flip the libc shim to the default SLATE_CLANG parsing path
description:
Once the shim (slate-k89h.2) and the ctype.h flagship rewrite (slate-k89h.4) are both in place, make SLATE_LIBC_SHIM's directory the default target_args() behavior instead of an opt-in env var — i.e. system libc headers stop being what SLATE_CLANG parses in the common case.

This is also the point where several test-fixture assertions that were calibrated against real glibc's exact header structure need reconciling, since the shim intentionally produces cleaner (structurally different but equally correct) output in a few spots discovered during slate-k89h.2:
  • tests/differential.rs's c11_library_callbacks_preserve_c_abi asserts the generated Rust contains `struct __once_flag { f0: i32 }`, which only holds because real glibc's threads.h anonymous-typedefs its once_flag struct through an internal __once_flag alias first. The shim's clean single-level typedef legitimately produces `struct once_flag` instead — update the assertion.
  • tests/stdlib_coverage.rs's KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED list carries setjmp/setjmp (slate-nk3.19) as expected-to-fail; the shim's plain (non-macro) setjmp.h makes it pass. Remove that entry once the shim is default, to lock the win in.
  • slate-k89h.7's remaining cleanup (dropping the "_IO_FILE"/"__mbstate_t" glibc-internal-name fallbacks from clib_record_type) belongs here too.
  • The three ctype_classify_* differential tests presently fail under the shim because ctype.h's bitmask-macro shape no longer exists to pattern-match — slate-k89h.4 owns making that fixup logic work against the shim's plain function-call shape (or confirming it's no longer needed); this task should not proceed until that's resolved.
acceptance_criteria: target_args() parses with the shim by default (no SLATE_LIBC_SHIM env var required); cargo nextest r --release passes in full with no env var overrides; the once_flag assertion, the setjmp KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED entry, and slate-k89h.7's internal-name fallbacks are all updated/removed in the same change.
close_reason: target_args()/libc_shim_dir() now default to the repo's libc-shim/include when SLATE_LIBC_SHIM is unset (still overridable to another directory, or to empty to explicitly fall back to system headers). cargo nextest r --release passes 211/211 with zero env var overrides. Reconciled the three fixture assertions flagged in the description: c11_library_callbacks_preserve_c_abi now checks the shim's plain 'i32' once_flag (also simplified libc-shim/include/threads.h's once_flag from a glibc-shaped struct{__data} to a bare int, matching musl and avoiding gratuitous glibc-internal-field coupling — same size/alignment so real linked glibc's call_once is unaffected); stdlib_coverage's setjmp/setjmp KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED entry removed (now passes under the shim's plain setjmp.h); slate-k89h.7's _IO_FILE/__mbstate_t fallback-arm cleanup pulled in and done in this same change (see k89h.7 close reason).

title: Rewrite ctype.h against the shim as the flagship simplification case
description: ctype.h (ef00d5a, bb23375, 4ffe14d) is the motivating pain case: glibc's isupper/tolower-family macros expand through __ctype_b_loc()/__exctype bitmask internals that ctype_classify.rs and ctype_libc.rs have to pattern-match around. Re-declare these as plain extern functions in libc-shim's ctype.h so CIR only ever sees ordinary CallExprs, and confirm the existing ctype fixtures (ctype_libc_fixup.c, ctype_classify_*.c, setlocale variants) still pass — ideally with simpler matching logic in ctype_classify.rs/ctype_libc.rs, since the macro-bitmask special-casing should no longer be needed.
acceptance_criteria: All existing ctype_* fixtures pass against the shim. ctype_classify.rs/ctype_libc.rs no longer need to special-case glibc's macro-expansion bitmask shape (or that special-casing is proven still necessary and documented why).
close_reason: Extended Known/classify_function with direct is*() ctype calls (IsAlpha..IsSpace, header ctype.h) so classify_plan in ctype_classify.rs recognizes libc-shim's plain-function ctype.h shape directly, no bitmask-chain reconstruction needed. Since k89h.8 (folded into this same session) flips the shim to the default parsing path, the old glibc-macro-bitmask detection path (Classification::from_mask, __ctype_b_loc chain walking) is now fully unreachable and was deleted outright, along with the now-dead Known::CtypeBLoc/CallSummary::CtypeBLoc plumbing — matches the acceptance criteria's 'or that special-casing is proven still necessary and documented why' by making it provably unnecessary instead. All ctype_classify_* differential tests updated to assert the shim-native shape (plain unsafe { isalpha(...) } calls, not glibc's '& 1024' bitmask literal) and pass in the default (no env override) gate.

title: Bootstrap core libc-shim headers and get the existing test suite green against them
description: Port declarations-only headers for whatever the current fixture + stdlib_coverage suites already rely on (stdint.h, stdio.h, stdlib.h, string.h, math.h, etc. — enumerate via grep across tests/fixtures and tests/stdlib for #include). Use plain extern function declarations and simple typedefs/macros rather than reproducing glibc's internal macro machinery, since Slate only needs the parseable surface, not glibc's implementation tricks. Full cargo nextest r --release must pass with SLATE_CLANG pointed at the shim instead of system headers.
acceptance_criteria: cargo nextest r --release passes in full with SLATE_CLANG parsing exclusively against libc-shim headers for every currently-supported fixture and stdlib probe. No fixture regresses or gets silently skipped.
notes:
All 19 headers written under libc-shim/include/ (18 by me + complex.h by the user): assert stdio stdlib string ctype math time locale threads pthread fenv wchar wctype uchar setjmp signal errno inttypes complex. Declarations-only, no glibc macro machinery - real linked glibc .so still provides all runtime behavior.

Verification: default (SLATE_LIBC_SHIM unset) cargo nextest r --release = 209/209 clean, zero regressions. Shim-enabled (SLATE_LIBC_SHIM=libc-shim/include) = 204/209; the 5 non-passes are all understood and non-blocking:
  - c11_library_callbacks_preserve_c_abi: asserts literal struct __once_flag shape, an artifact of glibc's own internal double-typedef chain (anonymous struct -> __once_flag -> once_flag). My once_flag is a clean single-level typedef producing struct once_flag instead - legitimately different, not a bug. Deferred to slate-k89h.8.
  - 3x ctype_classify_* differential tests: the ctype_classify/ctype_libc fixups pattern-match glibc's __ctype_b_loc() bitmask macro expansion shape, which a plain-function ctype.h (no macros) never produces. Expected per slate-k89h.4's own design - that fixup logic needs porting to the plain-call shape, or dropping if baseline is already correct without it (baseline is correct either way per CLAUDE.md: fixups are optional).
  - stdlib_coverage: fails only because tests/stdlib/setjmp/setjmp (KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED, slate-nk3.19) now unexpectedly PASSES under the shim (previously broken under real glibc's macro-driven setjmp/__sigsetjmp indirection). A genuine win; leave KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED untouched until slate-k89h.8 locks it in for real (removing it now would break the still-current default/system-header run, where it's still legitimately broken).
  - complex/functions.c: now parses successfully (previously blocked entirely on missing complex.h) but still correctly fails for the pre-existing, separately-tracked slate-nk3.25.2 gap (long double complex lowering/ABI) - unrelated to header content, still correctly silent in KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED.

Two real bugs found and fixed along the way:
  1. assert.h: assert((int[2]){3,4}[1] == 4) has a top-level comma inside {} that a single-parameter macro can't handle; fixed by making assert variadic (assert(...)/__VA_ARGS__) matching glibc's own documented reason for doing the same.
  2. string.h: strerror_r under _POSIX_C_SOURCE needs the actual XSI int-returning symbol, which on glibc is __xpg_strerror_r via a __REDIRECT_NTH - the plain 'strerror_r' symbol is the GNU char*-returning variant. Declared with __asm__("__xpg_strerror_r") to link the right symbol. This is unavoidable ABI truth (which symbol provides which semantics), not glibc-internals-for-convenience.

Also found and fixed a real pre-existing bug per explicit direction not to route around glibc internals: src/lower.rs's clib_record_type() recognized FILE/mbstate_t only by matching glibc's PRIVATE tag spelling (_IO_FILE, __mbstate_t) instead of the public standard typedef name, which is exactly the coupling slate-k89h exists to eliminate. Fixed by also matching the public names (FILE, mbstate_t), verified zero regression on the default path. Full removal of the internal-name fallback (and resolving the shape-coupled test assertions above) filed as slate-k89h.7, gated on slate-k89h.8 (make the shim the default path) so today's still-default system-header behavior isn't broken in the meantime.

title: Design + wire the libc-shim include path into SLATE_CLANG only
description: Decide the exact mechanism (-nostdinc + -isystem <repo>/libc-shim/include, keeping clang's own freestanding resource-dir headers available) and thread it through only the two SLATE_CLANG invocations in c_ast.rs (AST-dump JSON, CIR emission) — never SLATE_CC. Create the empty libc-shim/include/ tree and confirm a trivial C file with no libc usage still parses to CIR and AST JSON with -nostdinc active, so the plumbing is proven before any real header content is ported.

SLATE_CC's invocation and existing differential runtime behavior are untouched. The include path is documented in CLAUDE.md/docs alongside the other SLATE_* toolchain vars.

When set to a directory, target_args() in src/cir/emit.rs adds -nostdinc -isystem <dir> to all three SLATE_CLANG invocations (CIR emission, AST dump, predefined-macros oracle) via the shared target_args() hook - SLATE_CC (tests/support/mod.rs compile_c/compile_c_multi) is untouched, confirmed by code inspection: it hardcodes its own args and never calls target_args(). Created libc-shim/include/ (empty, .gitkeep placeholder) as the future shim root - default path CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/libc-shim/include is NOT wired in yet since the dir has no content; k89h.2 should flip target_args() to default-on against that path once real headers land, removing the opt-in gate. Proved the wiring two ways: tests/fixtures/comments.c (no #include) translates identically with/without the shim; tests/fixtures/add.c (#include <stdio.h>) fails with a clean 'stdio.h file not found' once the shim is active and empty, confirming -nostdinc actually took effect. Documented SLATE_LIBC_SHIM in CLAUDE.md's toolchain table.

title: (EPIC) Ship a Slate-owned libc header shim to decouple CIR parsing from the host's real libc
description:
Why: SLATE_CLANG currently parses C against whatever libc headers the host machine happens to have on its include path (in practice glibc). Two problems fall out of that: (1) portability — translation results and even parseability depend on the exact glibc version/layout of the dev or CI machine, not on the C standard; (2) header complexity leaks into Slate's own logic — e.g. ctype.h (ef00d5a, bb23375) required reverse-engineering glibc's internal __ctype_b_loc()/__exctype bitmask macros just to recognize isupper/tolower-family calls, and slate-t97h's trusted-header provenance is keyed off resolving physical system header paths rather than anything Slate controls.

Goal: give SLATE_CLANG its own self-contained, Slate-owned set of header declarations (a 'fake libc') and point CIR parsing (SLATE_CLANG's AST-dump + CIR-emission invocations only) at it via -nostdinc plus -isystem into a repo-owned include dir, instead of the system's real headers. Real system glibc headers on this machine remain the reference/benchmark to check declarations against, not something we parse.

Scope is compile-time declarations only: function signatures, types, and macros needed for parsing and for Slate's own idiom-detection (e.g. plain extern declarations for ctype.h functions instead of glibc's macro fast-path), not implementations. SLATE_CC (compiling/running the C side of a differential test) keeps linking the real system libc — runtime behavior under test is unaffected; only what SLATE_CLANG sees while producing CIR changes. This also gives slate-t97h a much simpler trusted-provenance root: 'resolves into Slate's own header tree' instead of 'resolves into some system path that looks like glibc.'

Target surface: everything the parser currently accepts, tracked against C23 + the GNU extensions Slate already claims to support (see docs/README.md, c.bnf, the slate-3f8g GNU-extensions epic tree, and the slate-nk3 header-by-header stdlib epic tree) — extend in lockstep with that existing investigation rather than duplicating it.
design: Headers-only shim, not a runtime libc replacement. Lives in-repo (e.g. libc-shim/include/). Threaded into SLATE_CLANG's own invocation only (c_ast.rs AST-dump call and the CIR-emission call), never into SLATE_CC. Keep clang's own freestanding headers (stddef.h, stdarg.h, stdbool.h, float.h, etc., from clang's resource-dir -isystem) since those come from the compiler itself, not a libc, and reimplementing them buys nothing.
acceptance_criteria: SLATE_CLANG's AST-dump and CIR-emission invocations compile the full existing fixture + stdlib_coverage test suite (cargo nextest r --release) using only Slate-owned headers (-nostdinc + -isystem into a repo include dir), with zero includes resolving into system libc paths — verified by asserting no #include resolves outside the repo header dir (or clang's own freestanding builtin headers for stddef.h/stdarg.h/etc). SLATE_CC/differential runtime behavior is unchanged. slate-t97h's trusted-header check is updated to recognize the shim's physical paths. ctype.h is re-implemented against the shim as the flagship case and its existing fixtures still pass. Remaining stdlib headers are extended in the shim incrementally, tracked via the existing slate-nk3 per-header issues rather than new duplicate ones.

title: Decompose removable-parameter analysis into orthogonal facts

Removed diagnostic metadata assertions and extended unused_params fixture to preserve an address-taken signature. Move Box/Vec eligibility and HeapOwnershipPlan construction into the heap-ownership rule and typed recipe layer.

QueryContext returns no HeapOwnershipPlanSet, ownership kind/read-safety/extent policy is composed by the rule, unsupported or incomplete lifetimes reject conservatively with evidence, and focused differential fixtures pass.

The Function QueryRule composes complete binding uses and navigable statements, decides ScalarBox versus VecBuffer, rejects unknown or potentially uninitialized vector extents, and constructs private recipe plans. Match immutable local definitions as QueryItems, follow exact def-use handles, query type/effects/place and phase constraints orthogonally, and let the inline-temp rule decide whether and how to replace the sole use.

Returned definition/use sites are stable handles, phase and safety rejection retains evidence, and early/late inline-temp behavior and focused differential fixtures pass.
notes: Migrated inline-temp selection to Binding query items composed from generic initializer, exact binding-use, enclosing-statement, type, and effects facts. title: Preserve weak alias binding in cross-TU GNU pragma output
description: The required full release suite persistently fails cross_tu::gnu_symbol_pragmas_preserve_cross_tu_linkage because the generated pragma_weak_alias symbol has STB_GLOBAL binding instead of the expected weak binding. Reproduces independently with cargo nextest r --release --test cross_tu -E 'test(gnu_symbol_pragmas_preserve_cross_tu_linkage)' --nocapture.
acceptance_criteria: The isolated cross-TU test and the full release nextest suite pass; generated GNU weak aliases retain the expected ELF binding.
close_reason: Root cause was not in Slate's weak-alias codegen itself (symbols.rs's 'core::arch::global_asm!(".weak pragma_weak_alias\n.set pragma_weak_alias, pragma_weak_target")' correctly mirrors clang's own per-TU output for #pragma weak) -- it was that this raw asm text is invisible to rustc's own #[no_mangle] symbol-uniqueness frontend check, so a same-named strong definition elsewhere in the same combined crate (strong.rs's real pragma_weak_alias fn) only collides at the assembler stage, and only if both land in the same object file. Verified #[linkage="weak"] as an alternative fails unconditionally (rustc's frontend rejects duplicate #[no_mangle] names regardless of linkage), so the raw-asm approach is the only one that can work, and its correctness is entirely contingent on codegen-unit partitioning keeping the two modules in separate objects -- which neither generated_crate_manifest (tests/support/mod.rs, used by every differential/cross_tu/chibicc harness) nor lib_crate_manifest (src/main.rs, the real translate-project --lib output) guaranteed, since neither set an explicit codegen-units and this rustc/cargo installation doesn't default to enough units for a crate this small. Bisected empirically: codegen-units=1/2 reproduce the STB_GLOBAL failure, =16 and =256 both avoid it. Fixed by adding codegen-units = 256 (Cargo's own traditional dev-profile default, well above the empirically-necessary 16 for headroom) to [profile.dev] in both manifest generators -- this is a real end-user-facing robustness gap, not just a test artifact, since translate-project --lib would hit the identical nondeterministic failure for any real C project combining a #pragma weak alias TU with a strong-override TU into one crate. Un-ignored gnu_symbol_pragmas_preserve_cross_tu_linkage. cargo fmt/clippy clean, cargo nextest r --release fully green at 212/212 (2 skipped are the pre-existing intentionally-ignored diagnostic tests).

title: Generalize query engine around matchable Rust items
description: Refactor the query engine so rules iterate matchable Rust AST items, bind stable semantic identities, query generic facts including def-use relationships, and produce anchored edit sets independently of candidate type. Capture the architecture and migrate final_return_temps as the first vertical slice.

A first vertical slice matches locals using semantic facts rather than generated names, exposes stable binding/def-use information, rewrites every matching final-return temporary, and the release nextest suite, clippy, and fmt pass.
