close_reason: Implemented CIR is_volatile handling for loads and stores with std::ptr::read_volatile/write_volatile, added volatile.c fixture, added generated-Rust assertion for volatile intrinsics, extended BNF fuzz coverage and docs. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo run --quiet -- emit-fixtures, cargo test -- --nocapture, and git diff --check.

title: Remove unsound struct derives
description: Struct lowering should not derive Clone, Copy, or Default without proving every field supports those traits.
close_reason: Removed unsound Clone/Copy/Default derives from generated structs and kept explicit field initialization. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo run --quiet -- emit-fixtures, and cargo test -- --nocapture.

title: Retire the CIR UEFI workaround for MSVC lowering
description: Slate's basic x86_64-pc-windows-msvc profile currently lowers CIR through x86_64-unknown-uefi with Itanium C++ ABI selection, Microsoft extensions disabled, and writable strings because the CIR MSVC path rejects createCXXABI, HandleTagDeclDefinition, and string literal mangling. Track direct use of the requested MSVC triple once upstream CIR supports records, external declarations, and string literals, and validate the replacement against the pinned xwin ABI probes.

title: Phase 4b.3: id-stability differential fixture + full gate
description: Once .6.6.1 and .6.6.2 land, write the differential fixture required by .6.6's own acceptance criteria: an edit that leaves one function untouched, proving its FunctionId (and derived facts) are unchanged after the edit - now trivially true by construction (interned on name/kind/path) rather than needing runtime assertion machinery, but the fixture should still exercise the pipeline end to end (e.g. two functions, edit one, confirm the other's translation output is identical/unaffected and the run still passes differential stdout/exit-code comparison). Run the full completion gate (cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo nextest r --release unfiltered) and close out .6.6 and its children.
acceptance_criteria: Differential fixture added under tests/fixtures/ exercising a multi-function edit scenario. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest r --release all green. slate-kby1.6.6 and its three children closed.
close_reason: Added multi-function ID-stability differential fixture; focused and full gates pass

title: Phase 4b.1: interned FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId + ProgramInput core types
description:
Add #[salsa::input(singleton)] ProgramInput { #[returns(ref)] program: Program } to src/fixups/salsa.rs. Convert FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId in src/fixups/facts/mod.rs from plain usize newtypes to #[salsa::interned] structs carrying a genuine 'db lifetime (textbook salsa, no unsafe(no_lifetime) adapter): FunctionId<'db> interned on the function's name; BindingId<'db> interned on (function: FunctionId<'db>, name: String, kind: BindingKind, path: AstPath); LoopId<'db> interned on (function: FunctionId<'db>, kind: LoopKind, path: AstPath). Interning gives natural, content-derived id stability for untouched functions/bindings/loops with zero hand-rolled counters or invalidation bookkeeping - a function/binding/loop keeps the same id across an edit iff its (name/kind/path) identity is unchanged, regardless of what else in the program changed.

Rewrite src/fixups/facts/walk.rs's BaseWalk/Collector (currently a stateful global-counter walker: next_binding/next_loop increment across the whole program in item order, purge_function/splice_function/remove_items do incremental bookkeeping) into 'db-lifetime-aware pure derivation logic - free functions taking db: &'db dyn FixupDb (or equivalent) that walk one function's AST and intern each binding/loop as they're encountered. No more manual id counters: interning subsumes them. No more purge/splice/remove-items machinery: a pure per-function walk naturally reproduces the same ids for unchanged content on every call.

This is a large, mostly-mechanical fan-out: every Fact struct in facts/mod.rs that embeds FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId (~30 types) needs a 'db lifetime added, which cascades to every signature across the ~26 facts/*.rs family files, src/fixups/salsa.rs, src/fixups/query/context.rs, and src/fixups/query/rules/*.rs. Acceptance for THIS ticket is narrower than the full migration: get the crate compiling again with the new id shape and existing behavior preserved (full differential suite green) - it does not yet require FunctionInput's fields to actually be reimplemented as tracked fns backed by ProgramInput (that's .6.6.2), nor does it require collapsing SalsaFacts's Dirty/TouchedItems apparatus (that's .6.8, already filed and depends on this whole chain).
acceptance_criteria: ProgramInput exists as a salsa::input(singleton). FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId are #[salsa::interned] structs with a 'db lifetime, keyed on stable content (name/kind/path), not global counters. facts/walk.rs's Collector no longer does manual next_binding/next_loop counting or purge/splice/remove-items bookkeeping - interning replaces it. Crate compiles; cargo fmt/clippy clean; full existing differential + stdlib_coverage suite passes unchanged (proves the id-shape change alone didn't regress behavior, even though it doesn't yet change how facts are actually derived/cached).
notes: Completed. Lifetime-aware facts/query handles and matcher captures compile cleanly; ProgramInput is a salsa singleton updated by resolve(); FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId are content-interned; BaseWalk is reconstructed purely and no longer has next counters or splice/remove/purge mutation paths. Validation: cargo check, cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, git diff --check, and cargo nextest r --release (226 passed, 4 skipped).
close_reason: Added singleton ProgramInput, completed interned ID lifetime migration, replaced BaseWalk splice/remove/purge bookkeeping with pure content-interned reconstruction, and passed fmt, Clippy, and the full 226-test release suite.

title: Phase 4b.2: retire FunctionInput's per-field salsa::input; tracked fns keyed on FunctionId<'db>
description:
Once .6.6.1 lands interned FunctionId<'db>/BindingId<'db>/LoopId<'db>, replace FunctionInput's externally-set body/bindings/binding_types/loops fields (currently a #[salsa::input] struct populated by SalsaFacts::sync_function calling set_body()/set_bindings()/etc. on every touched function) with genuine #[salsa::tracked] fns keyed directly on (ProgramInput, FunctionId<'db>) - e.g. FunctionId::body(db) -> &'db FnDef, deriving straight from ProgramInput.program(db).items by matching the interned name, with no external .set_*() writes at all.

SalsaFacts must stop storing functions: HashMap<FunctionId, FunctionInput> and the all_functions/definitions fields as owned state, since a 'db-bound map can't live inside a struct that also owns the Database it borrows from (self-referential). Replace with SalsaFacts holding just Database + ProgramInput (both lifetime-free/Copy), with every accessor method doing a fresh call through &self.db at read time - mirroring QueryContext<'snapshot>'s existing borrow-per-call shape rather than SalsaFacts's current cache-per-field shape. Keep the Dirty/TouchedItems/resolve() shell functioning for now (even if its sync methods become thin/no-ops in places) - fully deleting that invalidation-hinting apparatus is explicitly .6.8's job, not this one; don't scope-creep into it here.
acceptance_criteria: FunctionInput's body/bindings/binding_types/loops are real #[salsa::tracked] fns of (ProgramInput, FunctionId<'db>), not externally-set input fields. SalsaFacts no longer stores a HashMap<FunctionId, FunctionInput> or owned AllFunctions/DefinitionsInput state - reads go through &self.db fresh each call. Existing SalsaFacts public API surface (the ~40 accessor methods) keeps working, updated to the new call shape. cargo fmt/clippy clean; full differential + stdlib_coverage suite green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 4b: docs + sanity-check the per-edit full-rederive tradeoff
description: Once slate-kby1.6.6 through .6.9 land: update docs/facts.md, docs/fixups.md, docs/passes.md, docs/salsa-migration.md again for the ProgramInput-centric design (no more manual touched-set tracking anywhere - salsa is the only incremental layer, full stop). Also do a lightweight sanity check on the design's real tradeoff (documented in .6.6's ticket): every edit now reruns a cheap per-function derivation for every function, not just touched ones, relying on salsa backdating to stop the cascade. Confirm this isn't a measured regression on a realistic-sized fixture (the deleted temp_bench module in salsa.rs is a reasonable template to adapt, though per prior guidance a benchmark harness should be temporary/deletable once its number is recorded here, not kept as permanent test-suite weight).
acceptance_criteria: docs/facts.md, docs/fixups.md, docs/passes.md, docs/salsa-migration.md contain no stale references to the deleted Dirty/TouchedItems-driven invalidation, BaseWalk's external sync, or SalsaFacts::sync_all/sync_touched; a recorded before/after timing comparison exists in the closing bd reason (not necessarily a committed benchmark file); cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green.

title: Phase 4b: migrate QueryContext's remaining non-salsa query methods to #[salsa::tracked] fns
description:
The 29 methods slate-kby1.6.4 inlined out of the deleted query_cache! macro (byte_source, pure, anonymous_structs, first_nul, counted_loop, ptr_len_slices, ...) still build their QueryResult<Proof/Rejection> + evidence directly on QueryContext, reading self.program (a bare &Program reference) and self.salsa() - none of that Proof-construction work is salsa-memoized, only the raw fact reads underneath it are. This was flagged and deliberately left as-is when query_cache! was deleted, since Program wasn't a salsa input yet and several return types borrow 'snapshot from &Program directly (ByteSource<'snapshot>, &'snapshot FnDef, &'snapshot [IndentStmt], ByteView<'snapshot>) - salsa tracked fns can't return values borrowed from a non-salsa-input that way.

Once slate-kby1.6.6 lands ProgramInput, that obstacle is gone: rewrite these methods (and any other QueryContext method still reading self.program directly instead of through salsa) as #[salsa::tracked] fns - either on a new type or as free tracked fns taking (db, ProgramInput, ...) - keyed the same way the deleted query_cache! macro's key: lines did (roughly half take a real per-item key like ExprSite/FunctionId/BindingId/StatementRef, the rest take a whole-program () key). Confirmed via src/fixups/query/rules/memchr.rs that repeat-key calls within one pass are real (both its case arms call byte_source(&same_site)), so this genuinely restores (and generalizes, across passes too) the caching value query_cache! provided - not just parity.

The 'snapshot-lifetime return types need their signatures reworked to return owned/salsa-lifetime data instead of borrowing from a bare &Program, now that Program is reachable through the db.
acceptance_criteria: No QueryContext method reads self.program directly for fact computation (only for genuinely program-structural, non-cached lookups if any remain, documented if so); every one of the ~29 methods is backed by a #[salsa::tracked] fn; the memchr.rs two-case repeat byte_source(&source) call is confirmed (via a differential fixture or targeted check) to hit salsa's memoization on the second call, not recompute; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (222/222).
notes: Migrated all 29 cached QueryContext proof methods to tracked ProgramInput queries composed directly from Salsa inputs/facts; QueryContext now delegates through SalsaFacts owner entry points. Temporary byte_source execution probe on mem_memchr showed one body execution per distinct ExprSite across both rule cases. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; cargo nextest r --release (226 passed, 4 skipped).
close_reason: All cached proof queries migrated to Salsa and completion gates pass

title: Phase 4b: delete TouchedItems-driven invalidation, collapse fixups/mod.rs to set_program()+read
description:
Once FunctionInput and DefinitionsInput are both fully derived from ProgramInput (slate-kby1.6.6, slate-kby1.6.7), SalsaFacts no longer needs external touched-set hints to know what to resync - every read lazily re-derives from the current ProgramInput and salsa's own value-backdating stops the invalidation cascade at whatever didn't actually change. Delete: Dirty enum, SalsaFacts::mark_touched/mark_everything_dirty/resolve's dirty-checking, and the sync_all/sync_touched/sync_function split (collapse to one sync path, or delete sync methods entirely if reads can go straight through the tracked fns). Replace fixups/mod.rs's ~75 call sites' incremental.mark_touched(&report.touched)/incremental.mark_everything_dirty()/incremental.resolve(&program) dance with a single program_input.set_program(&mut db).to(program.clone()) per edit.

Keep TouchedItems and ItemApplyReport.touched themselves (the computation, not the consumption) - they're still useful as a diagnostic/test-assertion value (see the existing report.touched.in_place/unbounded assertions in query/item.rs's tests) even once nothing reads them to drive salsa invalidation.
acceptance_criteria: grep for Dirty/mark_touched/mark_everything_dirty/IncrementalFacts-shaped resolve() logic in src/fixups/ returns nothing; fixups/mod.rs's pass-invocation call sites are just set_program(...) + direct reads; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (222/222).
close_reason: Removed TouchedItems-driven invalidation shell, switched pass boundaries to direct ProgramInput updates, retained touched reports for diagnostics, and passed all gates

title: Phase 4b: derive DefinitionsInput from ProgramInput
description: Once slate-kby1.6.6 lands ProgramInput, replace DefinitionsInput's externally-set records/structs/enums/extern_call_signatures/statics fields (currently pushed by SalsaFacts::sync_definitions, a full program.items rescan on every call) with #[salsa::tracked] fns keyed on ProgramInput that derive them the same way sync_definitions does today. This is a smaller, more mechanical version of .6.6's FunctionInput work - no id-stability concern here since these aren't FunctionId-keyed, just whole-program collections.
acceptance_criteria: DefinitionsInput's fields are #[salsa::tracked] fns of ProgramInput, not externally-set; SalsaFacts::sync_definitions is deleted; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green.
close_reason: DefinitionsInput and sync_definitions were removed by the ProgramInput migration; verified tracked definition queries, updated current architecture docs, and passed all gates

title: Phase 4b: make Program a salsa input, derive FunctionInput from it
description:
Add a #[salsa::input] ProgramInput { #[returns(ref)] program: Program } (or a #[salsa::input(singleton)], matching AllFunctions's existing pattern) to src/fixups/salsa.rs. Replace FunctionInput's externally-set body/bindings/binding_types/loops fields with #[salsa::tracked] fns keyed on (ProgramInput, FunctionId) that re-derive from the current program on every read - the base program walk (currently facts::walk::BaseWalk, driven externally by SalsaFacts::sync_all/sync_touched/sync_function) becomes one or more tracked fns instead of externally-synced state.

FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId assignment stability across edits is the load-bearing correctness property here (an untouched function must keep the same FunctionId, or every downstream FunctionInput-keyed tracked fn backdating breaks) - preserve BaseWalk's existing id-assignment algorithm (traversal-order assignment, stable for untouched functions) inside the new tracked fn, don't redesign it. Write a differential fixture proving id stability across an edit before closing.

sync_all_functions and sync_definitions already do a full program.items rebuild on every sync call today (no per-item incrementality currently exploited there) - and mark_everything_dirty() is already called 48 times vs mark_touched()'s 32 in fixups/mod.rs, meaning most passes already force a full resync in practice. So 'salsa reruns the cheap derivation fn for every function on every edit, backdating stops the cascade for functions whose derived value didn't change' is not a meaningful regression from today's actual behavior, just a different (simpler, salsa-native) mechanism for getting the same backdating property.
acceptance_criteria: FunctionInput's body/bindings/binding_types/loops are #[salsa::tracked] fns of (ProgramInput, FunctionId), not externally-set input fields; a differential fixture exercises an edit that leaves one function untouched and confirms its FunctionId and derived facts are unchanged after the edit; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green.
notes: Rescoped into 3 children after design investigation found the true blast radius: interned salsa structs carry a 'db lifetime by construction (struct Foo<'db>(salsa::Id, PhantomData<&'db ()>)), so FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId becoming interned forces 'db onto every Fact struct that embeds one (~30 types) and onto SalsaFacts itself, which can't keep owning Database while also storing 'db-bound derived maps (self-referential). Real fix: SalsaFacts stops storing per-function state entirely; everything becomes a fresh call through a borrowed db, matching QueryContext's existing lifetime shape. See children .6.6.1-.6.6.3 for the ordered breakdown.
close_reason: ProgramInput migration and tracked per-function derivation completed across all three children

title: Complete AArch64 macOS Rust and Mach-O verification
description:
Turn the AArch64 macOS implementation into a stable completion gate for the parent epic. Consolidate the supported-header manifest, SDK-oracle probes, differential or structural fixtures, generated Rust checks, and Mach-O import/export inspection.

Audit generated uses of libc::FILE, libc::mbstate_t, libc::timespec, pthread types, and other host-Linux assumptions. Replace or target-gate them so macOS output uses verified generated types or core::ffi primitives. Verify that C definitions with external linkage retain public C ABI and stable Mach-O names and that imported declarations preserve weak or explicit link identities.

Document the SDK and deployment baseline, AArch64-only scope, supported headers, feature macros, deliberately unsupported frameworks and Apple platforms, SDK probe procedure, and user responsibility for final linking.
design: Use a layered gate: libc-shim compilation proves declaration consistency; external SDK probes prove ABI agreement; C fixtures prove Slate preservation; cargo check proves valid aarch64-apple-darwin Rust; llvm-readobj or llvm-nm proves Mach-O symbol identity. Keep SDK-dependent oracle tests skippable with an explicit reason when no SDK is configured, while checked-in derived fixtures continue to test Slate on all hosts.
acceptance_criteria: The documented AArch64 macOS manifest has automated libc-shim compilation, SDK signature/layout comparison when configured, fixture translation, cargo check for aarch64-apple-darwin without linking, and Mach-O symbol inspection; generated code contains no incompatible Linux libc type assumptions; imports, weak symbols, link names, and exported C definitions match the selected ABI; all parent-epic criteria are met; cargo fmt, cargo clippy, focused tests, and cargo nextest r --release pass; documentation precisely states the SDK baseline, deployment target, supported headers, exclusions, and linking boundary.

title: Preserve Darwin feature macros and source-to-symbol redirects
description:
Make macOS source declarations lower to the actual Darwin symbols and availability surface selected by the deployment baseline. A plausible POSIX prototype is insufficient when Apple headers attach an assembler name, compatibility suffix, weak import, alias, or inline redirect.

Model _DARWIN_C_SOURCE and supported POSIX feature-test behavior, deployment availability guards, public inline wrappers, errno and standard-stream access, and source-to-symbol mappings such as UNIX2003, INODE64, NOCANCEL, DARWIN_EXTSN, or their current SDK equivalents whenever they appear in the supported manifest. Preserve weak imports, explicit assembler labels, aliases, and link names through the macro dump, Clang AST, CIR, and Rust lowering paths.

Do not expose APIs newer than the selected deployment baseline merely because the installed SDK contains them.
design: Treat feature selection, deployment availability, and concrete Mach-O symbol identity as Darwin libc ABI data. Retain both source spelling and foreign identity where fixups need the source API while code generation needs the actual imported symbol.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures covering representative feature-test branches, deployment guards, errno and streams, inline redirects, compatibility symbol suffixes, aliases, and weak imports agree with SDK preprocessing and object probes; generated Rust uses correct link names and does not invent unavailable declarations or data symbols; APIs newer than the baseline are absent unless explicitly selected; earlier macOS and existing libc tests remain green.

title: Add the public macOS POSIX libc header and layout surface
description:
Expand the basic AArch64 macOS profile across the public POSIX libc headers used by ordinary C programs. Work header-family by header-family from failing fixtures and macOS SDK comparison probes.

Model FILE and fpos_t, mbstate_t and locale types, stat and statfs, dirent, signal and context types, pthread objects, timespec and timeval, fd_set, socket and sockaddr families including Darwin length fields, poll, termios, spawn, regex, semaphore, dynamic loading, user and group records, and related public aggregates. Include common Darwin libc extensions only when their declaration and ABI are covered by fixtures.

Keep objects opaque when source code can only pass pointers; provide exact size, alignment, fields, and calling shape whenever source can allocate, embed, initialize, pass by value, or access them. Do not import Mach, framework, Objective-C, or private SDK surfaces.
design: Maintain a macOS-only supported-header manifest and Darwin bits overlay. A future common BSD source layer may reduce duplication, but macOS layouts and signatures remain independently verified. Every header family begins with end-to-end C fixtures rather than unit-only declaration tests.
acceptance_criteria: Every header in the agreed AArch64 macOS libc/POSIX manifest compiles through libc-shim; fixtures exercise all exposed aggregate and divergent signature categories; canonical types, sizes, alignments, and offsets agree with the selected SDK oracle; unsupported headers are explicitly excluded or tracked; no Linux or other BSD ABI is inferred; generated Rust checks for aarch64-apple-darwin; existing libc tests and the full release suite remain green.

title: Establish basic AArch64 macOS libc-shim support
description:
Create the smallest correctness-checked Darwin libc profile that lets Slate parse and lower representative ISO C programs for aarch64-apple-darwin at the selected macOS deployment baseline.

Map the Rust target to Apple vendor, macOS platform, Darwin kernel, Darwin libc, Mach-O object format, AArch64, LP64, and little endian without falling back to generic libc. Add a macOS-specific supported-header manifest. Implement fundamental and compiler-provided types and the basic freestanding and hosted ISO C headers, including stddef, stdint, stdarg, limits, float, assert, errno, ctype, string, stdlib, minimal stdio, math, and time declarations.

Add C fixtures before implementation that expose target-selection and ABI failures. Ensure Linux-only declarations and layouts are not selected for macOS.
design: Use shared ISO declarations plus Darwin-specific type and bits overlays selected by both libc and architecture. Keep the milestone deliberately narrow: unsupported POSIX headers are absent from the manifest until their public layouts and signatures have been checked against the SDK oracle.
acceptance_criteria: With SLATE_TARGET=aarch64-apple-darwin and the documented deployment baseline, the focused macOS header test compiles the basic manifest through libc-shim; representative fixtures translate; fundamental integer, pointer, wchar_t, time, floating-point, and variadic types agree with SDK probes; ordinary imported functions emit correct extern C signatures; Linux-only declarations are absent; generated Rust checks for aarch64-apple-darwin without linking; existing libc tests and the full release suite remain green.

title: Establish the AArch64 macOS SDK oracle and deployment baseline
description:
Add repository tooling that uses an externally installed macOS SDK as the ABI oracle for aarch64-apple-darwin. On macOS, discover it through xcrun --sdk macosx --show-sdk-path; on other hosts, require an explicit SLATE_MACOS_SDK path. Do not download, copy, or commit Apple SDK contents.

Choose and document the initial deployment baseline, starting with macOS 11. Feed the baseline consistently to Clang through the target or minimum-version option. Add probe modes for predefined and header macros, preprocessed declarations, JSON AST output, record layouts, assembler labels, availability attributes, and Mach-O symbol identities. Store transient probe output under target/ and keep any checked-in expectations small, derived, and reviewable.

The tooling must make the SDK version and build identifier visible so reference changes are intentional rather than silently following whichever Xcode happens to be installed.
design: Provide a tools/ probe script with a stable header/fixture input and machine-readable output. Separate SDK discovery from probing, accept only an existing SDK root, and pin the Slate support contract to a declared deployment baseline rather than the latest SDK API surface.
acceptance_criteria: A documented command locates or accepts a macOS SDK, verifies that it contains the required public libc headers, records the SDK identity, and successfully probes representative ISO C and POSIX declarations for aarch64-apple-darwin at the chosen deployment baseline; macro, AST, layout, and symbol probe modes are available; all transient SDK-derived artifacts stay under target/; absence or mismatch of the SDK produces an actionable skip or error; no Apple SDK files are committed.

title: Support the AArch64 macOS libc and LibSystem ABI in libc-shim
description:
Objective

Allow Slate to translate C for the aarch64-apple-darwin Rust target using declaration-only headers compatible with the public macOS libc and LibSystem ABI. SDK selection and final linking remain the responsibility of the user.

Scope

Support AArch64 macOS only. Cover ISO C, the public POSIX libc surface used by ordinary C programs, target-visible aggregate layouts, feature macros, macro-selected symbols, imports, and exported C definitions. Use a documented macOS deployment baseline beginning at macOS 11, the first Apple Silicon release.

Required work

Map aarch64-apple-darwin to an explicit macOS platform and Darwin libc profile rather than generic libc. Add a deployment-target input because the Rust triple does not encode API availability. Model AArch64 macOS fundamental types and Darwin-specific FILE, fpos_t, mbstate_t, stat, dirent, signal, pthread, locale, time, socket, and related public layouts. Preserve Darwin source-to-symbol redirects, assembler labels, aliases, weak imports, availability behavior, and exported names when they affect generated Rust. Remove or target-gate Linux libc crate type assumptions.

Use the installed macOS SDK as the primary oracle and Apple open-source libc sources as supporting references. Keep SDK contents external and check in only clean declaration-only libc-shim definitions and derived test expectations.

Out of scope

Intel macOS, iOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, simulators, Catalyst, Objective-C, C++, Apple frameworks, private SDK declarations, automatic SDK acquisition, final linking, and execution.
design: Build a single macOS/AArch64 libc profile selected by architecture, Apple vendor, macOS platform, Darwin kernel, Darwin libc, Mach-O object format, and an explicit deployment baseline. Share ISO declarations only when ABI identity is verified. Maintain a macOS-specific supported-header manifest rather than compiling Linux-only headers or claiming every SDK header.
acceptance_criteria: For aarch64-apple-darwin at the documented deployment baseline, Slate parses and lowers representative programs using every header in the supported macOS libc manifest; fundamental and exposed aggregate types match the selected macOS SDK; macro and alias backed declarations reference the correct Darwin symbols; imports and exported definitions retain their C ABI and Mach-O names; generated Rust checks for aarch64-apple-darwin without linking; Mach-O symbol inspection passes where required; existing libc targets remain green; the exact SDK baseline, supported headers, and exclusions are documented.

title: Phase 4: delete FixupFacts, facts::analyze, and every family's dead legacy collect_facts fn
description: Once every other kby1.6.3.* sub-ticket has landed, nothing should reference FixupFacts, facts::analyze, IncrementalFacts, or Dirty anywhere in src/fixups/. Delete: the FixupFacts struct and its impl block in facts/mod.rs; facts::analyze and the whole-program Collector it used (superseded by BaseWalk); every family's now-dead legacy collect_facts(program, &mut facts) fn across the ~29 files in facts/ (keep collect_for_function/compute/collect/candidates_for_function - those still back the tracked salsa fns); splice_function/remove_items/purge_function_facts if any trace of them remains outside the base-walk ticket's replacement. Make QueryContext.salsa a mandatory field (drop Option), delete every remaining None branch and the with_salsa() builder step (or leave the final constructor-collapse ergonomics to kby1.6.4 per its own ticket, whichever reads cleaner once you're here).
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'FixupFacts\|facts::analyze\|IncrementalFacts' src/fixups/ returns nothing; every family file in facts/ has no collect_facts fn taking &mut FixupFacts; QueryContext has no None branch anywhere; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason:
Deleted FixupFacts, facts::analyze, the whole-program Collector, and every family's legacy collect_facts(program, &mut FixupFacts) fn (~26 files) - kept collect_for_function/compute/collect/candidates_for_function, which back the salsa tracked fns. Made QueryContext.salsa mandatory (dropped Option, merged .with_salsa() into .new()).

Since .6.3.2 deliberately kept SalsaFacts owning a facts: FixupFacts field internally (a documented simpler-than-suggested choice at the time), deleting FixupFacts for real required finally building the BaseWalk extraction that ticket deferred: added facts::walk::BaseWalk (functions/bindings/binding_types/loops only) by relocating Collector/splice_function/remove_items/purge_function_facts's exact algorithm onto BaseWalk's own fields, including the resume-vs-fresh id-counter comments verbatim. SalsaFacts::resolve's Dirty::Touched arm still captures pre-removal function->item_index lookups before calling remove_items, for the same correctness reason the original splice_incremental_facts did - incremental id-stability is unchanged.

Tracing what still read the now-gone facts fields cascaded past the ticket's named surface: SalsaFacts::resolve's FixupFacts return value turned out to be consumed by nothing (once .6.3.4 had already moved ItemPlan::apply off &FixupFacts), so resolve() now returns (); QueryContext::new dropped its facts parameter entirely and absorbed .with_salsa() into one constructor call (every call site already chained them back-to-back); that forced updating all ~75 .apply(...)/QueryContext::new(...) call sites in fixups/mod.rs - well past the ticket's 3 named files, but purely mechanical (swap which already-in-scope variable gets passed). Also deleted 5 further functions that became dead 2-3 hops removed from any direct FixupFacts reference (calls::collect_signatures/collect_cfg_signature, duplicate statics_from_program in atomic_locals.rs/lazy_singleton.rs, pointer_option_safety::union_record_names, ptr_len/string_params's collect_candidates) - found via rustc's dead_code lint after each deletion round, not by grepping for FixupFacts.

Deleted salsa.rs's temp_bench module (the legacy-vs-salsa timing harness) despite its "do not delete until the epic tree is closed" comment - its entire premise (comparing against facts::analyze) became impossible to compile once facts::analyze was gone, so keeping it contradicted this very ticket's mandate. Documented the override plainly rather than working around the comment's letter.

Verified: grep -rn 'FixupFacts|facts::analyze|IncrementalFacts' src/fixups/ returns nothing. Every facts/*.rs family file has no collect_facts fn taking &mut FixupFacts. title: Phase 4: collapse QueryContext construction and update the ~20 fixups/mod.rs call sites
description: Depends on the legacy-engine-deletion ticket landing first. Once QueryContext never needs &FixupFacts, its constructor collapses from QueryContext::new(program, facts).with_salsa(salsa) to a single QueryContext::new(program, salsa: &SalsaFacts) (or similar) -- update all ~20 call sites in fixups/mod.rs (one per fixup pass invocation) to match. Also investigate and resolve the query_cache! macro (context.rs): it's QueryContext's own per-query-per-key cache for QueryResult (Proof/Rejection) values, layered on TOP of the raw fact data -- independent of whether that data came from legacy or salsa. Determine whether it's now redundant (salsa's own tracked-fn memoization already covers the expensive part) or still earns its keep (deduplicating repeated QueryResult/evidence construction within one fixup pass), and either delete it or keep it deliberately with that reasoning documented in the close reason.
acceptance_criteria: QueryContext has a single salsa-only constructor; all ~20 fixups/mod.rs call sites updated; query_cache! macro's fate (deleted or kept) is a deliberate, justified decision, not a leftover; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason:
Constructor collapse was already done as a side effect of slate-kby1.6.3.5 (QueryContext::new(program, salsa: &SalsaFacts) is the only constructor, no .with_salsa() step, all ~75 call sites already updated). This ticket's remaining work was resolving query_cache!'s fate.

Investigated first rather than guessing: docs/salsa-migration.md's own "Target architecture" section had already answered the question when the migration was originally planned - "The query_cache! macro is deleted once every cached query is salsa-backed - salsa's memoization subsumes it, and today's cache is strictly worse (doesn't survive past one snapshot anyway)." Verified the premise still holds: all 29 cached methods read exclusively through self.salsa()/self.program, and QueryContext is rebuilt fresh at every one of the ~75 pass-invocation call sites, so the RefCell<HashMap> cache never survived across passes even before this change - it only ever deduplicated repeat calls with the same key within one pass, which is exactly what was deemed not worth keeping.

Implementation: mechanically inlined all 29 query_cache!-generated methods (fn name(&self, ...) -> QueryResult<T>; key: ...; { body }) into a plain impl QueryContext<'snapshot> block, dropping the key:/cached() wrapper and keeping each body verbatim - a scripted transformation (query_cache! block has 6 whole-program () keys and 23 per-item keys like FunctionId/ExprSite/BindingId, all regular enough to convert programmatically), then verified against a hand read of the boundaries (the query_cache! macro itself, the QueryCache struct, and the cached() helper) before deleting them. Removed the now-unused std::cell::RefCell and HashMap imports.

Updated docs/fixups.md (the Scheduling section's code sample and the "recompute facts" line), docs/facts.md (intro, addressing scheme, collector ordering, the "Adding a fact" workflow - rewritten from the FixupFacts-field/collect_facts/facts::analyze recipe to the salsa-tracked-fn recipe), docs/passes.md (the facts/ and rewrite/ directory bullets, the apply-as-scheduler paragraph), and docs/README.md's one-line facts.md description, per the epic's own closing criterion. Also fixed adjacent dangling doc links I found while in these files (src/fixups/rewrite/ -> src/fixups/query/rules/, writing-a-fixup.md -> fixups.md, to_fixpoint_items -> to_fixpoint_program_with_facts) since they sat right next to what I was already correcting - did not attempt to fix docs/passes.md's dangling adding-features.md reference, which is unrelated pre-existing doc debt outside this ticket's scope.

Verified: grep for FixupFacts/IncrementalFacts/query_cache/facts::analyze in the 3 named docs returns nothing except one deliberate "unlike the old facts::analyze sweep" contrast sentence. cargo fmt/clippy clean, 222/222 nextest green, zero new comments (git diff on context.rs has none).

title: Phase 4: eliminate FixupFacts param from Bucket-2 and DefinitionsInput-shaped collectors
description: Mirrors kby1.6's Bucket-1 ticket but for the whole-program reduction families: calls/callsites, interprocedural_alloc_eligibility, string_params, ptr_len, lazy_singleton (genuinely whole-program, using AllFunctions) and struct_field_ownership/anonymous_structs/union_records (DefinitionsInput-shaped). These currently build throwaway whole-program FixupFacts snapshots (the ptr_len_snapshot/lazy_singleton pattern: aggregating bindings/binding_types/def_use/callsites/string_buffers from tracked per-function reads into one FixupFacts just to satisfy a legacy compute()/collect() signature) inside their AllFunctions/DefinitionsInput tracked fns. Change compute/collect to take the specific typed slices/maps they need directly (e.g. bodies: &Bodies, statics: &[StaticDeclFact], callsites: &[CallsiteFact]) instead of &FixupFacts.
acceptance_criteria: No compute/collect fn in these families takes facts: &FixupFacts; legacy collect_facts() call sites updated; every AllFunctions/DefinitionsInput tracked fn updated to pass typed fields/Bodies maps directly instead of building a FixupFacts snapshot; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason:
Eliminated &FixupFacts from every genuinely whole-program family's
compute/collect fn. Investigated all 8 families named in the ticket first:

- struct_field_ownership, anonymous_structs, union_records: already clean
  (Phase 2 precedent - collect(records: impl Iterator<Item = &RecordDef>),
  no FixupFacts anywhere in their tracked path). No work needed.
- lazy_singleton: already clean (compute(shapes, bodies, statics) - ported
  correctly in slate-kby1.5.9). No work needed.
- interprocedural_alloc_eligibility: collect(functions: &[FunctionSummary])
  already clean since .5.5; only its caller in find_call_allocation still
  built a throwaway FixupFacts{bindings} wrapper (a leftover from before
  heap_ownership's .6.1 signature change) - simplified to pass
  caller.bindings directly, no wrapper.
- calls/callsites: collect_callsites_for_function took &FixupFacts but only
  ever read .bindings - narrowed to bindings: &[BindingFact]. Updated both
  the legacy collect_facts loop and AllFunctions::callsites (which was
  needlessly cloning input.bindings(db) into a local_facts wrapper each
  iteration - now passes the tracked &Vec<BindingFact> straight through).
- ptr_len, string_params: the two real fixpoint families. Their compute()
  and ~20 mutually-recursive helpers each read 4-6 FixupFacts fields
  (bindings/binding_types/def_use/callsites, plus string_buffers/
  string_libc_uses for string_params). Rather than rewrite every helper's
  argument list to 5-6 separate slice params (high-risk diff across ~20
  functions per file, no behavioral or memoization benefit over a bundle),
  defined a small file-local Snapshot<'a> struct per family holding exactly
  the slices actually read, with inherent methods mirroring the subset of
  the FixupFacts API these files called (def_use, binding_named,
  binding_read_under, binding_type, string_buffer, local_binding_at - each

Wire all of them through the same 'prefer self.salsa when present, fall back to self.facts otherwise' pattern resolved_value_at already uses, and expand .with_salsa(&salsa_facts) wiring from the 2 DeadLocals sites to every step in fixups/mod.rs's pass sequence that constructs a QueryContext and can reach these methods (mirroring incremental.resolve()'s call sites 1:1), so the legacy def_use/effects Vec fields stop being read by any pass, not just DeadLocals. This is what 'replacing IncrementalFacts/Dirty's role for the two Phase 0 families end to end' (the kby1.3 epic description) actually requires -- Phase 0 proved the mechanism on one call site/one pass, this finishes the family.
acceptance_criteria: every QueryContext method that reads facts.def_use(..)/facts.effect(..) consults self.salsa first when Some, falling back to self.facts only when None; salsa_facts.sync(...) plus .with_salsa(&salsa_facts) is wired into every fixups/mod.rs step that constructs a QueryContext (same call-site count as incremental.resolve()); full nextest r --release green with identical output to before (pure internal-mechanism swap, no behavior change); fixup-debug trace output unchanged for a representative fixture; cargo fmt/clippy clean.
close_reason: All def_use/effect QueryContext call sites (binding_def_use, binding_value, statement_effects, observed_statement_effects, expression_effects, pure, and resolved_value_at) now route through two shared helpers (def_use_fact/effect_fact) that consult self.salsa first when present, falling back to self.facts otherwise -- zero duplicated branching logic this time (unlike kby1.1's inline duplication). Centralized SalsaFacts syncing INTO IncrementalFacts itself (now owns a salsa: SalsaFacts field) rather than wiring sync calls at each of the ~65 call sites by hand: IncrementalFacts::resolve() now updates salsa in lockstep with facts on every Dirty::Everything (sync_all) or Dirty::Touched (sync_touched when touched.removed is empty, else sync_all as a safe fallback given the item_index renumbering risk when removals and in-place edits mix in one batch) transition. This eliminates the whole class of body/bindings-mismatch bug found in kby1.3.1 by construction -- there is no longer a call site that can pass mismatched facts/program pairs. All ~76 QueryContext::new call sites reachable via incremental.resolve() now call .with_salsa(incremental.salsa()); the 12 call sites living inside to_fixpoint_program_with_facts closures were deliberately left unwired (that helper maintains its own per-round FixupFacts entirely independent of IncrementalFacts, so incremental.salsa() would be stale there -- wiring those correctly needs to change to_fixpoint_program_with_facts's own signature to carry synced salsa per round, out of scope for this ticket); late_loop_cleanup (a free function with no access to incremental, already doing a full facts::analyze every iteration) also deliberately left unwired. title: Prototype salsa on def_use + effects facts

title: Salsa migration
description: Migrate the fixup query/facts layer from hand-rolled per-pass recomputation (facts::analyze() + QueryContext BTreeMap indexing + query_cache! macro, rebuilt from scratch at all ~82 call sites) to salsa-based incremental queries. Goal: fix slow rewrite passes caused by full-program fact reanalysis on every pass, and get automatic interprocedural invalidation instead of hand-reasoned dirty-marking. EditSets/plan/apply (the rewriting layer) stay as-is; only facts + query context move to salsa. Granularity: per-item (FunctionId-keyed) salsa inputs, driven by the existing TouchedItems (src/fixups/query/plan.rs) after plan.apply instead of full facts::analyze(). Interprocedural facts (heap_ownership, callee_alloc_summary, etc.) use a map/reduce pattern: per-item local facts unioned in a tracked fn, so a single-function edit only recomputes that item's local contribution.

title: Implement query-driven fixup substituting classified calls with libc:: paths
description:
Consume the substitution table from slate-4wl9.1. For each confirmed
substitutable symbol, extend src/function_identity.rs's Known/classify_function
(or an adjacent classification keyed the same way) so calls to it are
identifiable at fixup time via the existing Provenance::TrustedHeader path -
do not build a new provenance mechanism, the CallBinding::Direct { identity,
.. } facts already carry what's needed.

Add a query-driven fixup under src/fixups/query/ (per
docs/writing-a-query-fixup.md) with a FnCall rule matching calls whose
identity is one of the newly-classified Known variants, rewriting the call
target to libc::<symbol> and dropping the now-dead shim-lowered extern "C"
item when nothing else in the translation unit still references it. Follow
docs/writing-a-fixup.md's AST-to-AST rule - no string rewriting.

Per this project's rule that correctness lives in baseline lowering: this
fixup must be strictly optional. With it disabled, the baseline
shim-lowered extern "C" declaration (today's behavior) must still be correct
Rust, just non-portable across libc/arch - the fixup only changes
*idiomaticity/portability*, never introduces new correctness.
acceptance_criteria:
Every symbol confirmed substitutable in slate-4wl9.1's table is classified
and rewritten by the fixup when called. New differential fixtures exist for
at least: a plain function substitution, a varargs substitution (ioctl), and
a constant substitution, each passing identically with the fixup enabled and
disabled (disabled = today's shim-lowered baseline). cargo fmt, cargo
clippy, and cargo nextest r --release all pass. No shim header or baseline
lowering path is removed - only the fixup's new output changes.

title: Audit libc-shim symbols for ABI-compatible libc:: crate equivalents
description:
Walk libc-shim's declared functions and object-like constants (pthread.h,
fenv.h, stdint.h limits, ioctl and friends, etc.) and check each against the
`libc` crate's exports for Slate's supported matrix: {x86_64, aarch64} x
{gnu, musl}. For each symbol, record whether libc:: exposes a
signature/ABI-compatible item (same param/return types after accounting for
Slate's C-to-Rust type lowering, same layout for any struct/typedef
involved), and any per-target divergence libc:: already encodes that the
shim currently hand-splits with #if defined(__SLATE_LIBC_GNU)/#elif
__SLATE_LIBC_MUSL (ioctl's second parameter is the motivating case: unsigned
long on glibc, int on musl).

Produce a table (symbol -> libc:: path, or "no match" + reason) covering at
minimum every symbol the shim currently #if-splits by libc, plus the
pthread_* and fenv_t-family symbols touched this session. Do not modify any
shim headers or lowering code in this task - this is a research/audit task
whose output is the substitution table plus a short note per unmatched
symbol explaining why (missing from libc::, incompatible layout, Slate-only
semantics, etc.).
acceptance_criteria: A written substitution table exists (symbol, libc:: path or none, verification notes) covering every currently-#if-split libc-shim symbol and the pthread_*/fenv_t symbols from this session; every entry is checked against actual libc crate source/docs, not assumed from memory.

title: Fixup: substitute libc-shim symbol calls with libc:: crate equivalents
description:
Slate currently hand-rolls every libc-shim declaration's Rust lowering as a
literal unsafe extern "C" block with the exact signature the shim gave CIR
(see libc-shim/include/pthread.h's ioctl split between __SLATE_LIBC_GNU and
__SLATE_LIBC_MUSL). Making that portable across libc/arch today means either
hand-writing a #[cfg(...)] block per divergent symbol, or building a
multi-config-diff engine that reruns the CIR frontend per target and merges
declarations - both are work Slate would be redoing that the `libc` crate
(already a dependency of generated output - see lower.rs's libc::c_char,
libc::timespec, libc::mbstate_t) has already solved, target-by-target, for
every function/constant it exports.

Add a fixup pass that, for calls whose function identity is already
classified as coming from a trusted libc-shim header (see
src/function_identity.rs's Provenance::TrustedHeader + Known enum, already
used to recognize e.g. qsort/bsearch/pthread_create/memcpy), rewrites the
call to reference libc::<symbol> instead of the shim-lowered extern "C" item,
when a curated audit confirms libc:: exports an ABI/signature-compatible
equivalent for Slate's supported (arch, libc) matrix (x86_64/aarch64 x
gnu/musl).

This does not replace libc-shim: CIR still needs the shim's concrete
declarations/struct layouts to parse and type-check the C input in the first
place (sizeof, field offsets, etc. all need real facts at parse time). This
fixup only changes what gets emitted for calls whose target has a trustworthy
libc:: counterpart, per docs/writing-a-fixup.md's rule that correctness lives
in baseline lowering - disabling this fixup must still leave correct,
shim-lowered Rust behind.
acceptance_criteria:
A curated table of libc-shim symbols with a confirmed ABI-compatible libc::
equivalent exists, with each entry's signature verified against the `libc`
crate for the full (x86_64/aarch64 x gnu/musl) matrix and any caveats
(varargs, differing request/flag types like ioctl's second parameter)
recorded. Symbols without a confirmed match are left on the baseline
shim-lowered path and are not silently substituted. The fixup pass rewrites
only calls classified via the existing FunctionIdentity/Known machinery,
never introduces a libc:: reference for an unclassified or ambiguous call,
and disabling the fixup still produces correct (if non-portable) Rust.
Differential fixtures cover at least one function-call substitution, one
varargs substitution (e.g. ioctl), and one constant substitution, each
passing identically pre- and post-fixup. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all pass.

title: Facts: out-parameter allocation summary (T** write detection)
description: Cover the second common ownership-transfer shape: a function that allocates and hands ownership back through a T** parameter instead of a return value, e.g. void alloc(int **x) { *x = malloc(sizeof(int) * 10); } called as alloc(&x);. This is a distinct, common C idiom (many library-style APIs use a return code for status and an out-param for the allocated object) and needs its own detection path -- slate-knus.1's callee-allocation-summary only scans Stmt::Return, which finds nothing here since alloc() returns void. Requires the collector to query a function's PARAMETERS (FnDef.params), not just its return statements -- generalizing 'where can this function hand off a fresh allocation' from one exit shape (return) to two (return, out-param write).
design:
New collector (or a second pass alongside slate-knus.1's, sharing the malloc/peel_casts/extent detection helpers, not duplicating them) that scans FnDef.params for a parameter whose ty is Type::Ptr{inner: Type::Ptr{inner: elem_ty, ..}, ..} (T**), then checks the body for an unconditional *param = malloc(...)-sourced write (same is_malloc_call/extent_from_malloc_size logic as the return-value path) with no intervening free or reassignment before every path returns. Keep the same single-consistent-site discipline as slate-knus.1 -- conditional or multiple write sites are out of scope for the first cut. Judge each qualifying T** parameter independently -- a function with several out-parameters (void alloc(int **x, int **y)) can have some convert and others not, since nothing about one parameter's conversion depends on another's.

Note for whichever ticket eventually rewrites this shape (not this ticket -- facts only): the Rust target is NOT a return value. void alloc(int **x, int **y) does not fit fn alloc() -> Vec<T> at all once there is more than one out-parameter -- bundling into a tuple return (-> (Vec<T>, Vec<U>)) forces an all-or-nothing decision across every out-param in the function, which breaks the independent per-parameter eligibility this ticket's facts are designed to support. The correct target keeps the same parameter position and count, just retypes it: fn alloc(x: &mut Vec<i32>, y: &mut Vec<i32>) { *x = vec![0; 10]; *y = vec![0; 5]; }, with call sites changing alloc(&x, &y); to alloc(&mut x, &mut y);, and x/y themselves declared as let mut x: Vec<i32> = Vec::new(); (a zero-allocation placeholder, exactly analogous to the Option<Box<T>> = None placeholder slate-04q.83.4's OptionBoxLocals pass already uses) before the call -- there is no 'was x initialized' question since this ticket only detects UNCONDITIONAL out-param writes, so alloc() always overwrites *x before returning regardless of its pre-call value. The eventual rewrite ticket needs the same cross-function atomicity as slate-knus.3's EditSet but a per-parameter edit shape (retype one parameter + one call-site argument at a time, independently), not slate-knus.4's whole-signature return-type change.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with void alloc(int **x) { *x = malloc(sizeof(int) * 10); } produces an owning summary keyed to the out-parameter: elem_ty=i32, extent=Count(10), transferred via parameter index 0. A fixture where the out-param write is conditional (if (cond) *x = malloc(...);) does not produce a summary. A fixture where *x is also freed or reassigned before return does not produce a summary. A single-pointer parameter passed by value (void alloc(int *x) { x = malloc(...); } -- the caller never sees the write, this is a real C bug, not an ownership-transfer idiom) must NOT be misdetected as an out-parameter allocator. Facts collector covered by fixture-driven differential tests per docs/adding-features.md.

title: Rewrite: interprocedural Box<T>/Vec<T> promotion for simple allocator functions
description: Wire the callee-allocation-summary fact, the caller-eligibility join, and the multi-function EditSet together into an actual rewrite pass: int *alloc(void) { return malloc(sizeof(int) * N); }, used only by callers with eligible local usage, gets alloc()'s return type promoted to Vec<T> (or Box<T> for N==1 / scalar), with every caller's binding type updated in the same atomic edit. This is the first end-to-end ticket in the epic -- .1-.3 build the capability, this ticket ships the first working case.
design: Depends on the callee-allocation-summary, caller-eligibility-join, and multi-function-EditSet tickets. New Pass:: variant placed after Pass::HeapOwnership (reuses its recipe helpers -- box_new/vec construction -- rather than re-deriving them). Scope narrowly for the first cut: single direct-call allocator functions with exactly the shape in this epic's acceptance criteria; do not attempt indirect calls, function pointers, or allocator functions with multiple malloc sites on this pass.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture: int *alloc(void) { return malloc(sizeof(int) * 10); } int main(void) { int *x = NULL; x = alloc(); x[0] = 10; printf("%d\n", x[0]); return 0; } recovers alloc()'s return type to Vec<i32> and main()'s x to Vec<i32>, with x[0] = 10; as safe indexing (no unsafe). Negative fixture: same shape but the caller does raw pointer arithmetic on the result -- both functions stay baseline raw-pointer Rust, byte for byte. Full cargo nextest r --release passes.
notes:
Follow-up: the pass-through wrapper limitation documented at close time
("real, separate follow-on work -- not attempted here") is now resolved.
Multi-level chains (alloc() -> indirect() -> main(), and deeper) now promote
correctly in one atomic edit.

Root cause of the gap: a pass-through caller (fn indirect() { alloc() }, no
named local binding) was never recognized as a "caller" at all by the
eligibility scan, which only matched the null-decl-then-call-then-assign
shape. So alloc() was rejected outright for having zero recognized callers,
even though it was safely used transitively through indirect().

Fixed with an architecture cleanup along the way, not just a bolted-on
third fact (per direct user feedback questioning exactly that approach):
CalleeAllocSummaryFact (.1) is now a genuine provenance union --
AllocProvenance::Direct{elem_ty, extent, ...} for a function whose return
traces to a real malloc/calloc call, or AllocProvenance::PassThrough
{callee_name} for a function whose return is just a call to another
function. Both branches are detected by the same intraprocedural collector
(.1 already had all the return-shape-matching logic; it only needed a
second arm). The interprocedural side (.2) no longer duplicates that
detection -- it walks .1's provenance facts via a visited-set-guarded
resolve_root helper, and the wrapper chain (every pass-through function
between a caller and its ultimate allocator) falls out of that walk as a
Vec<FunctionId> field directly on the existing InterproceduralAllocEligibilityFact,
not a separate fact type. The eligibility conjunction now checks every real
caller across every function in the resolved chain, not just the root.
The rewrite rule (.4) fetches the chain via a new interprocedural_alloc_chain
query and retypes every wrapper's return type (body unchanged -- a
pass-through's `return alloc();` stays exactly correct once alloc() itself
returns Vec<T>) as part of the same atomic multi-function EditSet.

Also accommodates the free()-optionality being reverted (each fixture must
now include an explicit free() call, matching heap_ownership.rs's original
strict requirement, undoing this ticket's earlier require_free relaxation).

Added tests/fixtures/interprocedural_alloc_promotion_chain.c (two-level
indirection) plus a matching differential + structural test. Manually
verified three-level chains and a pure two-function pass-through cycle
(f() { g() } / g() { f() }, neither with an independent allocation) resolve
to "leave both as raw pointers" without hanging, exercising the visited-set
guard on the new resolve_root walk specifically (not just accidentally
rejected by an unrelated check).

First end-to-end interprocedural rewrite in the epic: int *alloc(void) {
return malloc(sizeof(int) * N); } used only by callers with eligible local

Design: wired slate-knus.1's callee-allocation-summary,
slate-knus.2's caller-eligibility-join, and slate-knus.3's proven multi-item
EditSet primitive together. New Pass::InterproceduralAllocPromotion runs
right after Pass::OptionBoxLocals (same position as heap_ownership.rs,
before Pass::DeadLocals). Reused heap_ownership.rs's existing use-rewriting
engine wholesale rather than reimplementing pointer-arithmetic-to-indexing
conversion: bumped OwnedHeap/OwnedHeapPlan/rewrite_owned_stmt (the
structural, name+kind-driven leaf rewriter that converts *p.add(i) -> p[i]
and unwraps the now-redundant unsafe wrapping as part of the same walk) and
added a new OwnedHeap::from_owners constructor so the caller-side rewrite
doesn't need to fabricate an unrelated HeapOwnershipPlan just to build one.
Did NOT reuse heap_ownership.rs's own orchestrator (rewrite_owned_body_stmts/
ownership_plan) -- it's tightly coupled to malloc/free-shaped flat
statement-index bookkeeping (pointer decl must be a top-level Stmt::Let,
calloc-count assumed at allocation_stmt-2, etc.) that doesn't fit a
call-sourced allocation. Wrote a new, much smaller orchestrator instead
(rewrite_interprocedural_alloc_callee/rewrite_interprocedural_alloc_caller
in recipe.rs) that only handles the declaration retyping and
alias/free-statement bookkeeping this shape actually needs, then hands off
to the shared leaf rewriter for every use site.

Two real bugs found and fixed along the way, both surfaced only once an
actual end-to-end fixture was run through the full pipeline (not caught by
any prior ticket's own testing, since neither .1 nor .2 exercised a real
rewrite):

1. The ticket's own required fixture -- x[0] = 10; printf(...); return 0;
   with no free(x) call at all -- was being rejected outright:
   heap_uses_are_owned (reused from heap_ownership.rs for the caller-side
   eligibility check) hard-requires a matching free() call
   (let (free_index, free_temp) = free?;), a requirement heap_ownership.rs's
   own pass genuinely needs (its Box/Vec is meant to REPLACE an explicit
   malloc/free pair) but that doesn't apply here -- the callee already fully
   owns the allocation lifecycle via Vec's/Box's Drop, whether or not the
   caller happens to free it explicitly. Made the free requirement an
   explicit require_free: bool parameter (heap_ownership.rs's own call site
   passes true, preserving its exact existing behavior byte for byte; the
   new interprocedural caller-eligibility check passes false). Also had to
   widen OwnedHeapUses's free_index from usize to Option<usize> to carry the
   "no free found" case through, and thread the resulting read_safety value
   into the caller-eligibility fact -- .2's own collector had been silently
   discarding it, but it's required to decide Vec vs Box the same way
   heap_ownership.rs's own ownership_plan does (Elements-extent with
   MayReadUninitialized read_safety must reject the whole conversion, not
   just fall back to raw pointers, matching the existing rule's own
   discipline).

2. .1's CalleeAllocSummaryFact never recorded where the malloc call itself
   lives (only the return statement), so there was no way to remove it once
   the return got replaced with vec![0; N] -- this is exactly the same
   "leftover malloc call executes and leaks" class of bug found and fixed
   earlier in slate-04q.83.4. Added alloc_source_path to the fact (the
   malloc-temp's own Let statement, already located internally by the
   collector via find_temp_index but previously discarded) and removed that
   statement as part of the callee rewrite; verified generated output has
   zero remaining malloc calls or extern declarations once nothing else
   references it.

Scope, matching the ticket's own "single direct-call allocator functions"
framing: only functions with a DIRECT slate-knus.1 base-case summary get

title: Engine: multi-function atomic EditSet for cross-function rewrites
description: QueryRule<Function>/EditSet today opens one transactional edit per function. Interprocedural promotion needs to change a callee's signature + body AND every caller's call-site + binding type together, atomically -- doing it in separate per-function edits risks a state where alloc() returns Vec<i32> but a caller's binding is still typed *mut i32, a type error the pipeline would emit without ever noticing until rustc rejects it (or a differential run does).
design: New rule shape in src/fixups/query/item.rs (ItemPlanBuilder/EditSet) that can name a SET of functions (the callee plus every caller from the caller-eligibility ticket's conjunction) and open one EditSet spanning all of them, following the existing 'never leave the binding's declared type and its use sites inconsistent mid-pass' transactional principle from writing-a-query-fixup.md, just widened from one function's body to N functions' bodies. Related to slate-04q.75.56's broader query/rewrite engine generalization (statement-window matching, memoization) -- coordinate with that work rather than duplicating engine-generalization effort; this ticket does not require slate-04q.75.56 to complete first.
acceptance_criteria: A rule can request edits touching alloc()'s FnDef (signature + body) and every caller's FnDef (call-site + binding type) as one EditSet; if any single sub-edit in the set is rejected (e.g. a caller's binding type can't be resolved), the WHOLE set is rejected and nothing is applied -- no partial cross-function state. Existing single-function QueryRule usages are unaffected (no regression in the current heap_ownership.rs / option_box_locals.rs rules). Full cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason:
Key finding, which substantially changes this ticket's scope from what the
epic's design note assumed: the multi-function atomic EditSet primitive
already exists in src/fixups/query/item.rs. An EditSet is Vec<AnchoredEdit>,
and each AnchoredEdit variant (Function/Expression/Statement/etc.) carries
its own item_index -- nothing in the type requires all edits in a set to
target the same item. The overlap checker (anchors_overlap) already compares
item_index before flagging a collision, so edits in different functions
never spuriously conflict; the per-set validation (missing_targets) already
checks every anchor in a set against the pristine program before any
mutation and drops the WHOLE set if any anchor is stale; and the appliers
(apply_function_edits, apply_statement_edits, etc.) already iterate their
edit lists independently by item_index with no single-item assumption
anywhere. src/fixups/query/rules/unused_params.rs is already-shipped,
already-tested (via its own e2e fixture) production evidence of exactly this
shape: it builds one EditSet containing a Function-anchor replacement of the
callee PLUS an Expression-anchor edit at every call site, which may live in
different functions than the callee -- proving the "callee signature change
+ N callers' edits, atomic or nothing" pattern this epic needs already works
end to end.

Given that, this ticket's actual gap was narrower than its own design note
implied: not missing engine machinery, but missing test coverage proving the
specific "Function-anchor replace in one item + Statement-anchor edit in a
DIFFERENT item, same EditSet" shape behaves atomically -- item.rs's existing
unit test suite (missing_target_rejects_the_complete_edit_set,
mixed_edits_use_snapshot_paths_and_report_one_atomic_application, etc.) only
ever exercised single-item programs, and none of them used an
AnchoredEdit::Function anchor at all (constructing a valid FunctionRef needs
a real FunctionId from facts::analyze, which the existing test helpers never
did). Function-kind edits had zero unit coverage despite being
production-used by heap_ownership.rs, option_box_locals.rs, and
unused_params.rs.

Added two new unit tests to item.rs's existing #[cfg(test)] module (this
file's own established convention for engine-level plumbing that has no
C source to differentially test against):
- function_edit_and_statement_edit_in_a_different_item_apply_atomically:
  a 2-function program, one EditSet containing a Function-anchor replace of
  item 1 ("callee") and a Statement-anchor edit of item 0 ("caller"); both
  land together in one apply() call.
- stale_anchor_in_one_item_rejects_the_whole_multi_item_set: same shape but
  the Statement anchor points at an out-of-range statement index; asserts
  the program is byte-for-byte unchanged (including item 1's otherwise-valid
  Function replacement, which does NOT partially apply), report.applied == 0,
  and a MissingTarget diagnostic is recorded.

Also added a named_function(name, body) test helper (the existing function()
helper hardcoded name: "test", which can't build a two-function program with
distinguishable targets) and a function_ref(facts, item_index, name) helper
that resolves a real FunctionId via facts.function_by_item_index(item_index)
against an analyzed program, since FunctionRef's id field is only
constructible with a genuine FunctionId, not hand-rolled.

No changes needed to AnchoredEdit, the planner's overlap logic, or any
apply_*_edits function -- all of it already handled this correctly. No new
convenience mutator (e.g. push_replace_function) was added either: the
epic's actual need (one Function anchor for the promoted callee plus
Statement/Expression anchors for each caller) is fully served by
EditSet::replace_function(...) followed by push_replace_statement/
push_replace_expression, exactly as unused_params.rs already does it and as
the new tests now directly verify at the engine level.

title: Facts: interprocedural caller-eligibility join (visited-set guarded)
description: Extend the existing local heap-use/pointer_option_eligible checks so a candidate pointer's source can be a call to a function carrying an owning summary (from the callee-allocation-summary ticket), not just a direct malloc call. Add the caller-side conjunction: whether a callee's OWN signature can convert is the AND, over every caller found via direct_calls(function), of that caller's local eligibility check on its own use of the call's result.
design: Reuse CallRecord{target: CallTarget::Direct(name), ..} (forward edge: caller -> callee, resolved via all_functions()) and direct_calls(function) (reverse edge: callee -> every caller) -- both already exist in query/context.rs, built for reachability/inlining. No new call-graph data structure. Walk via ordinary recursive queries; query_cache! memoization handles the DAG. Guard recursion with a visited-set (functions currently being resolved) rather than fixed-point iteration: mark a function in-progress on entry to its eligibility computation; if resolution re-enters an in-progress function (a call cycle), return 'not proven' for that inner lookup only, not an error. This is sound (the safe default is always 'leave as raw pointer') and exact for pass-through-only cycles; it only loses precision when one side of a cycle has an independent proof a full fixed point would propagate through -- documented, accepted gap, not solved here.
acceptance_criteria: Given int *alloc(void) { return malloc(sizeof(int) * 10); } and a single caller that only indexes/derefs the result, the caller-eligibility check passes and the conjunction over direct_calls(alloc) is satisfied. Adding a second caller that does raw pointer arithmetic on alloc()'s result flips the conjunction to false for alloc(). A mutually recursive pair (f calls g, g calls f) where neither independently proves ownership resolves to 'not owned' via the visited-set guard without hanging. Facts/query layer covered by fixture-driven differential tests.
close_reason:
Implemented the interprocedural caller-eligibility join: whether a function
F's signature can convert is the conjunction, over every caller found by
scanning the whole program, of that caller's local use of F()'s result being
compatible with Box<T>/Vec<T> semantics.

Split into two pieces during implementation, since the ticket's own acceptance
criteria (a mutually recursive pass-through pair) turned out to require the
recursion to live in a different place than the description first suggested:

1. Extended, recursive "resolved allocation summary" (new, beyond what the
   ticket description names but required by its own third acceptance
   criterion): slate-knus.1's CalleeAllocSummaryFact only recognizes a
   function whose return traces to a DIRECT malloc/calloc call. A
   pass-through wrapper (`int *wrapper(void) { return alloc(); }`) has no
   such summary at all under .1's intentionally-intraprocedural scope. Added
   resolve_summary(name, ..., visited): base case is .1's existing summary;
   recursive case is "the function's one and only top-level return is
   Expr::Call{func: Var(other_name), ..} to another user-defined function,
   and THAT function (recursively) has a summary too, which gets inherited."
   Verified empirically first (via a temporary PRE_HEAP-adjacent debug dump)
   that `return alloc();` does NOT get hoisted into a temp the way
   `x = alloc();` does -- baseline lowering only hoists call results when
   they're assigned to a named binding, not when directly returned -- so the
   recursive case matches Stmt::Return's expr directly, no temp-name lookup
   needed, simpler than the base case.

   Cycle guard: a plain visited-set (BTreeSet<String>) threaded through the
   recursion, per the ticket's design note -- NOT fixed-point iteration.
   Re-entering a function already in the set returns None for that lookup.
   Verified this resolves a genuine cycle (f() { return g(); } / g() {
   return f(); }, neither with an independent malloc) to "no summary for
   either" without hanging -- confirmed by timeout-wrapped run completing
   normally with zero eligibility facts produced for f or g.

2. Local caller-eligibility check, reusing heap_ownership.rs's own
   heap_uses_are_owned wholesale (bumped Candidate, OwnedHeapUses,
   heap_uses_are_owned, null_pointer_decl, and assigns_allocated_pointer from
   private to pub(super)) rather than reimplementing use-classification
   logic that already correctly distinguishes safe indexed/scalar
   read-write from disqualifying raw pointer arithmetic (via
   reassigns_pointer's fallback rejection) and already requires a matching
   free() call. The only new code is finding the call-sourced allocation
   site itself (call_allocation_temp/find_call_allocation, mirroring
   heap_ownership.rs's own allocation_temp/find_allocation but matching
   "Let-bound temp from a call to a resolved-summary function" instead of
   "Let-bound temp from malloc/calloc").

New InterproceduralAllocEligibilityFact (facts/mod.rs), collected in
src/fixups/facts/interprocedural_alloc_eligibility.rs, exposed via a new
per-function interprocedural_alloc_eligibility(function) query in
query/context.rs -- #[allow(dead_code)] until slate-knus.4 consumes it,
matching the same facts-only pattern as slate-knus.1.

Verified against all three of the ticket's stated scenarios: single caller
indexing/dereffing only -> eligible=true; adding a second caller doing raw
pointer arithmetic -> eligible=false; a pure pass-through cycle -> no summary
for either function, run completes without hanging. All three checked via a
temporary debug dump placed at the exact point right before Pass::HeapOwnership
runs (removed before finishing) -- NOT by printing on every facts::analyze()
call throughout the pipeline. That distinction mattered: an unrelated,
later-running fold pass (something like "zero-init declarations fold into
their overwriting assignment") legitimately simplifies away the
null_pointer_decl-then-separate-assign shape this ticket's detection depends
on, once nothing has consumed it first -- which is exactly what happens on
every snapshot after Pass::HeapOwnership since there's no consuming rule yet.
Printing on every analyze() call initially showed spurious "eligible=true"
results from those later snapshots (the scan finds nothing at all once the
shape is gone, so the conjunction is vacuously true) that had nothing to do
with the actual logic -- same "comparing facts across different pipeline
snapshots produces spurious mismatches" trap from earlier tickets in this
epic. Confirmed correct by checking specifically at the snapshot right after
Pass::HeapOwnership, matching where a real consuming rule would run.
