- Recognize memmove(dst_expr, src_expr, n) operating on overlapping regions of the *same* underlying buffer and rewrite to buf.copy_within(src_range, dest_start).
- Recognize memcmp(a, b, n) compared against 0 (==, !=) where n is provably within both buffers' bounds and rewrite to slice equality (a[..n] == b[..n], or a == b for full-length compares).
- Each rewrite is independent and optional; gate strictly on provable length/bounds, falling back to V0 otherwise.

## Success Criteria
- All four mem* idioms (memset/memcpy/memmove/memcmp) have a landed, independently-toggleable fixup pass.
- Each fixup is covered by a differential fixture demonstrating the before/after shape and passes cargo nextest.
- docs/idiomatization.md documents these as a new rung, consistent with the existing strcmp/printf write-ups.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each child ticket lands as its own fixup pass with a differential fixture.
- No fixup fires when length/bounds are not provable at the call site (falls back to V0 unchanged).
close_reason: Closed

title: Recover argv[i] + atoi/strtol as direct String parsing (drop raw pointer round-trip)
description:
## Why
Baseline lowering for `int main(int argc, char **argv)` already builds the safe Rust form:

```rust
let mut __slate_argv_storage: Vec<std::ffi::CString> = std::env::args().map(|arg| std::ffi::CString::new(arg).unwrap()).collect();
let mut __slate_argv_ptrs: Vec<*mut i8> = __slate_argv_storage.iter().map(|arg| arg.as_ptr() as *mut i8).collect();
```

but then throws it away by reconstituting a raw `*mut *mut i8` array and indexing/decoding through it:

```rust
let _v9: *mut i8 = unsafe { *argv.add(1) };
let x: i32 = unsafe { atoi(_v9 as *mut i8) };
```

This is the most wasteful gap of the batch: the safe data (`__slate_argv_storage`) is sitting right there, computed for exactly this purpose, and discarded.

## What to do
- Recognize `argv[i]` reads (constant or provably-in-bounds-against-`argc` index) feeding either `atoi`/`atol`/`atoll`/`strtol`-family calls or direct string use (e.g. `printf("%s", argv[i])`).
- Rewrite to index `__slate_argv_storage[i]` directly: `.to_str().unwrap().parse().unwrap()` for the atoi-family case, `.to_str().unwrap()` (or the `&str` binding directly) for direct string use.
- Must not fire when `argv`/`argc` are reassigned, passed to another function taking `char**`, or the index is not provably in range — those keep the existing raw pointer path (baseline correctness must not depend on this fixup).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New differential fixture(s): argv[i] -> atoi, argv[i] used directly as a string, and a rejected case (argv passed to a helper function or non-provable index) that must NOT be rewritten.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
- Fixup is independently toggleable.

title: Recover sprintf into a local buffer as format! into a String
description:
## Why
V0 lowers `sprintf(buf, fmt, ...)` with a constant format string to a raw unsafe variadic call writing into a fixed-size buffer:

```rust
let mut buf: aligned::Aligned<aligned::A16, [i8; 64]> = aligned::Aligned([0; 64]);
unsafe { sprintf(buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut i8, c"%d-%d".as_ptr() as *mut i8, 3, 4) };
unsafe { puts(buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut i8) };
```

## What to do
- Recognize sprintf(buf, fmt, ...) where fmt is a compile-time-known constant string, reusing the same conversion-spec parser as the printf/eprintf rungs.
- Rewrite the buffer declaration + sprintf call to `let buf = format!(...);`.
- Reconcile downstream uses of `buf`: raw-pointer/CStr uses (e.g. passed to `puts`) must be rewritten to use `buf` as a `String`/`&str` directly (e.g. `println!("{}", buf)` in place of `puts` on the old buffer).
- `snprintf` can share the same recognizer; truncation semantics (return value / actual written length) must be preserved if the return value is observed, otherwise the size arg is irrelevant once bounded by `format!`.
- Must not fire when the format string is not a compile-time constant, or when the buffer is reused/mutated in ways format! output can't represent (e.g. partial in-place edits after the sprintf call).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New differential fixture(s): sprintf then puts/printf of the buffer, snprintf with observed return value, and a rejected case (non-constant format or buffer reused after the call) that falls back to V0 unchanged.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
- Fixup is independently toggleable.
close_reason: Implemented as a new query-driven fixup pass (src/fixups/query/rules/sprintf_format.rs, Pass::SprintfFormat), positioned right after call_args and before string_lift (string_lift doesn't know sprintf writes through a pointer, so it would otherwise mis-lift the buffer as an empty read-only &str before this pass gets a chance to see the raw array form). Extended facts/printf.rs's collector to also index sprintf (format at arg 1) and snprintf (format at arg 2), reusing the exact same conversion-spec parser and PrintfEnv-based constant tracking printf/fprintf already use. Added a static worst-case-length bound (per-conversion max width, e.g. 24 digits for any integer conversion, constant-string length for %s, reject entirely for float/exponent/general since those aren't safely boundable) that must provably fit the buffer's declared capacity (or snprintf's size argument, itself resolved through the same temp/cast aliasing the lowerer introduces) before rewriting -- this was flagged mid-implementation as a correctness requirement (an unbounded sprintf into an undersized buffer is UB in C; format! has no such bound, so firing without a fits-proof would silently change the program's meaning) and is now a hard precondition, not an afterthought. The declaration + fill call collapse into a single let buf = format!(...) constructed at the fill call's position (not the original declaration's), since intervening statements -- e.g. the format args' own temp bindings -- can appear between them and moving the construction earlier would reference not-yet-declared variables. Downstream puts/printf/fprintf consumers of the buffer are reconciled (puts rewrites to println!, printf/fprintf are left alone since their own rust_string detection picks up the now-String-typed buffer once facts refresh). Buffer mutation or non-constant format after the fill correctly falls back to V0 unchanged, per the bead's explicit 'partial in-place edits' exclusion (a String can't safely represent an arbitrary raw byte write without UTF-8 validity guarantees). Added EditSet::extend to item.rs to compose independently-built edit sets (buffer decl, fill-call statement(s), each consumer rewrite) into one transactional edit. Six new differential fixtures: sprintf+puts, sprintf+printf(%s), snprintf with observed return value, non-constant format (no rewrite), buffer mutated after fill (no rewrite), and an overflow-risk case (4-byte buffer, no rewrite -- exercises the new bound check directly). Full release suite (cargo nextest r --release, 215 tests), cargo fmt, and cargo clippy --all-targets are clean.

title: Recover fprintf/fputs to stderr as eprintln!/eprint!
description:
## Why
V0 lowers `fprintf(stderr, fmt, ...)` and `fputs(s, stderr)` to raw unsafe libc calls even though the existing printf format-string recognizer (Rung 1, docs/idiomatization.md) already knows how to parse the format string and map conversions to Rust format specs for the no-FILE* stdout forms:

```rust
unsafe { fprintf(stderr, c"error: %d\n".as_ptr() as *mut i8, 42) };
unsafe { fputs(c"bye\n".as_ptr() as *mut i8, stderr) };
```

## What to do
- Extend the printf/puts recognizer to also match `fprintf`/`fputs` (and `fputc`/`putc` if in scope) where the FILE* argument is source-provably `stdin`-adjacent well-known stream: `stdout` -> `print!`/`println!`, `stderr` -> `eprint!`/`eprintln!`.
- Reuse the existing conversion-spec mapping and constant-format-string recovery rather than writing a second parser.
- Must not fire when the FILE* argument is not provably one of the two standard streams (arbitrary FILE* stays on the existing libc path).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New differential fixture(s): fprintf(stderr, ...) with args, plain fputs(s, stderr), and a negative case (fprintf to a non-standard FILE*) that must NOT be rewritten.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
- Fixup is independently toggleable.
close_reason: Implemented as a new query-driven fixup pass (src/fixups/query/rules/printf_stream.rs, Pass::PrintfStream) registered right after printf_format. Added Known::FPrintf, extended the shared facts/printf.rs collector to also parse fprintf's format string at its offset index-1 (reusing the identical PrintfEnv-based constant-tracking and conversion-spec machinery printf already uses), and made printf_macro stream-aware (PrintfStream::Stdout/Stderr picks println!/print! vs eprintln!/eprint!). fputs targeting stdout/stderr gets its own literal-string extraction (fputs doesn't interpret %-specifiers). Both rules resolve the FILE* stream argument through the lowerer's single-use temp aliasing (e.g. let _v1 = unsafe { stderr }; fprintf(_v1, ...)) back to a bare stdout/stderr identifier, rejecting any other FILE* source (arbitrary FILE* stays on the existing libc path, matching the negative acceptance criterion). Factored the shared 'replace a call whose int result is discarded or a provably-unused let' logic out of printf_format.rs into replace_int_returning_call so all three call sites (printf, fprintf, fputs) share it. Added four differential fixtures: fprintf_stderr_with_args, fputs_stderr_plain, fprintf_stdout_with_args (symmetry), and fprintf_non_standard_file_no_rewrite (negative). Updated docs/passes.md (renumbered) and docs/README.md. Full release suite (cargo nextest r --release, 215 tests), cargo fmt, and cargo clippy --all-targets are clean.

title: (EPIC) Idiomize stdio output and process-env patterns
description:
## Why
V0 lowers several output- and environment-facing libc idioms to raw unsafe extern "C" calls even though std has direct, safe equivalents: fprintf/fputs to stderr, sprintf into a local buffer, argv[i] indexing paired with atoi/strtol, getenv, and perror. Some of these (stderr printf-family) are a straightforward extension of the existing printf->println! recognizer (Rung 1); others (argv/atoi) are notable because baseline lowering already builds the safe Rust form (std::env::args()-derived CString storage) and then discards it by reconstituting a raw pointer array.

## What to do
- Extend the printf format-string recognizer to fprintf(stderr, fmt, ...) / fputs(s, stderr) -> eprintln!/eprint!, and to fprintf(stdout, ...) if not already covered.
- Recognize sprintf(buf, fmt, ...) with a constant format string and rewrite to `let buf = format!(...);`, reconciling downstream buffer uses (String vs *mut i8).
- Recognize argv[i] indexing (in-bounds against argc) feeding atoi/atol/strtol or direct string use, and rewrite to index the existing __slate_argv_storage Vec<CString> directly (.to_str().unwrap().parse() etc.) instead of round-tripping through the raw pointer array baseline already builds.
- Recognize getenv(name) null-check + CStr decode and rewrite to std::env::var(name) matched via Ok/Err in place of non-null/null.
- Recognize perror(msg) immediately following a libc call that sets errno on failure (e.g. fopen returning null), with no intervening errno-affecting call, and rewrite to eprintln!("{msg}: {}", std::io::Error::last_os_error()). Gate this using the existing def-use/effect fact infrastructure (src/fixups/facts, effects) to prove errno freshness rather than a syntactic heuristic.

## Success Criteria
- All five patterns (stderr printf-family, sprintf/format!, argv+atoi, getenv, perror) have a landed, independently-toggleable fixup pass.
- Each fixup is covered by a differential fixture demonstrating the before/after shape and passes cargo nextest.
- The perror fixup correctly declines to fire when an intervening call could have clobbered errno (regression fixture required).
- docs/idiomatization.md documents these as new rungs, consistent with the existing printf/stdin rung write-ups.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each child ticket lands as its own fixup pass with a differential fixture demonstrating the before/after shape.
- docs/idiomatization.md is updated for each landed rung.
- No fixup fires outside its proven-safe gate (non-stderr/stdout FILE* handles, out-of-bounds argv access, errno clobbered between the failing call and perror, etc. all fall back to V0 unchanged).

title: Recover numeric-only stdin scanf as split_whitespace + parse
description:
## Why
V0 lowers `scanf("%d %d", &a, &b)` to a raw variadic FFI call:

```rust
unsafe extern "C" { fn __isoc23_scanf(_0: *mut i8, ...) -> i32; }
let n: i32 = unsafe { __isoc23_scanf(c"%d %d".as_ptr() as *mut i8, addr_of_mut!(a), addr_of_mut!(b)) };
```

This is the ugliest V0 output of the three stdin cases (variadic unsafe extern C, raw pointer args) and it has a provably-safe rewrite whenever the format string is *purely* whitespace-separated numeric conversions: no literal text, no %s/%c, so there's no ambiguity in how scanf would tokenize the input.

## What to do
- Recognize `scanf`/`fscanf(stdin, ...)` calls where the format string is a compile-time-known constant consisting only of `%d`/`%i`/`%u`/`%f`/`%lf`-style numeric conversions separated by whitespace (reuse the printf format-string parsing/recognition machinery from Rung 1 as a base rather than writing a second parser).
- Reject (leave as V0) any format string containing literal text, `%s`, `%c`, `%n`, or unsupported conversions.
- Rewrite to: read a line from stdin, `split_whitespace()`, and `.parse()` each token into the corresponding out-param's target type, preserving the original return-count semantics (n == number of successfully parsed args) so callers checking `scanf`'s return value against the expected count still see correct behavior.
- Handle both the single-call and loop-until-scanf-fails idioms (see scanf_string.c-style loops) since both appeared in exploration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New differential fixture(s): all-numeric format success case, partial-match/short-input failure case (verify n still reflects partial success correctly), and a rejected case (format string with literal text or %s) that must fall back to V0 unchanged.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
- Fixup is independently toggleable.

title: Recover stdin fgets read-loops as std::io::stdin().lock().lines()
(EPIC) Idiomize stdin patterns
description:
## Why
V0 lowers all stdin-driven C idioms (fgets/scanf/getchar loops) to raw unsafe extern "C" libc calls with pointer buffers, even though several stdin-specific shapes have well-defined safe Rust equivalents in std::io. Slate already has a printf-format-string recognition rung (docs/idiomatization.md Rung 1); this epic adds the symmetric input-side rungs, scoped narrowly to the stdin FILE* (not arbitrary owned FILE* handles, which is a separate tracked gap) so the rewrites stay provably safe.

## What to do
- Recognize fgets(buf, n, stdin) read-loops (with the common trailing-\n strip idiom) and rewrite to `for line in std::io::stdin().lock().lines()`.
- Recognize scanf(fmt, ...) calls where fmt is a constant, purely-whitespace-separated sequence of numeric conversions (%d/%i/%u/%f/%lf, no %s/%c/literal text) and rewrite to read-line + split_whitespace + parse.
- Recognize getchar() != EOF byte-scanning loops and rewrite to `for byte in std::io::stdin().lock().bytes()`.
- Each rewrite must be an independent, optional fixup verified by the differential harness; baseline correctness must not depend on any of them.

## Success Criteria
- All three stdin idioms (fgets/lines, scanf-numeric/parse, getchar/bytes) have a landed, independently-toggleable fixup pass.
- Each fixup is covered by a differential fixture demonstrating the before/after shape and passes cargo nextest.
- docs/idiomatization.md documents a new stdin ladder rung, mirroring the printf rung's structure.
- None of the three fixups fire on non-stdin FILE* handles (own-handle fgets/scanf remain out of scope, tracked separately).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each child ticket lands as its own fixup pass with a differential fixture demonstrating the before/after shape.
- docs/idiomatization.md gets a new rung section documenting the stdin ladder.
- None of the three fixups fire on non-stdin FILE* handles.

title: rewrite_stdio_file_ownership rejects fopen paths stored in a local char[] instead of an inline literal (stdio_file_ownership.c)
description: tests/fixtures/stdio_file_ownership.c stores its filename once in a local array (char name[] = "...";) and reuses it across fopen(name,"w"), fopen(name,"r"), and two remove(name) calls -- an idiomatic way to avoid repeating a literal in C. The rewrite_stdio_file_ownership fixup already handles this exact open/write/read/close/remove shape correctly elsewhere (verified: tests/fixtures.generated/stdio_gets_loop_lines.rs cleanly becomes std::fs::OpenOptions/BufReader/write_all/read_until), but bails here. Traced with 'cargo run -- fixup-debug tests/fixtures/stdio_file_ownership.c --debug-only-pass stdio', which reports rejected_case.file_ownership=item_guard:unsupported_shape. Root cause is src/fixups/query/stdio.rs fopen_path_literal (~line 559), which calls c_string_arg(&args[0]) and requires the fopen path argument to be an inline C string literal expression -- a MethodCall on a local array variable returns None and the whole owner_plan bails for all four calls in the function.
acceptance_criteria: fopen_path_literal (or its caller) also resolves a local char[] that is initialized exactly once from a string literal and never mutated before use, following the alias back to the literal. stdio_file_ownership.c's generated output uses std::fs::OpenOptions/write_all/BufReader/read_until/std::fs::remove_file instead of raw fopen/fputs/fclose/fgets/remove extern "C" calls, and the differential test still passes.
notes: Highest-confidence ticket in this batch -- root cause traced to an exact file:line, and the target behavior is proven working on an adjacent fixture (stdio_gets_loop_lines.c), so this is a guard-loosening fix to an existing fixup rather than new fixup design.
close_reason: Fixed: fopen_path_literal (src/fixups/query/stdio.rs) now resolves a local char[] initialized once from a string literal, in addition to inline literals. Root cause was two-fold: the guard only accepted inline literal exprs, and the array-decay arg shape is Expr::ArrayPtr (not MethodCall) which the original c_string_arg helper didn't handle. Verified via cargo run -- translate: the write-side (f) owner in stdio_file_ownership.c now converts to std::fs::OpenOptions/write_all/drop. Full release suite (201 tests) passes, cargo fmt/clippy clean. The read-side (g) owner hits a separate, distinct gap (fgets rewrite only supports a while-loop shape) -- split out as slate-bsnk.6.

title: Clean up cargo check dead_code warnings
description: Fix 40 dead_code warnings from cargo check: delete genuine orphans (is_rust_ident, is_pack_pragma, unread bookkeeping fields), and mark deliberate-but-not-yet-exercised query-engine/rust_ast surface with #[allow(dead_code)] per existing convention.
close_reason: Cleaned up all 40 cargo check dead_code warnings: deleted genuine orphans, marked designed-but-not-yet-exercised query/AST surface with #[allow(dead_code)] per existing convention

title: Preserve builtin identity when sanitizing fatal directives
description: The release test sanitizes_fatal_directives_without_changing_frontend_source_identity fails because translated Rust no longer contains i32::MAX. Reproduce the directive sanitization path and preserve the frontend source identity needed for builtin constant recovery.
acceptance_criteria: The isolated directive_translate test passes and fatal directive sanitization retains expected builtin lowering without weakening directive diagnostics.
close_reason: Rebuilding the matching SlateMacroDump plugin restored source provenance; the isolated directive identity test now passes without code changes.

title: Restore macro plugin header and record-pack provenance output
description: The release tests reports_toolchain_macro_header_provenance and reports_resolved_record_pack_attributes fail because the macro dump has no headers array and no record-pack entry. Determine whether the CIR Clang plugin output or fixture integration is stale and restore both provenance payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Both isolated plugin_provenance tests pass with the configured CIR-enabled Clang and matching SlateMacroDump plugin.
close_reason: Rebuilt and installed SlateMacroDump.so against this machine's CIR Clang; both plugin provenance tests now pass.

title: Make chibicc union differential insensitive to source-display whitespace
description: The required full release suite persistently fails chibicc_suite::chibicc_supported_tests_match_c although every computed union value matches. The C and Rust stdout differ only in whitespace inside the source-expression text printed by the chibicc harness.
acceptance_criteria: The chibicc union comparison validates semantic output without failing on formatting-only differences, and cargo nextest r --release --test chibicc_suite passes.
close_reason: Root cause wasn't whitespace: anon_local_records (src/lower.rs) named anonymous struct/union fields differently (_tmp / f{i}) than lower_get_member's use-site convention (__slate_anon_{index}), so accesses like x.__slate_anon_0 didn't match the definition -- a real rustc compile error (E0609), not a formatting difference. Fixed the naming to agree on both sides, and fixed tests/support/mod.rs build_multi_bin_batch to stop silently reusing a stale binary from a prior successful build when a batched --keep-going cargo build fails for that bin (that staleness is what made the underlying compile error look like a 'whitespace-only' stdout diff in the original report). union fixture now matches C exactly. Filed slate-5kii for the one remaining chibicc_suite blocker (vla_param, an unrelated ptr-mutability bug), and chibicc_supported_tests_match_c stays #[ignore]d pointing at it.

title: Track enum-constant DeclRefExpr provenance to re-symbolize folded enum values
description: ClangIR constant-folds enum constant references (e.g. 'enum Color c = GREEN;') into bare integer cir.const ops before slate ever sees them - confirmed via emit-cir. This makes unused_items' textual reachability scan see a genuinely-used enum as unreferenced. Fix: mirror the existing MacroConst mechanism (c_ast.rs / lower.rs) - collect EnumConstantDecl DeclRefExpr locations globally (resolving enum tag->typedef name via the existing enum_rust_name helper), thread per-function like macro_consts, and in lower_const match by exact resolved Loc (like next_long_double_macro_const_expr, not value-only like the plain int case, since enum discriminants collide constantly at 0/1/2...) to re-symbolize the folded literal back into Expr::Path(EnumName::Variant), cast to the result type when needed. This lets unused_items treat enums uniformly with structs under real mark-and-sweep instead of needing a special always-alive case.
acceptance_criteria: A C fixture with enum Color { RED, GREEN, BLUE }; enum Color c = GREEN; produces Color::GREEN as <int ty> (or equivalent) instead of a bare literal in the generated Rust, with identical differential (stdout/exit code) behavior; existing enum fixtures (tests/fixtures/enums.c) still pass; cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Implemented enum-constant DeclRefExpr provenance mirroring the MacroConst mechanism: c_ast.rs now builds a global EnumConstantDecl id -> (enum_name via enum_rust_name, constant_name, discriminant value) map, then per-function collects EnumConstRef{enum_name, constant_name, value, loc} entries for DeclRefExpr sites. lower.rs threads these through FunctionLowerer (mirroring macro_consts' BTreeMap/VecDeque wiring) and next_enum_const_expr re-symbolizes a folded cir.const back into Expr::Path(Enum::Variant), cast to the result type when needed. Matching requires BOTH exact loc AND matching discriminant value - loc-only matching (like the long-double macro-const precedent) turned out to be unsafe here: caught a real bug where atomic_flag_ops.c's builtin-expanded atomic ops share source locations across multiple unrelated cir.const ops, which without the value check silently substituted the wrong enum constant into unrelated boolean flag logic, changing stdout. Verified via git-stash diff and the full release suite (194/194) after adding the value guard. Updated the outdated differential test (renamed preserves_enum_declaration_when_variants_are_folded -> preserves_enum_variant_names_instead_of_folded_constants, since the old assertion literally expected the bug this fixes). fmt/clippy/nextest all pass.

title: Add ValueRule query rule kind; migrate string_lift and array_element_pointer_origin
description:
Query-based fixups have DefinitionRule (whole-function fact bag, whole-body rewrite) and
StmtWindowRule (fixed-width statement window, declarative Local matcher, small inline rewrite).
string_lift.rs and array_element_pointer_origin.rs want the StmtWindowRule/CallRule style
(declarative matching, small per-value queries, rewrite built inline in the case) but are stuck
on DefinitionRule because their unit of work is "one local binding plus affected reads," not
"one function."

Add a new ValueRule rule kind (src/fixups/query/value.rs): candidates are one per Stmt::Let
binding (matched via the existing unmodified Local matcher), case returns Vec<ValueEdit> (Stmt
replace/remove or Expr replace via the existing ExprSite/ReplaceExpr type), letting one case
propose edits at multiple sites (def + read sites + a redundant statement to drop). Query layer
exposes small orthogonal per-binding facts (buffer_kind/buffer_provenance/buffer_bytes/
buffer_nul_termination/buffer_ascii_only/buffer_interior_nul/buffer_rejections for strings;
pointer_origin for array-element), not a bundled "plan" verdict - the liftability decision and
the replacement AST construction both live inline in the rule file.

Migrate string_lift.rs and array_element_pointer_origin.rs onto ValueRule as the two proving
consumers. heap_ownership.rs stays on DefinitionRule (deferred, separate follow-up issue) - its
rewrite needs whole-body alias-state tracking and multi-statement removal per binding, a poor
fit to validate the new abstraction against first.

Full design plan at /home/takashi/.claude/plans/sharded-orbiting-aho.md (approved via plan mode
after several rounds of discussion - see that file for the exact API shape, case-body sketches,
and file-by-file cleanup list).
close_reason: Closed

title: Generalize DefinitionRule to a Definition<Cx> matcher
description:
Why: DefinitionRule had the same anti-pattern CallRule did (fixed in .75.56.10.3) - five hardcoded constructors (function, extern_function, header, known_extern_functions, support_module), each locking in one DefinitionRuleSelector variant. Every new selection shape needed a new method. Found while reviewing whether query/definition.rs's rules were still in active use (they are: memchr::helper, externs.rs's two rules, support.rs's one rule) and confirming they should also go through the matcher API for consistency ("rely on the matcher api for all matching").

What to do: added a Definition<Cx = ()> matcher struct (src/fixups/query/patterns.rs), following the same Field<T,Cx> pattern as FnCall:
- kind: Field<DefinitionKind, Cx>
- name: Field<String, Cx>
- group: Field<Option<DefinitionGroup>, Cx>

Replaced DefinitionRule's five constructors and its DefinitionRuleSelector enum with one DefinitionRule::matches(pass, rule, matcher: Definition) constructor. candidates() changed from three different selector-specific QueryContext methods (definitions(exact-key-lookup), definitions_in_group, definitions_of_kind) to one full scan+filter over QueryContext::all_definitions() (new, flattens the existing definitions index) checking kind/name/group via Field::matches. Removed definitions()/definitions_of_kind() (superseded); kept definitions_in_group (still used internally by zero_group_users()'s case-level proof, unrelated to candidate selection).

Updated all four call sites: memchr::helper (function selector -> kind=Function,name=eq), externs::unused_known_declarations (known_extern_functions -> kind=ExternFunction, group=predicate(is_some)), externs::unused_header (header -> group=eq(Some(Header(..)))), support::unused_numeric_parse (support_module -> kind=SupportModule,name=eq). DefinitionRule::extern_function (previously defined, never called anywhere) is gone with the old constructor set - no replacement needed since nothing used it.

Verified via cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical output. Pure refactor, no behavior change.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in the same pass it was created for - see description for full detail. cargo build/clippy/fmt/nextest all clean, 191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical differential output.

title: Generalize CallRule to a FnCall<Cx> matcher, replacing generated()/known()
description:
Why: CallRule::generated(pass, rule, symbol, arity) and CallRule::known(pass, rule, target, arity) are two hardcoded constructor shapes, each locking in one CallTarget variant + a fixed arity via its own method. Every new selection shape (e.g. "match by name AND arg types") needs a new constructor method - not generic, doesn't scale, and can't express anything neither constructor anticipated (like memchr's rule wanting to select on argument types, which today's exact (CallTarget, arity) BTreeMap lookup in QueryContext.calls has no way to express at all).

What to do: build a hand-written FnCall<Cx = ()> matcher struct (src/fixups/query/patterns.rs or a new file), following the same Field<T,Cx> pattern already used by NullaryMethodCall/LetStmtPattern/LoopStmtPattern:

pub(in crate::fixups) struct FnCall<Cx = ()> {
    target: Field<CallTarget, Cx>,
    arity: Field<usize, Cx>,
    arg_types: Field<Vec<Option<Type>>, Cx>,
}

- target reuses the existing CallTarget enum (Known/Generated/Direct/Indirect), so one matcher field subsumes both generated()'s and known()'s selection - Field::eq(CallTarget::Generated("__slate_memchr".into())) or Field::eq(CallTarget::Known(Known::Exit)).
- arg_types matches against each call argument's declared_ty (CallArgFact.declared_ty via facts.call_arg_at(function, path) - already-collected fact, no new fact collection needed). None where the call's target has no known/declared signature (e.g. memchr's synthetic __slate_memchr target - expected to just be Field::Any for that rule, demonstrating the field exists without forcing every rule to use it).
- Requires adding #[derive(PartialEq, Eq)] to rust_ast::Type (currently missing; verified safe - every field/variant in Type's definition is already Eq-safe, no floats anywhere in it, and every component type (CLibType, Prim, Abi, Ident, etc.) already derives PartialEq/Eq).
- #[derive(Default)] on FnCall<Cx> (Field<T,Cx> already derives Default via #[default] Any), giving the "ignore this field" default the matcher-plan.md design calls for - e.g. FnCall { target: Field::eq(...), ..Default::default() }.

Replace CallRule::generated/known with one CallRule::matching(pass, rule, matcher: FnCall) constructor. candidates() changes from an exact BTreeMap lookup to a full scan+filter over QueryContext's call index (add a QueryContext method exposing all calls, e.g. all_calls(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &CallRecord>, plus a call_arg_types(&self, call: &CallRecord) -> Vec<Option<Type>> helper for resolving each arg's declared_ty via facts.call_arg_at).

Update src/fixups/query/rules/memchr.rs and src/fixups/query/rules/libc_exit.rs to build FnCall matchers instead of calling generated()/known() (libc_exit's arity/target selection moves into the matcher; its semantic proof - the never_returning_extern decomposition from .10.2 - stays in the case body).

Verify via cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - full differential suite must produce byte-identical output (pure refactor/generalization, no behavior change intended for existing rules).
close_reason:
Generalized CallRule to accept a FnCall<Cx> matcher struct, replacing the two hardcoded CallRule::generated()/CallRule::known() constructors.

Added rust_ast::Type: PartialEq, Eq (previously missing) - verified safe first: every field/variant in Type's definition (Prim, Custom(String), Box<Type>, Vec<Type>, bool, u64, Ident, Abi, CLibType, etc.) is already Eq-safe, no floats anywhere in Type itself (those live in Expr::Value(RustValue::Float(f64)), a different enum). Needed because Field<T,Cx>::matches requires T: PartialEq for every variant including Eq, and arg_types: Field<Vec<Option<Type>>, Cx> needs that bound transitively.

Added FnCall<Cx = ()> (src/fixups/query/patterns.rs), following the exact pattern NullaryMethodCall/LetStmtPattern/LoopStmtPattern already established with Field<T,Cx> (Any/Eq/Predicate) - but this is the first Field<T,Cx>-based matcher backed by facts/caching rather than pure AST shape:
- target: Field<CallTarget, Cx> - reuses the existing CallTarget enum (Known/Generated/Direct/Indirect) directly, so one field subsumes what generated() and known() each hardcoded separately.
- arity: Field<usize, Cx>.
- arg_types: Field<Vec<Option<Type>>, Cx> - matches against each argument's CallArgFact.declared_ty (already-collected fact via facts.call_arg_at(function, path), no new fact collection needed). None per-arg where the call's target has no known/declared signature.
- #[derive(Default)] works transparently (Field<T,Cx> already derives Default via its #[default] Any variant, verified empirically - no T: Default bound leaks through), giving the "ignore this field" default: FnCall { target: Field::eq(...), ..Default::default() }.

CallRule::matching(pass, rule, matcher: FnCall) replaces both old constructors. candidates() changed from an exact (CallTarget, arity) BTreeMap lookup to a full scan+filter: QueryContext::all_calls() (new, flattens the existing calls index) filtered by matcher.target.matches(...) && matcher.arity.matches(...) && matcher.arg_types.matches(&query.call_arg_types(call), ...) - the && short-circuits, so arg type resolution (the only non-trivial-cost check) only runs for calls that already passed target+arity. QueryContext::call_arg_types(call) is the new per-call-site arg type resolver.

Updated rules/memchr.rs and rules/libc_exit.rs to build FnCall matchers (target + arity; arg_types left at the Field::Any default for both, since neither __slate_memchr's synthetic generated target nor exit's single-int-arg signature needs type-based disambiguation beyond what target+arity already provides - the field exists and is usable by future rules that do need it, without forcing every rule to specify it). libc_exit's semantic proof body (never_returning_extern) is untouched - that decomposition is .10.2's separate scope, not this ticket's.

Verified via the full gate: cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical output. Confirms the full-scan-and-filter candidate collection produces the exact same candidate set as the old exact-key lookup for both migrated call-based rules.

title: Build ExternFnMatch matcher, replace never_returning_extern
description:
Why: never_returning_extern() bundles "matching extern declaration exists" + "arity matches" + "return type is never" into one opaque predicate keyed on a CallRecord, unreusable by anything besides libc_exit's exact case. The project already has a matcher combinator (Field<T, Cx> in field.rs: Any/Eq/Predicate) and hand-written matcher structs built from it (NullaryMethodCall/LetStmtPattern/LoopStmtPattern in patterns.rs) - but those are pure AST-shape matchers only (no facts lookup, no evidence, no caching). This ticket extends that same pattern to a facts-backed, cached, evidence-producing query for the first time.

What to do:
1. In src/fixups/query/patterns.rs (or a new file if it doesn't fit that structural-only module), add ExternFnMatch<Cx = ()> with Field<T,Cx> members: name: Field<String, Cx>, arity: Field<usize, Cx>, returns: Field<Option<Type>, Cx>. Unset fields default to Field::Any (matching existing Field<T,Cx>::Any/Default precedent).
2. In src/fixups/query/context.rs, add a QueryContext method (e.g. extern_fn(&self, matcher: &ExternFnMatch) -> QueryResult<ExternFnView>) that scans Item::ExternBlock declarations, checks each candidate's name/arity/return type against the matcher's fields via Field::matches, and returns the usual cached Proof/Rejection with Evidence - same shape as every other predicate, just matcher-driven candidate selection instead of a single hardcoded target. Note: this predicate is decoupled from any specific CallRecord/call site (the fact "does this extern function exist and have this shape" is a program-level fact, not tied to a call) - key the cache off the matcher's fields directly (or a derived key), and use the extern declaration's own item_index as the evidence site (matching the lazy_singletons() precedent for a program-level predicate with no natural call-specific location).
3. Define ExternFnView (in views.rs, matching existing typed-proof-view precedent) with whatever fields the caller needs (arity, ret type at minimum) - or return the matched Item::ExternBlock's function decl info directly if that's simpler.
4. Add a small CallCaseContext::require(&self, condition: bool) -> Result<(), Rejection> helper (rule.rs) mirroring StmtWindowCaseContext's existing one, using a new Predicate::CallGuard - needed for any remaining plain boolean checks in call-rule cases that don't warrant their own named predicate.
5. Update src/fixups/query/rules/libc_exit.rs's case to build and pass an ExternFnMatch explicitly (name: Field::eq("exit"), arity: Field::eq(1), returns: Field::eq(Some(Type::Never))) instead of calling the old never_returning_extern().
6. Remove never_returning_extern from context.rs, CallCaseContext (rule.rs), Predicate enum (proof.rs), and predicate_name (rewrite.rs). Add Predicate::KnownExternDeclaration (or similar) for the new matcher-based predicate's own tracing identity if EvidenceDetail::KnownExternDeclaration's existing shape doesn't already cover it.

Verify via cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - full differential suite must produce byte-identical output (pure refactor, no behavior change intended).
close_reason:
Replaced never_returning_extern() with an ExternFn<Cx> matcher, following the same Field<T,Cx> pattern as FnCall/Definition/Local rather than the original ticket's standalone ExternFnMatch-with-its-own-view design - kept consistent with what actually shipped in .10.3/.10.4/(unticketed Value/Local work) since this ticket was written before that pattern was established.

ExternFn<Cx = ()> (patterns.rs): name: Field<String,Cx>, arity: Field<usize,Cx>, returns: Field<Option<Type>,Cx>.

QueryContext::extern_fn(&self, matcher: &ExternFn) -> QueryResult<()> (context.rs) - NOT wrapped in the query_cache! macro, unlike most predicates: a Field<T,Cx>-based matcher can hold a boxed Predicate closure, which can't implement Eq+Hash, so it can't be used as a query_cache! HashMap key. Written as a plain method instead (same pattern already used for local_value/call_arg_types/all_calls, none of which are cached either). Scans Item::ExternBlock declarations, checks name/arity/returns via Field::matches, preserves the original's MissingEvidence-vs-Contradicted rejection distinction (saw a declaration with a matching name but wrong arity/return type, vs. no declaration with that name at all).

This predicate is now decoupled from CallRecord entirely (matches by name, not by a specific call site or the Known enum) - it's a program-level fact about a named extern declaration's shape, reusable by any future case that needs "does this named extern function exist with this signature," not just libc_exit's.

Predicate::NeverReturningExtern -> Predicate::ExternFn; EvidenceDetail::KnownExternDeclaration{target: Known, arity, returns_never} -> EvidenceDetail::ExternFnDeclaration{name: String, arity, returns_never} (decoupled from the Known enum for the same reason - a name-based matcher shouldn't require a Known identity to report evidence). Both were used nowhere else, safe to rename outright.

libc_exit.rs's case now composes: case.extern_fn(&ExternFn { name: Field::eq(Known::Exit.symbol().into()), arity: Field::eq(1), returns: Field::eq(Some(Type::Never)) })?; - using Known::Exit.symbol() rather than hardcoding "exit" as a string literal, keeping it tied to the existing Known enum identity used by the call-side FnCall matcher (from .10.3) even though extern_fn itself only needs a plain name.

Skipped ticket step 4 (CallCaseContext::require + Predicate::CallGuard): not needed - libc_exit's rewritten case has no bare boolean check left, only the one extern_fn proof call. Would have been speculative infrastructure with no current caller; add it when a real case needs it.

Found and fixed a real test coupling: tests/differential.rs's noreturn_c11_uses_process_exit_and_removes_dead_false_branch asserted on the exact old trace string ("evidence.never_returning_extern=known:exit;arity=1;returns_never=true"). Updated to "evidence.extern_fn=name=exit;arity=1;returns_never=true" matching the renamed predicate/evidence format - verified against actual `fixup-debug --debug-only-pass libc_exit` output before updating. The case name itself ("never_returning_extern", the .case() label, distinct from the Predicate enum) was left unchanged since it still accurately describes what the case proves, and renaming it wasn't required by this ticket - avoided incidental extra churn.

Verified via cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, output identical apart from the one intentionally-updated trace-format assertion.

title: Decompose dead_local/sole_use into orthogonal no_reads/no_writes/sole_read predicates
description:
Why: dead_local(window, name) bundles "no reads" and "no writes" into one predicate; sole_use(window, name) bundles "no writes" and "exactly one read at a specific path" into another. Neither condition is independently reusable as currently written, even though "no writes alone" is exactly what a future mut-removal-style predicate would want (a variable can be non-mutable if it's not written to, regardless of read count).

What to do: in src/fixups/query/context.rs, replace:
- dead_local(window, name) -> QueryResult<BindingId> with two predicates: no_reads(window, name) -> QueryResult<BindingId> (proves def_use.reads.is_empty()) and no_writes(window, name) -> QueryResult<BindingId> (proves def_use.writes.is_empty()). Factor the shared binding/def_use resolution (function lookup, def_path construction, binding_by_local_path, def_use fact lookup) into a private non-cached helper both predicates call, to avoid duplicating that boilerplate.
- sole_use(window, name) -> QueryResult<BindingId> with no_writes (reuse the one above) plus sole_read(window, name) -> QueryResult<AstPath> (proves reads.len() == 1, returns the read's path - RejectionReason::Ambiguous for reads.len() != 1, matching the existing const_u8/const_usize precedent for "found the wrong count").

Update src/fixups/query/stmt_window.rs's StmtWindowCaseContext with no_reads/no_writes/sole_read wrappers (delete the sole_use/dead_local ones).

Update the two rule cases:
- src/fixups/query/rules/dead_locals.rs: case.dead_local(name)? becomes case.no_reads(name)?; case.no_writes(name)?;
- src/fixups/query/rules/final_return_temps.rs: case.sole_use(name)? becomes case.no_writes(name)?; let read_path = case.sole_read(name)?; case.require(read_path == <expected return-statement path>)?;

Update Predicate enum (proof.rs) and predicate_name (rewrite.rs): remove DeadLocal/SoleUse, add NoReads/NoWrites/SoleRead.

Verify via cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - full differential suite must produce byte-identical output (pure refactor, no behavior change intended).
close_reason:
Superseded by a bigger design than originally scoped here - implemented as "Value<Cx>/Local<Cx> matchers" rather than flat no_reads/no_writes/sole_read predicates, per follow-on discussion after this ticket was created. See matcher-plan.md.

Rather than exposing three separate case-level predicate calls (no_reads/no_writes/sole_read), the usage information (reads/writes counts) moved up to StmtWindowRule's candidate SELECTION step, the same way FnCall/Definition already moved call/definition matching to selector-level Field<T,Cx> matchers (.75.56.10.3/.10.4). Concretely:

- New shared value types (views.rs): Usage { reads: usize, writes: usize }, ResolvedValue { ty: Option<Type>, usage: Option<Usage>, purity: Option<Purity> } - "what do we know about the data at this expression position," generalizing beyond just locals so the same resolver can eventually back FnCall argument matching too (not wired for args yet - no concrete rule needs it, deferred until one does).
- Value<Cx> matcher (patterns.rs): ty/usage/purity as Field<T,Cx> members, with its own matches(&ResolvedValue, &Cx) method (same shape as NullaryMethodCall/LetStmtPattern).
- Local<Cx> matcher: name/mutable/value: Value<Cx>, for StmtWindowRule's per-window binding matching.
- StmtWindowRule::matching_local(matcher: Local) (stmt_window.rs) - when set, candidates() additionally requires the window's first statement to be a Stmt::Let matching the matcher (structurally and via QueryContext::local_value, a new plain resolver: binding_type_ast for ty, def_use counts for usage, the Let statement's own EffectFact for purity).
- context.rs: dead_local/sole_use predicates removed entirely (dead_local fully superseded - "reads:0,writes:0" is now a matcher field, no case-level predicate needed at all; sole_use partially superseded - "writes:0,reads:1" moved to the matcher, but a read_path(window,name) predicate stays case-level since final_return_temps still needs the read's specific AstPath for the window-shape comparison against the return statement, which a mere usage count can't express).
- Added StmtWindowCaseContext::stmt_path(offset) - computes the AstPath of a specific window statement, used to compare read_path against the return statement's own path.

Updated dead_locals.rs (usage:{0,0} in the matcher; case body now only handles the discardable_known_method-or-no_effects branch, which genuinely can't fold into a matcher field since it's an either/or between a structural AST check and a fact-based fallback) and final_return_temps.rs (mutable:false + usage:{reads:1,writes:0} in the matcher; case body keeps the is_temp_name/returned-name/read-path-equals-return-statement checks, which are window-shape relationships, not properties of the binding alone).

Verified via cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical output to before this change.

title: Orthogonal, matcher-driven query predicates
description:
Why: never_returning_extern() (libc_exit) bundles three separate facts into one opaque predicate - a matching extern declaration exists, its arity matches the call, its return type is never - so nothing else can reuse any one of those facts independently. dead_local(name) (dead_locals, from slate-04q.75.19) has the same shape problem at smaller stakes: "no reads" and "no writes" are useful independently (e.g. a mut-removal predicate only needs "no writes") but only queryable as a bundled pair today. Full design: see matcher-plan.md at the repo root ("Orthogonal, matcher-driven query predicates").

What to do, two different fixes for two different problem shapes:

1. Binding-level fact predicates (no_reads, no_writes, sole_read, no_effects) - these prove a property of one already-identified binding, no "which one matches" search involved. Split dead_local into no_reads(window, name) and no_writes(window, name) as flat named QueryContext methods; split sole_use (final_return_temps) into no_writes (reuse the same one) and sole_read(window, name) -> AstPath (proves exactly one read, returns its path, caller checks the path matches what it expects via case.require()). Update dead_locals.rs and final_return_temps.rs rule cases to compose these instead of calling one bundled predicate.

2. Language-item queries (calls, extern declarations, and future kinds) - these search for a candidate matching a shape with independently-optional criteria. Build on the existing Field<T, Cx> combinator (field.rs) and hand-written matcher pattern (NullaryMethodCall/LetStmtPattern/LoopStmtPattern in patterns.rs), which today are pure-AST-shape-only (no facts, no evidence, no caching) - extend the same pattern to a facts-backed, cached, evidence-producing query. Concretely: an ExternFnMatch<Cx> struct with Field<T,Cx> members (name, arity, returns), and a QueryContext method that scans extern declarations, checks each field via Field::matches, and returns the usual cached QueryResult<T> (Evidence/Rejection like every other predicate) instead of a boolean. Replace never_returning_extern with this; update libc_exit.rs's rule case to compose the matcher explicitly (name/arity/returns all as separate matcher fields, unset ones defaulting to Field::Any).

Out of scope: a generic/derived matcher mechanism (Matchable derive) - matcher-plan.md already called this "scope this down" until hand-written matcher structs are repetitive across 3+ item kinds; right now there's exactly one candidate (ExternFnMatch), so a reflection layer would be premature.
acceptance_criteria:
- dead_local and sole_use predicates are gone, replaced by no_reads/no_writes/sole_read composed directly in dead_locals.rs's and final_return_temps.rs's rule cases.
- never_returning_extern is gone, replaced by an ExternFnMatch<Cx> matcher struct (built from Field<T,Cx>) and a QueryContext method that takes it and returns a cached QueryResult; libc_exit.rs's rule case composes name/arity/returns explicitly via the matcher.
- No new generic/derive matcher mechanism introduced - hand-written matcher structs only, matching existing patterns.rs precedent.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass; full differential suite output identical to before this change (pure internal refactor, no behavior change).
close_reason: All four children complete: .10.1 (dead_local/sole_use decomposition, superseded by the later Value/Local matcher work), .10.2 (ExternFn matcher replacing never_returning_extern), .10.3 (FnCall matcher generalizing CallRule candidate selection), .10.4 (Definition matcher generalizing DefinitionRule candidate selection). The query engine's rule-selection layer is now uniformly matcher-driven: CallRule::matches(FnCall), DefinitionRule::matches(Definition), StmtWindowRule::matching_local(Local), and case-level predicates like extern_fn(ExternFn) all compose from the same Field<T,Cx> combinator, replacing the earlier one-constructor-per-shape and bundled-predicate APIs. Full differential gate clean throughout (191 passed, 2 skipped).

title: Generalize the diagnostic consistency check to cover every resolve() call
description:
Why: .8.3's diagnostic-only check (FixupFacts::diff_incremental, slate verify-incremental-facts, tests/incremental_facts_regression.rs) only verified the two hand-picked splice sites .8.4 wired up (LazySingleton, RangeLoop's no-op-changed path). Now that .9.2 makes every fact-needing point in the pipeline go through incremental.resolve(), the diagnostic should cover all of them uniformly, not just two.

What to do: update the verification hook (verify_incremental_facts/IncrementalFactsReport in fixups/mod.rs) to instrument IncrementalFacts::resolve itself (or wrap every resolve() call site) so that whenever a Touched(set) resolution happens, it's compared against a full facts::analyze of the same post-edit program - same diff_incremental-based comparison as before, just triggered generically instead of at two hand-picked call sites. Everything resolutions need no check (they already recompute via full facts::analyze, nothing to compare against).

Verify via:
- slate verify-incremental-facts <file.c> on a few manually chosen fixtures spanning several different migrated/legacy step transitions (not just LazySingleton/RangeLoop).
- cargo nextest r --release --test incremental_facts_regression --run-ignored=all across the whole fixture corpus - expect the same 238/240 baseline (the 2 failures are the pre-existing c23-args gap, unrelated).
- Full cargo nextest r --release (191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical output).

Update matcher-plan.md's "Verification" section if the mechanism ends up differing from what's currently described there.
close_reason: Cancelled per explicit user direction: the full differential suite (cargo nextest r --release) is sufficient verification for this mechanism swap - no separate diagnostic-only consistency check needed beyond what .8.3 already built. .9.2's acceptance criteria (byte-identical differential output) stands as the verification bar.

title: Rewire fixups/mod.rs to thread one IncrementalFacts through apply_with_logger
description:
Why: this is where the payoff lands - replacing ad hoc facts::analyze rebindings and .8.4's hand-picked LazySingleton/RangeLoop splice special-casing with the uniform IncrementalFacts mechanism from .9.1.

What to do: apply_with_logger currently rebinds `let facts::AnalyzedProgram { facts, .. } = facts::analyze(&program);` about 20 times by hand, plus has bespoke splice-vs-analyze logic for LazySingleton and RangeLoop from .8.4 (including RangeLoop's special-case around late_loop_cleanup). Replace all of this with:

- One `let mut incremental = IncrementalFacts::from(facts::analyze(&input).facts);` (or equivalent) constructed once near the top of apply_with_logger.
- Every migrated (query-engine) step calls `incremental.mark_touched(&report.touched)` after plan.apply() - uniformly, not just for LazySingleton/RangeLoop.
- Every legacy (Fixup-trait) step, and late_loop_cleanup, calls `incremental.mark_everything_dirty()` when it reports changed - uniformly, replacing RangeLoop's late_loop_cleanup special-case with the same generic treatment every legacy mutation gets.
- Every place that currently does `let facts::AnalyzedProgram { facts, .. } = facts::analyze(&program);` to get facts for the next step instead does `let facts = incremental.resolve(&program);`.
- Delete .8.4's splice_incremental_facts helper and the LazySingleton/RangeLoop-specific Option<TouchedItems> plumbing (lazy_singleton_touched, range_loop_touched) - fully subsumed.
- verify_incremental_facts/IncrementalFactsReport (the .8.3 diagnostic hook) needs updating to call into the new resolve() path instead of its own splice_incremental_facts copy - coordinate with .9.3, or do a minimal compatible update here and let .9.3 generalize it further.

Acceptance: cargo nextest r --release produces byte-identical output to before this change (same bar .8.4 used) - this is a pure internal-mechanism swap. cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets clean.
close_reason:
Rewired apply_with_logger to thread one IncrementalFacts (from .9.1) through the whole pipeline, replacing all ~20 manual `let facts::AnalyzedProgram { facts, .. } = facts::analyze(&program);` rebindings with `let facts = incremental.resolve(&program);`, and deleting .8.4's hand-picked LazySingleton/RangeLoop splice-vs-analyze special-casing entirely (the lazy_singleton_touched/range_loop_touched Option<TouchedItems> plumbing and their match blocks are gone).

Pattern applied uniformly to every step:
- Every migrated (query-engine Plan-based) step - AnonymousStructs, LazySingleton, MemchrPreludeFixupCalls, MemchrPrelude, RangeLoop (only on its no-op-changed path), LibcExit, PruneUnusedDefinitions - captures `let report = plan.apply(...)` and calls `incremental.mark_touched(&report.touched)`. This is now uniform across all 7 migrated steps, not just the 2 .8.4 hand-picked.
- Every legacy (Fixup-trait) step calls `incremental.mark_everything_dirty()` unconditionally as the last statement in its block (naturally gated by the step! macro's `run` check, so it only fires when the step actually executes) - matching today's actual behavior exactly, since the pre-existing code already blindly reanalyzed at every fact-consuming point regardless of whether intervening steps changed anything.
- RangeLoop's late_loop_cleanup hazard (mutates arbitrary functions without reporting what) is now handled by the same generic split every migrated step could hit: if report.changed (meaning late_loop_cleanup ran), mark_everything_dirty(); else mark_touched(&report.touched). No RangeLoop-specific code path anymore - it's the same two-branch pattern any future migrated step with a similar hazard would use.
- MemchrPreludeFixupCalls/MemchrPrelude/LibcExit's previously-internal `facts::analyze` calls (self-contained within their step bodies) now go through `incremental.resolve(&program)` too, so these three also benefit from splicing if they ever end up adjacent to another migrated step with nothing legacy in between.

Removed the .8.3 diagnostic infrastructure per explicit user direction (differential tests are sufficient verification for this mechanism, no separate diagnostic-only check needed): `fixups::verify_incremental_facts`, `IncrementalFactsReport`, the `slate verify-incremental-facts` CLI command in main.rs, and tests/incremental_facts_regression.rs (plus its Cargo.toml [[test]] entry) are all deleted. `FixupFacts::diff_incremental` itself (the comparison primitive) was left alone since it's not exclusively coupled to the deleted CLI/test surface, but nothing calls it anymore after this cleanup - noting this in case it becomes genuinely dead and worth removing in a future pass.

Verified via the full differential suite: cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical output to before this change, confirming the uniform IncrementalFacts mechanism produces exactly the same program transformations as the old hand-audited per-step-pair logic across every step transition in the pipeline, not just the two .8.4 covered. cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt clean throughout.

Also spot-checked cargo run -- translate on a few fixtures spanning different step transitions (add.c, lazy_singleton.c, range_loop_local_array.c) - all translate cleanly with no panics.

The epic's main promised payoff now holds: any future pass migration under slate-04q.75 that ends up adjacent to another migrated step (nothing legacy between them) gets the splice-instead-of-analyze treatment automatically via mark_touched/resolve, with zero additional wiring in fixups/mod.rs - no more per-pair auditing needed.

title: Add IncrementalFacts type: Dirty marker, mark_touched, mark_everything_dirty, resolve
description:
Why: this is the core mechanism slate-04q.75.56.9 needs - a single place that owns the splice-vs-analyze decision instead of it being hand-audited per call site.

What to do: add a new type (proposed name IncrementalFacts, likely in src/fixups/facts/mod.rs alongside FixupFacts) wrapping a FixupFacts plus a Dirty marker enum with three states: Clean, Touched(TouchedItems), Everything.

- mark_touched(&mut self, touched: &TouchedItems): unions touched.in_place/removed into the existing Touched set (or escalates to Everything if touched.unbounded, or if the current state is already Everything - Everything is absorbing). Cheap, no recompute.
- mark_everything_dirty(&mut self): sets the marker to Everything unconditionally.
- resolve(&mut self, program: &Program) -> &FixupFacts: the only place recompute happens. Clean is a no-op. Touched(set) splices via the existing FixupFacts::remove_items (for the removed set) then FixupFacts::splice_function per in-place item (reusing the exact logic already proven as fixups/mod.rs's splice_incremental_facts helper from .8.4 - move/adapt that helper's logic in here rather than duplicating it). Everything falls back to a full facts::analyze(program) and replaces self.facts entirely. Either way, clears the marker to Clean before returning.

This ticket only adds the type and its logic - do not wire it into fixups/mod.rs yet (that's a separate ticket, .9.2), so it can be verified in isolation first (e.g. via a temporary CLI hook or direct construction in tests, matching how .8.2 was verified before .8.4 wired it into production).
close_reason:
Added the IncrementalFacts type to src/fixups/mod.rs: a FixupFacts plus a Dirty marker enum (Clean, Touched(query::TouchedItems), Everything).

- mark_touched(&mut self, touched: &TouchedItems): unbounded touches or an already-Everything state escalate/stay at Everything; otherwise merges into the existing Touched set (or starts one) via TouchedItems::merge. Cheap, never recomputes.
- mark_everything_dirty(&mut self): sets Everything unconditionally.
- resolve(&mut self, program: &Program) -> FixupFacts: the only place recompute happens. Clean is a no-op, Touched(set) reuses the existing splice_incremental_facts helper (remove_items then splice_function per item, exactly the logic .8.4 already proved), Everything falls back to facts::analyze. Returns an owned clone of self.facts (not a borrow) - resolve() needing &mut self while later steps also need &mut incremental for mark_touched/mark_everything_dirty made a borrowed return type incompatible with this codebase's existing pattern of one facts variable read across several subsequent step blocks before the next recompute point.

Built and verified in isolation (not yet wired into apply_with_logger - that landed together with this ticket, see .9.2's close reason, since the user asked to roll both into one pass rather than stopping at the type-only checkpoint). cargo build and cargo clippy --all-targets clean throughout.

title: Query-owned incremental facts (dirty-tracked resolve-on-read)
description:
Why: slate-04q.75.56.8 proved per-function fact splicing (splice_function/remove_items) works, and .8.4 wired it in for exactly two step transitions (LazySingleton, RangeLoop) - but only after hand-auditing every step pair in fixups/mod.rs for whether an external facts::analyze immediately follows with nothing else mutating in between. That audit doesn't scale: every future pass migration (47 remaining under slate-04q.75) would need the same manual reasoning repeated for however many step-pairs it touches. Full design: see matcher-plan.md at the repo root ("Query-owned incremental facts").

What to do: replace the ~20 manual facts::analyze(&program) rebindings and the .8.4 hand-picked splice wiring in fixups/mod.rs with a single IncrementalFacts value (FixupFacts + a Dirty marker: Clean, Touched(TouchedItems), or Everything) threaded through apply_with_logger.

- Migrated steps call incremental.mark_touched(&report.touched) after plan.apply() - cheap, never recomputes.
- Legacy steps and late_loop_cleanup call incremental.mark_everything_dirty() when they changed something - same treatment for both, no RangeLoop-style special-casing.
- Any step that needs facts calls incremental.resolve(&program) - the only place recompute happens: Clean no-ops, Touched(set) splices via the existing splice_function/remove_items primitives, Everything falls back to facts::analyze. Resolving clears the marker.

This deletes .8.4's hand-picked LazySingleton/RangeLoop wiring and automatically extends the win to every future pass migration with zero added per-pair auditing, since resolve() decides splice-vs-analyze uniformly wherever it's called.

Out of scope: legacy Fixup-trait passes still don't report touched functions, so one running between two migrated steps still forces Everything and a full reanalyze at the next resolve() - not a regression, matches today's behavior. Extending self-healing across legacy-pass boundaries only makes sense pass-by-pass as each legacy pass itself migrates; not part of this epic.
acceptance_criteria:
- IncrementalFacts (FixupFacts + Dirty marker) exists and is the sole facts-recompute mechanism in fixups/mod.rs's apply_with_logger - the ~20 manual facts::analyze(&program) rebindings and .8.4's hand-picked LazySingleton/RangeLoop splice wiring are gone, replaced by uniform mark_touched/mark_everything_dirty/resolve calls.
- Every migrated (query-engine) step's transition to the next fact-needing point uses resolve() with no bespoke per-step-pair code.
- Legacy (Fixup-trait) steps and late_loop_cleanup mark_everything_dirty() uniformly when they change something; behavior at those boundaries is unchanged from today.
- The slate-04q.75.56.8.3 diagnostic-only consistency check (FixupFacts::diff_incremental / slate verify-incremental-facts) is generalized to run after every resolve() call across the whole pipeline, not just the two hand-picked sites .8.4 covered; tests/incremental_facts_regression.rs passes at the same or better rate as .8.4's baseline (238/240, modulo the pre-existing c23 gap).
- Full differential suite (cargo nextest r --release) produces output identical to before this change - this is a pure internal-mechanism swap, not a behavior change.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass throughout.

title: fixup-debug trace summary panics: usize subtraction underflow in PassInvocation::summary
description:
Why: found while manually verifying slate-04q.75.56.8.4 (incremental facts wiring) by running \`cargo run -- fixup-debug <file.c>\` to sanity-check trace output around the LazySingleton/RangeLoop steps. Unrelated to that ticket's changes - confirmed via git stash that it reproduces identically on HEAD before the .8.4 edits, and reproduces on the most trivial fixture (tests/fixtures/add.c) with no lazy_singleton/range_loop/incremental-facts involvement at all.

What's broken: \`PassInvocation::summary\` in src/fixups/trace.rs:398-408 computes \`self.after.stmts - self.before.stmts\` (and the same for temp_lets/items) where ProgramSummary's fields (src/fixups/trace.rs:648-652) are all \`usize\`. Any pass that decreases stmts/temp_lets/items (e.g. DeadLocals removing a statement) underflows and panics: "attempt to subtract with overflow".

Repro:
  cargo run -- fixup-debug tests/fixtures/add.c
  thread 'main' panicked at src/fixups/trace.rs:403:13: attempt to subtract with overflow

This affects the full (unfiltered) fixup-debug trace on essentially any nontrivial fixture, and any --up-to-pass value past the first stmt-removing pass. --only-pass filtering to a single pass usually avoids it since most individual passes don't shrink counts, but the general trace path is broken.

What to do: change PassInvocation::summary (and ProgramSummary's usize fields, or just the diff computation) to use signed arithmetic - e.g. cast to i64/isize before subtracting, or store deltas as i64 - so the {:+} formatting works for both growth and shrinkage.
close_reason: Fixed as a drive-by while adding fixup-debug trace coverage for the buffer_cursor query migration (slate-04q.75.13): cast ProgramSummary fields to i64 before subtracting in PassInvocation::summary (src/fixups/trace.rs), exactly as suggested here.

title: Per-function entry points for the 8 migrated-pass fact collectors
description:
Why: incremental facts (slate-04q.75.56.8) needs to re-derive one function's facts without re-walking the whole program, for both in-place edits (CallRule/StmtWindowRule) and as part of item deletion/insertion handling. The 8 collectors it needs (functions, bindings, binding_types, effects, values, string_buffers, string_pointer_views, counted_loops - see src/fixups/facts/*.rs) are each currently only callable as "collect for the whole Program," internally structured as a loop over every Item::Fn (see counted_loop.rs's collect_facts as a representative example: `for (item_index, item) in program.items.iter().enumerate() { ... }`).

What to do: for each of the 8, extract the per-function body of that loop into its own function taking a single (function: FunctionId, item_index: usize, f: &FnDef) (or whatever that collector's existing per-function state needs) and have the existing whole-program collect_facts call it in a loop, unchanged in behavior. This is a mechanical refactor - no new logic, just exposing an entry point that already exists implicitly inside each loop body.
design: Do this one collector at a time, verifying cargo nextest r --release after each (the whole-program collect_facts must produce byte-identical FixupFacts before and after each extraction). Some collectors carry cross-statement state within one function (e.g. counted_loop's Collector tracks slices/len_aliases across a function's body) - that state must stay scoped per-function-call, not leak across functions, which the current whole-program loop already keeps separate by constructing a fresh Collector per function; preserve that. Independent of slate-04q.75.56.8.1 (lazy_singleton migration) - can run in parallel.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 8 collectors has a per-function entry point callable independently of the whole-program pass. Whole-program facts::analyze output is unchanged (verified by the full differential suite). cargo fmt, clippy --all-targets, and nextest r --release pass.
close_reason:
Extracted per-function entry points for all 5 collector units backing the 8 target fact kinds (functions/bindings/binding_types/loops are one unit in facts/mod.rs's Collector::program, since they're produced by the same recursive walk):

- facts/mod.rs: Collector::function(&mut self, function: FunctionId, f: &FnDef) - bindings/binding_types/loops for an already-assigned FunctionId. Deliberately does NOT call push_function (which assigns a fresh FunctionId) - only program() does that, for a function seen for the first time.
- facts/effects.rs: collect_for_function(function, f) -> Vec<EffectFact> - no FixupFacts dependency at all.
- facts/values.rs: collect_for_function(function, f, facts: &FixupFacts) -> Vec<ValueFact>.
- facts/strings.rs: collect_for_function(function, f, facts: &FixupFacts) -> Collected { buffers, pointer_views, libc_uses } - widened Collected's visibility to pub(in crate::fixups) since it's now part of a broader-visibility function's return type. Deliberately does NOT cover ascii_numeric_strings, which is derived from the whole buffers list after every function is collected, not per-function - noted in a doc comment so .8.2 doesn't assume it's covered.
- facts/counted_loop.rs: collect_for_function(function, f, facts: &mut FixupFacts) - pushes straight into facts.counted_loops/counted_slice_loops, matching its existing direct-mutation style.

Verified each extraction individually against the full differential suite before moving to the next, per the ticket's own guidance - all 191 tests passed after every single one, confirming byte-identical whole-program facts::analyze output throughout.

Flagging for .8.2: the 5 entry points are NOT uniform in calling convention - effects/values/strings return an owned Vec/struct for the caller to extend into facts (immutable or no facts dependency), while counted_loop and the mod.rs Collector both mutate &mut FixupFacts directly in place. This is intentional (preserves each collector's existing internal style exactly, per "mechanical refactor, no new logic"), but .8.2's splice_function needs to handle both calling conventions, not assume one. Also: mod.rs's Collector owns FixupFacts outright (struct Collector { facts: FixupFacts }) rather than borrowing it like the other 4 - .8.2 will need to adapt that one's shape (borrow instead of own) since incremental splicing operates on an existing &mut FixupFacts, not a fresh owned one.

cargo build/clippy/fmt/nextest r --release all pass throughout. Not committed per standing instruction - left for review.

title: Wire incremental facts into fixups/mod.rs for every migrated pass step
description: Why: this is the payoff - once .8.1/.8.5/.8.2/.8.3 are trusted, every currently-migrated query-driven step in fixups/mod.rs (AnonymousStructs, MemchrPreludeFixupCalls, MemchrPrelude, RangeLoop, LibcExit, PruneUnusedDefinitions, plus the newly-migrated LazySingleton) should use incremental facts instead of a fresh facts::analyze(&program) call. No exclusion for item-deleting (DefinitionRule/ProgramRule) steps - handling that case correctly is exactly what .8.1/.8.2 exist to prove out. Every still-legacy pass (the ~40 remaining rewrite::* passes) keeps calling facts::analyze exactly as today - "wrap the interleaving passes with a facts analyze," per the original scoping for this work.
design: Note the current pipeline has no two migrated query steps adjacent to each other (legacy passes always run between them today), so the near-term win is skipping the *next* full facts::analyze immediately after a migrated step where nothing legacy runs before the next thing that needs facts - verify this actually applies to at least one real step transition before claiming the win, and say so plainly if it currently doesn't apply anywhere yet. Clustering migrated steps together (sharing one QueryContext/one facts::analyze per docs/writing-a-query-fixup.md's existing guidance) is a separate, complementary, lower-risk lever worth doing alongside this if pass ordering allows it.
acceptance_criteria: Every migrated step (including item-deleting ones) uses incremental facts where a full re-analyze would otherwise immediately follow with no intervening legacy pass; every legacy step's facts::analyze call is unchanged. Full differential suite passes with output identical to before this change. cargo fmt, clippy --all-targets, and nextest r --release pass.
close_reason:
Wired incremental facts into fixups/mod.rs's production pipeline, but only where it's actually safe - not uniformly across all six migrated steps, per the ticket's own design note to verify the win applies before claiming it.

Audited all six currently-migrated steps (AnonymousStructs, MemchrPreludeFixupCalls, MemchrPrelude, RangeLoop, LibcExit, PruneUnusedDefinitions, plus LazySingleton) for "external facts::analyze immediately follows this step, with no intervening legacy pass." Only one qualifies:

- LazySingleton: plan.apply is directly followed by an external facts::analyze with nothing else in between. apply_with_logger now captures the step's report.touched as its result; when the step ran and !touched.unbounded, the next `facts` binding is built via a new shared splice_incremental_facts helper (FixupFacts::remove_items then splice_function per touched item) instead of a fresh facts::analyze. Falls back to full reanalyze when the step didn't run (debug-mode --only-pass/--up-to-pass filtering) or reported unbounded (never happens for LazySingleton in practice, but handled for safety).

RangeLoop looked like a second candidate but isn't safe when it matters: its step body calls late_loop_cleanup (a legacy pass: SingletonScopes/DeadLocals) whenever report.changed, and that legacy pass walks and can mutate every function in the program, not just the ones StmtWindowPlan::apply reported as touched. Splicing only the reported items in that case would leave late_loop_cleanup's untracked mutations stale - a real correctness bug, not just a missed optimization. So the wiring only splices when late_loop_cleanup did NOT run (!report.changed, where splicing an empty touched set is a no-op); whenever late_loop_cleanup does run, `facts` falls back to a full reanalyze exactly as before.

The other five migrated steps don't have an external analyze to skip at all: MemchrPreludeFixupCalls/MemchrPrelude/LibcExit each call facts::analyze internally within their own step body (nothing external follows immediately); AnonymousStructs has several legacy passes (ParamSpills, ZeroInit, StructFieldInit, SingletonScopes) running before the next external analyze, plus its edits are always TouchedItems::unbounded anyway; PruneUnusedDefinitions is the pipeline's last step, nothing follows it to skip. All of these, and every other legacy rewrite::* pass's facts::analyze call, are unchanged.

Refactored IncrementalFactsReport::check to take &query::TouchedItems directly instead of three separate slice/bool params (re-exported TouchedItems from query::mod.rs for this), and factored its internal splice logic into the same splice_incremental_facts helper the production wiring now uses, removing duplication between the diagnostic and production code paths.

Verified via cargo nextest r --release (191 passed, 2 skipped) producing byte-identical output to before this change - confirms the incremental path the pipeline now actually exercises for LazySingleton/RangeLoop matches full reanalysis exactly, not just in the .8.3 diagnostic harness. Also re-ran cargo nextest r --release --test incremental_facts_regression --run-ignored=all (238/240, same pre-existing c23-args gap as .8.3, unrelated).

Found and filed a pre-existing, unrelated bug while manually sanity-checking trace output during this work: slate-8lvb (fixup-debug trace summary panics on usize subtraction underflow in PassInvocation::summary, src/fixups/trace.rs:398-408 - reproduces on the most trivial fixture with no relation to incremental facts, confirmed via git stash that it predates this ticket's changes). Not fixed as part of this ticket; filed as follow-up per the session close protocol.

matcher-plan.md section 5 updated with the actual wiring outcome (which one of the six migrated steps got the incremental path and why the other five don't/can't).

Final gate clean: cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, no regressions.

title: Diagnostic-only incremental-vs-full-reanalyze consistency check
description:
Why: this is the actual "way to test that the incremental caching works" - before fixups/mod.rs is changed to skip a real facts::analyze() call based on incremental splicing (.4), there needs to be a check that catches the incremental path silently diverging from the ground truth (an undocumented cross-function dependency in one of the 8 collectors, a path-remapping edge case in a StmtWindowRule splice, etc).

What to do: add a diagnostic-only check, gated like the existing alive2 regression and compare-effects-rust-rust checks (CLAUDE.md: "diagnostic-only, not a required gate; run it only for explicit [...] work"; not part of the default cargo nextest r --release gate) - after ExprPlan::apply/StmtWindowPlan::apply + FixupFacts::splice_function, recompute the same touched function via a full facts::analyze(&program) and assert the two produce equal facts for that function's entries in the 8 relevant fields.
design: Follow the existing diagnostic-only precedent's plumbing (see tests/alive_regression.rs, tests/effects_regression.rs in Cargo.toml's [[test]] entries with test=false, and docs/effects.md/docs/fuzzing.md for how those are described as ignored-by-default). Needs the 8 relevant fact types to support a meaningful equality comparison scoped to one function - check which already derive PartialEq/Eq (several currently don't, e.g. CountedLoopFact) and add it if missing and safe (watch for float-containing types where Eq wouldn't be sound).
