acceptance_criteria: A diagnostic-only check exists comparing incremental-splice output against full facts::analyze for the touched function after every ExprPlan/StmtWindowPlan apply, runnable on demand, not part of the default cargo nextest r --release gate. Documented alongside the other diagnostic-only checks (docs/effects.md or a new short doc section).
close_reason:
Added a diagnostic-only incremental-vs-full-reanalyze consistency check, gated the same way as the alive2 and effects regressions.

FixupFacts::diff_incremental (src/fixups/facts/mod.rs) content-compares two FixupFacts across the 11 fields splice_function/remove_items maintain (functions, bindings, binding_types, loops, effects, values, string_buffers, string_pointer_views, string_libc_uses, counted_loops, counted_slice_loops), normalizing every FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId to a (function name, ...) key first via Debug-string formatting - no PartialEq/Eq derives were added to rust_ast.rs (Expr contains an f64, so Eq would be unsound there; Debug-string comparison sidesteps this and matches the approach already proven in .8.2's manual verification). Raw ids legitimately differ between a full reanalysis (renumbers from scratch) and an incremental splice (resumes from the current max) even when every fact is logically identical, so function identity is normalized by name throughout, not by raw FunctionId - this matters once removed items are involved (lazy_singleton), since full reanalysis renumbers every function after a deletion.

fixups::verify_incremental_facts(program) runs the real pipeline (apply_with_logger threaded with an optional IncrementalFactsReport) and, after every migrated step that reports touched items (LazySingleton, RangeLoop), splices the touched items into a cloned facts snapshot and diffs against a full facts::analyze of the post-edit program. Exposed as `slate verify-incremental-facts <file.c>`. tests/incremental_facts_regression.rs runs it across the whole fixture corpus (registered in Cargo.toml with test=false, #[ignore]'d, same posture as alive_regression/effects_regression - not part of the default cargo nextest r --release gate).

Found and fixed a real bug while building this: the LazySingleton step's touched.in_place item_index values are pre-edit indices (get_value's function item_index, recorded before its guard-flag static gets deleted), but the flag deletion shifts every later item's position in the already-mutated post-edit Program. Splicing in-place edits before applying remove_items looked up the wrong (shifted) item out of the post-edit program - e.g. spliced get_value's facts with main's actual body. Fixed by reordering the check to call remove_items first (which shifts the cloned facts' own item_index bookkeeping to match), then resolve/splice in-place items - splice_function reads the current item_index off its own facts snapshot, not a stale pre-edit one. This is a real correctness constraint for .8.4's production wiring, not just a diagnostic-harness artifact - documented in matcher-plan.md section 5.

Verified via cargo nextest r --release --test incremental_facts_regression --run-ignored=all: 238 of 240 fixtures match; the other two (c23.c, c23_nullptr.c) need SLATE_CLANG_ARGS=-std=c23, a pre-existing gap already shared with compare-effects-rust-rust/effects_regression.rs, not a splice bug. matcher-plan.md section 5 rewritten to reflect that DefinitionPlan/ProgramPlan edits are now in scope for incremental update (proven via lazy_singleton), not excluded as originally scoped, and documents the new diagnostic tool.

Final gate clean: cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, no regressions (the new diagnostic test target is excluded from the default run by test=false, matching precedent).

title: FixupFacts::splice_function handling in-place edits and item deletion/insertion
description:
Why: once the 8 collectors have per-function entry points (slate-04q.75.56.8.5) and lazy_singleton is migrated as a concrete item-deleting rule (slate-04q.75.56.8.1), something needs to (a) know which function(s)/item(s) an applied edit touched and (b) update FixupFacts to match, without a full facts::analyze.

What to do:
1. Add a FixupFacts method that, for an edit that stayed within one function's body (CallRule/StmtWindowRule), removes that function's entries from the 8 relevant Vec fields and re-inserts freshly computed ones via the per-function entry points from .8.5.
2. Add handling for item deletion/insertion (DefinitionRule/ProgramRule edits, proven out via the lazy_singleton migration): most FixupFacts content is already keyed by opaque FunctionId, not raw item_index (the mapping lives only in FunctionFact.item_index and any other item_index-keyed fact) - so a deletion needs to (a) remove the deleted item's own facts entirely and (b) shift item_index by the deletion count for every FunctionFact (and any other item_index-keyed fact) positioned after the deleted index. This is renumbering, not a full-reanalyze fallback - the whole point of tackling lazy_singleton first is to prove this out for real rather than deferring it.
3. Have ExprPlan::apply/StmtWindowPlan::apply/DefinitionPlan::apply/ProgramPlan::apply report which item_index(es)/FunctionId(s) they touched (added, removed, or content-changed), as part of their ApplyReport types.
design: Keep the in-place-edit path and the item-index-shift path as clearly separate code paths internally (different correctness arguments, different mechanisms) even if they end up behind one FixupFacts method - don't blur them into one case that tries to handle both with the same logic. QueryContext's own eager indexes (calls/definitions/symbol_uses) are unaffected in kind by this ticket - they already rebuild cheaply from whatever Program a new QueryContext is constructed against.
acceptance_criteria: FixupFacts supports both an in-place per-function splice and an item deletion/insertion splice (with correct item_index renumbering), each verified against a full facts::analyze for hand-picked cases. All four ApplyReport types report which item_index(es)/function(s) they touched. cargo fmt, clippy --all-targets, and nextest r --release pass.
close_reason:
Implemented FixupFacts::splice_function (in-place edits) and remove_items/remove_item/purge_function_facts (item deletion/insertion), wired via a new TouchedItems{in_place,removed,unbounded} struct threaded through ExprPlan/StmtWindowPlan/DefinitionPlan/ProgramPlan's ApplyReport types.

Two real bugs found and fixed during verification (manual instrumentation in fixups/mod.rs's RangeLoop step, gated behind SLATE_VERIFY_SPLICE=1, comparing splice_function output against a fresh facts::analyze() after normalizing BindingId/LoopId to (function,name/kind,path) keys - since those IDs are opaque per-snapshot and never compared across FixupFacts instances in production):

1. BindingId/LoopId collision on splice: Collector previously assigned new IDs via Vec::len(), which is only safe for pure-append construction. purge_function_facts's retain() leaves holes mid-Vec, so a post-removal .len() could collide with an existing higher ID belonging to an unrelated, untouched function. Fixed with a new Collector::resume() constructor that computes next_binding/next_loop as a true max(existing_id)+1 (O(n), paid once per splice, not per push). push_function is deliberately left .len()-based since splice_function never calls it - noted as a constraint for any future incremental function-insertion work.

2. Verification harness bug (not in splice_function itself): when one apply() touched multiple functions in a single batch, the original verification loop spliced only one function per iteration into a fresh facts.clone() while comparing against a fully-edited fresh analyze - so other touched-but-not-yet-spliced functions in that same clone read as stale mismatches. Fixed by splicing every touched function into the same clone before the single comparison against one fresh analyze.

Verified via SLATE_VERIFY_SPLICE=1 cargo nextest r --release across the full suite (191 passed, 2 skipped, no panics) after both fixes. All temporary instrumentation (the SLATE_VERIFY_SPLICE block in fixups/mod.rs's RangeLoop step and the verify_splice_matches function) has been removed per this ticket's scope boundary - a permanent diagnostic-only consistency check is .8.3's job, not this ticket's. Final gate (cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release) is clean: 191 passed, 2 skipped, no regressions.

title: Migrate lazy_singleton fixup to the query engine (item-index-unsafe proving ground)
description:
Why: this epic's first step is deliberately tackling the hard case - a pass that deletes a whole Program item - rather than starting with the easy CallRule/StmtWindowRule case and deferring item deletion indefinitely. lazy_singleton.rs (tracked generally as slate-04q.75.27) is the chosen proving ground: see slate-04q.75.56.8's description for why it was picked over unused_items.rs (slate-04q.75.51) - smaller, doesn't need a new reference-tracking domain, and its guard-flag static deletion is exactly the item-index-unsafe shape the rest of this epic needs to handle.

What to do: migrate src/fixups/rewrite/lazy_singleton.rs's three coordinated edits (static mutability/type/init change to OnceLock, function body replacement with a get_or_init call, guard-flag static deletion once dead) onto the query engine. The existing LazyInitSingletonFact (src/fixups/facts/lazy_singleton.rs, if that's where it lives) stays as the semantic source of truth; only the selection/mutation/deletion mechanics move to a declarative rule.
design:

title: Incremental facts for the query engine
description:
Why: this is a must-have property of the query engine, not an optional optimization. The two upgrades the query system needs to demonstrate over the legacy fixup style are (1) declarative rewrite/mutation instead of hand-walking ASTs (done - CallRule/DefinitionRule/ProgramRule/StmtWindowRule) and (2) never needing to worry about reanalyzing facts (this epic). On a large input (e.g. 100k LOC), repeatedly recomputing all ~40 FixupFacts sub-analyses over the whole program after every pass is the dominant cost once lowering is a one-time step and analysis+rewrite+analysis repeats dozens of times - the "sandwich" gets painful at scale even though it's already safe today.

This was originally scoped down to only cover edits that stay within one function's body (CallRule/StmtWindowRule), explicitly excluding item-deleting/inserting edits (DefinitionRule/ProgramRule) because item_index is used as an identity key throughout FixupFacts and shifts when Program.items changes shape. That exclusion is not acceptable as a permanent design: DefinitionRule/ProgramRule-based rules are exactly the ones several already-migrated passes use (MemchrPrelude's helper deletion, PruneUnusedDefinitions), and most of the ~40 still-legacy passes that will eventually migrate need item deletion too. If incremental facts only cover the easy case, the query engine never actually stops needing the reanalyze-everything fallback for a large and important class of rewrites.

Revised approach: solve the hard case directly rather than deferring it. Pick a not-yet-migrated pass that deletes/inserts whole Program items, migrate it onto the query engine, and build incremental facts that handle that case correctly - via item_index renumbering, not a full-reanalyze fallback. Most FixupFacts content is already keyed by opaque FunctionId, not raw item_index (the mapping lives only in FunctionFact.item_index and similar), so a deletion only requires: removing the deleted item's own facts, and shifting item_index by the deletion count for every FunctionFact (and any other item_index-keyed fact) positioned after it. QueryContext's own eager indexes (calls/definitions/symbol_uses, built fresh per QueryContext::new from the current Program) are unaffected in kind - they already recompute cheaply from whatever Program they're given, they just need to be rebuilt from the post-edit Program, which happens for free every time a new QueryContext is constructed.
design:
First child: migrate lazy_singleton.rs (slate-04q.75.27) rather than unused_items.rs (slate-04q.75.51). Both are item-index-unsafe (both delete whole Program items), but lazy_singleton is a much cleaner proving ground - one precomputed fact (LazyInitSingletonFact) drives three coordinated edits (static mutability/type/init change, function body replacement, guard-flag static deletion), and only needs a small DefinitionKind extension (or a ProgramRule, matching how anonymous_structs already coordinates multiple edits atomically) using reference tracking QueryContext already has (symbol_uses already indexes both reads and writes via Expr::Var/Expr::Path). unused_items.rs needs an entirely new reference-tracking domain (type positions, struct-literal names, pattern names) that symbol_uses doesn't cover at all - real work, but a second, mostly-orthogonal project from proving out incremental facts. Do unused_items later, once the item-index-shift mechanism is proven on the simpler case.

Then: give the ~8 relevant fact collectors (functions, bindings, binding_types, effects, values, string_buffers, string_pointer_views, counted_loops) per-function entry points; build FixupFacts::splice_function to handle both in-place recompute (function body changed, item_index stable) and item deletion/insertion (renumber item_index across affected facts, remove/add the affected item's own facts); prove it via a diagnostic-only check against full facts::analyze (same precedent as the existing alive2/effects diagnostics - not part of the default test gate); then wire it into fixups/mod.rs for every migrated step, with no more DefinitionRule/ProgramRule exclusion.
acceptance_criteria:
- lazy_singleton.rs is migrated onto the query engine (DefinitionRule/ProgramRule-based), legacy module removed, differential coverage passes.
- The ~8 relevant fact collectors each have a per-function entry point.
- FixupFacts::splice_function correctly handles both in-place function content changes and item deletion (with item_index renumbering), verified via a diagnostic-only comparison against full facts::analyze.
- Every currently-migrated query-driven step in fixups/mod.rs (including item-deleting ones) uses incremental facts instead of a full facts::analyze call.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass throughout.

title: Establish QueryContext as the sole reader of FixupFacts fields
description:
Why: FixupFacts (src/fixups/facts/mod.rs) is the shared data substrate for both legacy Fixup-trait rewrites and the query engine - it does not need to be rewritten to "match" the query engine, since QueryContext already wraps it and translates specific fields into typed Proof<T>/Rejection results (see matcher-plan.md's answer to this question). What's missing is enforcement: nothing currently stops a rule or case context from reaching into facts.<field> directly instead of going through a QueryContext accessor, which would silently reintroduce the coupling the query engine exists to remove.

What to do: audit src/fixups/query/*.rs for any direct FixupFacts field access outside context.rs, and document the convention (in docs/writing-a-query-fixup.md) that any new fact a rule needs gets a typed QueryContext method (memoized per the caching ticket) rather than being read inline. New fact kinds (e.g. counted_loops for the StmtWindowRule range_loop migration) get exposed the same way.
acceptance_criteria: docs/writing-a-query-fixup.md states the convention explicitly. No FixupFacts field is read outside src/fixups/query/context.rs within the query module.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add memoized query cache to QueryContext
description:
Why: QueryContext's semantic query methods (byte_source, const_u8, const_usize, pure, first_nul, full_byte_view, prefix_contains, never_returning_extern, zero_users, zero_group_users) recompute from FixupFacts/Program from scratch on every call. A rule with multiple cases against the same call site (e.g. memchr's two cases both call byte_source on the same arg) redoes the same lookup. At ~1000 rewrites this waste compounds.

What to do: add a RefCell<QueryCache> to QueryContext, keyed per query kind by the natural key (ExprSite for most, BindingId for first_nul). Each method becomes check-cache-else-compute-and-insert. QueryResult<T> already derives Clone so this is mechanical - no change to case-function call sites or Proof/Rejection semantics.
design: This is within-snapshot memoization only: a QueryContext is built fresh per Program snapshot today and the AST it wraps is immutable for its lifetime, so a cached result can never go stale before the context itself is discarded. Do not build dependency-edge invalidation inside QueryContext - there is nothing to invalidate against at this scope. Staleness only becomes a real concept at the pipeline level (facts::analyze being called ~20 times across fixups/mod.rs), which is explicitly out of scope here - see matcher-plan.md section 5.
acceptance_criteria: All existing QueryContext query methods are cache-backed. No change to any case-function call site. Existing differential tests pass unchanged. cargo fmt, clippy, and nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Memoized QueryContext's 11 QueryResult-returning query methods (byte_source, const_u8, const_usize, full_byte_view, first_nul, prefix_contains, pure, never_returning_extern, zero_users, zero_group_users, anonymous_structs) per snapshot. Went beyond the ticket's plan: instead of hand-writing a cache field + wrapper per method (easy to add one and forget the other), built a query_cache! declarative macro so each query is one entry (signature, cache key, body) generating both the QueryCache field and the memoizing wrapper together. Had to work around a macro hygiene gotcha where a literal 'self' in the macro template doesn't resolve against 'self' typed at the invocation site - fixed by capturing the receiver token (&$slf:tt) from each invocation instead. context.rs grew 1209->1262 lines (+53), well under estimate since no separate compute_X methods were needed. cargo build/clippy/fmt/nextest r --release all pass.

Design: QueryContext::string_lift_plans(definition, recovery: &Field<StringRecoveryCandidate>) is a new plain (uncached) predicate - like extern_fn, it takes a Field matcher argument so it can't be a query_cache! key (Field::Predicate holds a non-Eq/Hash closure). It precomputes every qualifying candidate for a function directly from facts.string_buffers/facts.string_lift_plans (joined by function+binding+path, filtered through the recovery matcher), producing StringLiftPlan{path, name, ty, expr, remove_path} views - no live body traversal needed at proof time since AstPath already encodes each candidate's exact nested position. The two legacy call sites (Pass::StringLift with [BorrowedStr,BorrowedBytes], Pass::StringLiftFixupCStrings with [BorrowedCStr]) became two rule-builder functions in rules/string_lift.rs (rewrite()/rewrite_c_strings()), each hardcoding its own Field::predicate/Field::eq recovery filter inline in the case closure body - DefinitionCaseFn is a plain fn pointer (not a closure trait object), so a runtime-parameterized matcher can't be captured from an outer rewrite(pass) parameter the way dead_locals::rewrite(pass) captures pass into the RULE identity only (never into a case body).

The recipe (rewrite_string_lift in recipe.rs) ports the whole-body rewrite algorithm as a single unified recursive apply_string_lift(path, body, plans) using the same recurse-into-children-then-process-this-level order as the legacy fixup_nested-then-fixup_body, but built on the shared support::walk::nested_body_vecs_mut_with_path/with_path_segment helpers (the same ones stmt_window.rs's apply_body already uses) instead of a bespoke path tracker. This incidentally fixes a latent legacy gap: the old fixup_nested never pushed a PathSegment for Stmt::Loop/Scope/LabeledBlock bodies (only If/Else did), so string buffers declared directly inside those bodies could never match facts.string_buffers' correctly-segmented Site.path and were silently never lifted; the new implementation uses the correct segment set (LoopBody/ScopeBody/LabeledBody/etc.) via the shared walker, so that shape is now covered too - not a behavior change flagged by any test, just strictly more complete coverage from not re-deriving a parallel, incomplete path tracker.

Preserved exactly: the downstream pointer-view rewrite's two shapes - MethodCall(as_ptr/as_mut_ptr) AND Expr::ArrayPtr (array-to-pointer decay, for buffers originally declared as C arrays) - both convert to the same  cast, per the user's explicit callout that this needs to keep working for the array-decay shape, not just the method-call shape. Dropped rewrite_expr_pointer_views, a private helper in the legacy module with zero call sites anywhere in the codebase (verified by grep before removing) - not ported, since it was dead code, not a live code path. Dropped the assignment_index/remove_index >= body.len() defensive bounds check in favor of the fresh-facts-boundary trust already established for heap_ownership: same_container(declaration, assignment) preserves the safety-critical parent-prefix check (never remove an assignment from a different container than the declaration, which would silently leave an assignment to a since-immutable binding in place) but the pure staleness bounds guard is dropped since facts are always freshly computed against the exact body being rewritten within one pass invocation.

StmtWindowPlan::apply already solves this generically: it collects every matching window against one frozen snapshot, then splices multiple non-overlapping windows within the same function body in Reverse(site.start) order (stmt_window.rs's apply_body), so index shifts from an earlier removal never corrupt a later one in the same apply() call. Fixed by inserting `let facts = incremental.resolve(&program);` immediately before the FinalReturnTemps step, so it resolves Retval's mark_everything_dirty() before running - caught by inspection before running the differential suite, not by a test failure.

Confirmed this is the genuine cascading case (unlike final_return_temps): removable_dead_local requires def_use.reads.is_empty() && def_use.writes.is_empty(). Deleting one dead `let x = y + 1;` removes one of y's recorded reads, so y can only become provably dead after that removal is reflected in fresh def_use facts - a real cross-round dependency, not just an index-shift artifact. Wired accordingly as a genuine loop (`loop { resolve -> apply -> mark_touched -> break if !changed }`) at both standalone Pass::DeadLocals pipeline steps, using the FixpointLimit::Unlimited-equivalent termination (loop until no change, same guarantee legacy fixpoint passes already relied on - each round's proof-gated rewrite narrows what's still eligible).

Added two new QueryContext predicates (context.rs): dead_local(window, name) -> BindingId (reads AND writes both empty - not the same as sole_use's exactly-one-read shape from final_return_temps) and no_effects(window) -> () (the init expression's EffectFact.effects set is completely empty). Confirmed no_effects is NOT equivalent to the existing pure() query: pure() only requires Purity::MovablePure, but dead_locals's legacy discardable_effect excludes all 10 EffectKind variants including ReadOnlyCall/VolatileRead/AtomicRead, which pure()/Purity classification does NOT treat as disqualifying (those keep purity at ReadOnly, not Effectful). no_effects is strictly narrower than "not Effectful" - its own distinct, more conservative predicate. Ported discardable_known_method/discardable_receiver (the `.len()`/`.as_slice()`/`.as_mut_slice()` structural allowlist) as plain structural checks in the rule case, matching how final_return_temps kept shape-matching out of QueryContext.

late_loop_cleanup (shared by SliceLoop/SliceReduce/RangeLoop cleanup) restructured: still runs the legacy SingletonScopes::fixup over every function first (untouched - singleton_scopes has its own separate migration ticket, .75.38), then builds and applies one query-engine dead_locals plan against the same per-round facts snapshot, `changed |= report.changed`, loops until neither produced a change. Reordering (all SingletonScopes calls, then one batched DeadLocals plan.apply, instead of interleaved per-function) is behaviorally equivalent: DeadLocals's proof for function A never depends on function B's state, and both versions use the exact same round-boundary facts snapshot, reproducing the existing (already-validated) per-round staleness/ordering behavior exactly.

Found and fixed two real, pre-existing incremental-facts coverage gaps while verifying - both latent since slate-04q.75.56.8, never triggered until dead_locals became the first migrated pass to actually chain multiple resolve() calls through mark_touched (not mark_everything_dirty) within one step:

1. def_use was never part of FixupFacts::splice_function's/purge_function_facts's maintained field set (`.8`'s original scope only covered functions/bindings/binding_types/effects/values/string_buffers/string_pointer_views/counted_loops - def_use wasn't needed by any of the six originally-migrated passes). Once dead_locals's loop spliced a function on round 2+, its def_use facts stayed frozen at whatever they were before round 1's edit - reads/writes no longer lined up with the current program. Symptom: anon_local_struct.c produced Rust with dangling `_v6`/`_v12` references to locals that were still genuinely read later but appeared to have zero reads under the stale facts. Fixed by adding def_use::collect_for_function (extracted from collect_facts's existing per-item loop, same shape as the .8.5 precedent) and wiring it into splice_function (extend, ordered after the bindings refresh since it resolves bindings by name+path) and purge_function_facts (retain).

2. borrow_alias had the identical gap - RemoveMut's binding_requires_mut depends on it. Symptom: target_stack_builtin_ops.c's `bytes` array lost its `mut` even though `bytes[0] = ...` writes to it, because RemoveMut ran against a spliced (not fully reanalyzed) snapshot for the function dead_locals had just touched, and borrow_alias in that snapshot was stale. Fixed the same way: borrow_alias::collect_for_function added and wired into splice_function/purge_function_facts.

Both gaps were caught by the full differential suite (cargo nextest r --release), not guessed in advance - confirms the suite is doing its job as the correctness bar for this mechanism, per the user's earlier direction that differential tests are sufficient verification without extra diagnostics.

title: Migrate memchr call rewrites to the query engine
description:
Why: memchr_prelude::fixup_calls is the first end-to-end proof that the query interface makes a real rewrite smaller and easier to audit while preserving differential correctness and downstream pass behavior.

Scope:
- Encode ordered memchr NUL and general byte-position rules using only the query API and typed AST recipes.
- Require positive source/view, value/range, and argument purity/stability proofs; leave the helper call unchanged when evidence is insufficient.
- Preserve the existing pointer-return semantics and the Option/index shape consumed by nullable_pointer and later cleanup passes.
- Replace the pass-local mutable expression walker, fact joins, eligibility helpers, and manual trace logging used only by memchr call rewriting.
- Wire the query pass into the existing MemchrPreludeFixupCalls trace/pass position.
- Recompute facts from the updated AST before the next fact-dependent query/pass and demonstrate that downstream nullable-pointer cleanup sees the newly emitted shape.
- Keep helper-body replacement and unused-helper pruning as legacy passes for this slice.

Out of scope: migrating memchr helper-body replacement, helper pruning, other libc/string rewrites, or changing baseline lowering correctness.
design: Register generated __slate_memchr calls with two ordered cases. The specific case proves needle == 0, derives the first NUL, and proves first_nul < count before building the known-index pointer recipe. The fallback derives a readable full byte view matching count and a stable needle before building iter().position() plus pointer reconstruction. Both cases produce owned ReplaceExpr intents. Apply all non-overlapping call edits from one snapshot, then reanalyze before downstream fact-dependent work. Initially preserve the current structured AST recipe shape so engine migration and further idiomatization remain separate changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- memchr_prelude::fixup_calls uses the query rule interface and no longer owns a recursive mutable AST walk or manual raw-fact joins.
- The NUL rule requires and tests first_nul < count; equal, smaller, or unknown counts cannot incorrectly return the terminator.
- The general rule rewrites only a proven readable byte extent and preserves argument evaluation semantics.
- Insufficient evidence leaves the generated helper call unchanged.
- Existing MemchrPreludeFixupCalls pass identity, ordering, --only-pass/--up-to-pass behavior, and useful trace output remain stable.
- Facts are recomputed after the changed query result before downstream fact-dependent work, and nullable_pointer/late cleanup continue to consume the emitted shape.
- The helper-body and prune passes continue working unchanged.
- Focused differential/output assertions plus cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Migrated memchr call rewriting to the query planner. Added ordered known_nul and byte_position rule cases, stable byte-source/full-view/prefix proofs, lazy query trace evidence and rejection diagnostics, and immediate fact analysis before planning. Preserved helper construction/pruning and downstream nullable-pointer cleanup. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets; focused memchr output/debug/query tests; isolated mem_memchr differential; full cargo nextest r --release (207 passed, 2 skipped); git diff --check.
close_reason: Completed the memchr migration to query-driven AST rewriting with proof-backed ordered cases, trace diagnostics, fact refresh, and passing release validation.

title: Add expression rewrite planning and application
description:
Why: query rules must inspect an immutable AST/fact snapshot but mutate the Program only after all eligibility decisions are complete. The engine should hide traversal, conflict resolution, mutation, and trace bookkeeping from individual rules.

Scope:
- Add the rule/case interface, proof-aware RuleResult, owned ReplaceExpr rewrite intent, and expression plan.
- Allow ordered specific/fallback cases while diagnosing ambiguous same-target results.
- Detect overlapping parent/child expression edits and apply a deterministic non-overlapping batch.
- Resolve planned expression sites during one shared mutable AST traversal and replace only structured rust_ast Expr nodes.
- Emit existing fixup trace events from rule identity, before/after nodes, consumed evidence, and useful rejection reasons without rule-local logging.
- Expose changed/no-change results suitable for once and fixpoint scheduling.

Out of scope: statement insertion/removal, region restructuring, function signatures, program items, and incremental fact invalidation.
design: Planning borrows QueryContext and produces an owned plan containing snapshot targets, replacement Expr values, rule identifiers, and trace evidence. No AST references or snapshot-only fact references survive planning. Application occurs after the immutable context is dropped. Expression replacements preserve path topology, making one-path-map mutable traversal sufficient for the first slice. Same-target cases use explicit registration order or specificity; unintentional overlaps fail visibly rather than silently choosing a rewrite.
acceptance_criteria:
- A concise rule can select call candidates, run proof predicates, and return ReplaceExpr without implementing traversal or mutation.
- Plans own all replacement data and can be applied after dropping Program/FixupFacts borrows.
- Same-target ambiguity and parent/child overlap are handled deterministically and tested.
- Application performs structured Expr replacement and reports whether the Program changed.
- Applied rewrites emit pass-compatible before/after and evidence traces; useful candidate rejection data is available without manual logging in the rule.
- No rendered-source matching or replacement is introduced.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Implemented query-driven expression planning/application in src/fixups/query/rewrite.rs. ExprRule selects candidates and ordered cases; RuleResult yields owned ReplaceExpr intents with semantic evidence. Planning diagnoses rejected candidates and target mismatches, rejects ambiguous same-target proposals, and removes both sides of parent/child overlaps. Application consumes the plan after QueryContext is dropped, performs one shared mutable AST traversal, reports changed/planned/applied counts, and emits pass-compatible trace events with rule/case evidence and fallback rejection facts. Tests cover specific/fallback selection, owned application, traces, no-change scheduling, ambiguity, overlap, and rejection diagnostics. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets; cargo nextest r --release passed 207 tests with 2 skipped.
close_reason: Completed expression rewrite planning and application

title: Add query snapshots and typed fact capabilities
description:
Why: rewrite rules need a compact semantic interface over Program plus FixupFacts instead of pass-local AST walkers and manual joins over fact vectors.

Scope:
- Create src/fixups/query/ and the read-only QueryContext built from one Program/FixupFacts snapshot.
- Introduce owned expression-site identities suitable for planning edits within a snapshot, while treating FunctionId and BindingId as invalid after reanalysis.
- Index expression calls by resolved/generated target and arity without matching only on rendered names.
- Add the first typed capabilities needed by memchr: ByteSource, byte representation, pointer mutability, byte extent, NUL position, constant u8/usize values, and expression purity/stability.
- Adapt BindingFact/BindingTypeFact, StringPointerViewFact, StringBufferFact, ValueFact, and EffectFact behind semantic query methods.
- Return structured missing/contradicted/unsupported proof results rather than plain false where useful for diagnostics.

Out of scope: AST mutation, statement/function/program edit kinds, a standalone textual query language, or copying every FixupFacts record into a second generic database.
design: QueryContext borrows the immutable Program and FixupFacts snapshot and owns only indexes. Rule-visible methods answer semantic questions such as byte_source(arg), const_u8(arg), full_byte_view(source,count), first_nul(source), prefix_contains(count,nul), and pure(expr). Capability values carry the minimum typed data a recipe needs and evidence for tracing. Existing fact collectors remain the source of truth; query adapters may derive relationships such as complete extent or first-NUL position from positive facts. Missing evidence is unknown and cannot authorize a rewrite.
acceptance_criteria:
- src/fixups/query/ exists with a read-only snapshot/context API and owned ExprSite target identity.
- Generated __slate_memchr calls and their arguments can be enumerated without a pass-local recursive walker.
- The memchr-required binding, pointer-view, string-buffer, value, extent, NUL, and purity questions are available through typed query methods.
- Query rules do not manually scan raw FixupFacts vectors or parse rendered Rust source/types where a structured fact or AST type is available.
- Query results retain enough structured evidence or rejection information for later rule tracing.
- Snapshot-local IDs and invalidation after reanalysis are documented and enforced by the API shape.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Implemented read-only src/fixups/query snapshot API with owned ExprSite edit identities, resolved/generated call+arity indexing, typed memchr capabilities, structured proof evidence/rejections, structured binding types, and shared AST target-path resolution. Query tests cover complete views, first-NUL range proofs, constants, purity, unsupported shapes, and resolved/generated targets. Validation: cargo fmt; cargo clippy; focused mem_memchr differential passed; cargo nextest r --release passed 203 tests with 2 skipped.
close_reason: Closed

title: Define memchr query semantics and expand differential coverage
description:
Why: memchr is the first query-engine migration and needs an explicit behavioral oracle before infrastructure changes obscure semantic regressions. The current zero-needle optimization uses a known NUL position without proving that the searched count includes it.

Scope:
- Expand the focused C differential fixture for full-buffer hits and misses, zero-length searches, and NUL searches where count is greater than, equal to, or less than the first NUL index.
- Cover unknown or partial counts, unsupported source provenance, const/mutable pointer views, and a nonconstant but pure needle where practical.
- State the exact proof obligations for the optimized NUL case and the general byte-position case.
- Correct the legacy behavior narrowly if required to keep the new semantic oracle green before the query migration lands.
- Preserve conservative fallback whenever the searched byte range cannot be proven safe.
design: The NUL optimization is legal only when the first NUL index is known and first_nul < count. The general iterator-position rewrite initially requires a proven readable byte view whose extent equals the memchr count. Argument evaluation must remain observable exactly once; fixture cases should expose dropped, duplicated, or delayed evaluation where relevant. This task establishes behavior and output expectations but does not build the query engine.
acceptance_criteria:
- Focused C fixture coverage distinguishes count > first_nul, count == first_nul, and count < first_nul.
- Complete-buffer hit/miss, zero count, unknown/partial count, and unsupported provenance remain differentially correct.
- Output-shape assertions identify which cases rewrite and which remain on the conservative helper path.
- The proof obligations consumed by the future query rules are recorded in the bead notes or relevant design documentation.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes:
Implemented semantic oracle and legacy guard.

Proof obligations for the future query rules:
- Candidate must be the generated __slate_memchr call with exactly source, needle, and count arguments.
- Source must resolve to a supported byte view with binding/type provenance and pointer mutability.
- Known-NUL shortcut requires a well-formed existing string-buffer fact, a known first-NUL index, needle proven equal to zero, and first_nul < count. Equality does not include the terminator. Missing count/range evidence leaves the helper call unchanged.
- General iter().position() rewrite initially requires count proven equal to the complete readable byte extent. Partial/unknown extents and unsupported offset-pointer provenance leave the helper call unchanged.
- Any query migration must preserve evaluation count/order: arguments moved into closures or omitted by the recipe require purity/stability evidence or explicit materialization.

Coverage added in tests/fixtures/mem_memchr.c: runtime-derived pure needle, full-extent mutable and const sources, full hit/miss, zero count, NUL count greater/equal/less than first NUL, volatile runtime partial count, and offset-pointer unsupported provenance.

Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy; cargo nextest r --release (201 passed, 2 skipped).
close_reason: Completed memchr semantic oracle, corrected NUL range proof, and passed all quality gates.

title: Make fixups query-driven and migrate rewrite passes
description:
Why: Slate rewrite passes currently mix AST traversal, local shape matching, fact lookup, proof gating, mutation, scheduling, and tracing. This makes each rewrite larger and harder to audit than the semantic rule it implements. Introduce a query-driven rewrite layer whose rule-authoring interface makes preconditions, captures, and the desired typed AST transformation concise, while allowing the engine and fact adapter to carry the implementation complexity.

Scope:
- Add src/fixups/query/ as the shared query and rewrite-engine implementation.
- Adapt Program plus each facts::analyze snapshot into an indexed query context; existing fact collectors remain the semantic source of truth during migration.
- Centralize node selection/traversal so rules query matching AST nodes and facts instead of implementing pass-local walkers.
- Let rules state positive proof requirements, local versus function/program scope, captures, fallback/specificity, and a typed transformation recipe. The interface need not resemble SQL, Datalog, or another data language; ergonomics and auditability of individual rules are the primary requirement.
- Apply query results deterministically to structured Rust AST nodes, detect conflicting or overlapping edits, and preserve the no-rendered-string-rewrites invariant.
- After a changed query round/pass, analyze the updated AST again before later rules that require fresh facts, preserving the current correctness model while moving scheduling behind the engine.
- Support incremental coexistence with legacy rewrites, then migrate every rewrite pass piece by piece.
- Use memchr_prelude::fixup_calls as the first end-to-end migration, covering its specific NUL-search optimization, general byte-position fallback, and unchanged fallback when proof is insufficient.
- Integrate accepted/rejected rule decisions and consumed facts with fixup tracing; coordinate focused fact provenance/debug behavior with slate-idu.

Out of scope for the first slice: designing a standalone textual query language, migrating every pass at once, incremental fact invalidation, or moving correctness from baseline lowering into fixups.
design:
Create a small rule-authoring surface over a more capable private engine. A rule should identify a node kind/semantic operation, bind arguments and relevant entities, list proof predicates over AST shape and FixupFacts, and return a typed rewrite recipe or no match. Recipes construct rust_ast Expr/Stmt/Item values and may produce expression-local, region, function-signature, or program plans; rendered source is never an input or output of matching.

The query context is built from a Program and immutable FixupFacts snapshot and provides indexed access by FunctionId, BindingId, call identity, and AstPath. Missing evidence is unknown and cannot authorize a rewrite. Universal claims such as all uses or all callers require an explicit complete domain and at least one member, so indirect/escaped/external references stay conservative.

The engine collects intents against one snapshot, rejects ambiguous overlapping intents unless specificity/priority resolves an intentional fallback, applies a deterministic non-overlapping batch, and reports whether the AST changed. Scheduling then invokes facts::analyze on the changed Program before the next fact-dependent round/pass. Start with whole-snapshot recomputation rather than incremental invalidation.

During migration, query-backed and legacy passes share the existing pass ordering and trace identities. The memchr migration establishes the vertical slice: AST/call lookup, value and string/buffer fact predicates, ordered specific/general alternatives, typed Expr construction, trace provenance, reanalysis, differential behavior, and unchanged fallback. Later child work migrates passes by semantic cluster until pass-local matching/walking boilerplate can be removed.
acceptance_criteria:
- src/fixups/query/ exists and exposes a documented, typed rule interface centered on declarative preconditions/captures plus a transformation recipe; a typical call rewrite does not implement its own recursive AST walker or manually join raw fact vectors.
- Program and FixupFacts snapshots can be converted/indexed into the query context without changing collector semantics, and rules can query nodes, call identities, values, bindings, effects, and domain-completeness proofs needed by migrated passes.
- Query execution updates only structured rust_ast nodes, is deterministic, detects conflicting/overlapping edits, and emits rule-level trace evidence for applied and useful rejected candidates.
- A changed fact-dependent query round is followed by facts::analyze on the updated AST before the next dependent rule/pass; tests demonstrate that a later rule sees facts exposed by an earlier rewrite.
- memchr_prelude::fixup_calls is migrated first with behavioral and output-shape parity or improvement, including correct first-n-byte bounds for NUL search, byte-position fallback when proven safe, and no rewrite when evidence is insufficient.
- Legacy and query-backed passes coexist throughout migration with stable pass ordering and fixup-debug behavior.
- Every existing rewrite is represented by child migration work and the epic closes only after all rewrite passes use the query method where applicable, bespoke traversal/matching boilerplate has been removed, and docs/facts.md, docs/writing-a-fixup.md, and docs/passes.md describe the new workflow.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass for each implementation slice and as the final completion gate.
notes:
First implementation milestone: establish the query directory, snapshot adapter, minimal rule API, engine scheduling/reanalysis, and migrate memchr_prelude::fixup_calls. Create focused child beads before implementation.

title: Lower fenv_t and femode_t ABI types from trusted headers
description: Calls using <fenv.h> aggregate types reach Rust generation, but Slate emits extern declarations and locals referencing fenv_t and femode_t without emitting either type. On active x86_64 glibc, fenv_t is a 32-byte ABI record and femode_t is an 8-byte ABI record; fexcept_t already lowers to u16. Preserve tests/stdlib/fenv/environment.c and tests/stdlib/fenv/mode.c as minimal e2e reproductions. Investigate representing trusted-header aggregate typedefs with correct target-specific size, alignment, field layout, and const pointer signatures so fegetenv/feholdexcept/fesetenv/feupdateenv and fegetmode/fesetmode compile and differentially match.
acceptance_criteria: The fenv/environment and fenv/mode stdlib probes translate to Rust with ABI-correct definitions for fenv_t and femode_t; all six affected functions compile, link, run, and differentially match C; unsupported ratchet entries are removed; release quality gates pass.
notes: Observed generated Rust declares fegetenv/fesetenv/feholdexcept/feupdateenv with pointers to fenv_t and fegetmode/fesetmode with pointers to femode_t, and declares locals of those types, but emits no Rust definitions. Compilation fails with E0412/E0425 missing types. Active x86_64 glibc reports sizeof(fenv_t)=32 and sizeof(femode_t)=8; fexcept_t lowers successfully to u16. Minimal reproductions are ratcheted as fenv/environment and fenv/mode.
close_reason: Closed

title: Support #pragma STDC CX_LIMITED_RANGE

notes:
Inventoried the C23 <threads.h> surface against cppreference and the active glibc header. Added one consolidated deterministic fixture at tests/stdlib/threads/functions.c covering all 25 mandatory functions: the eight thrd_* functions, six mtx_* functions, six cnd_* functions, four tss_* functions, and call_once. It also exercises thrd_t/thrd_start_t, mtx_t, cnd_t, tss_t/tss_dtor_t, once_flag/ONCE_FLAG_INIT, TSS_DTOR_ITERATIONS, all thread result constants, and all mutex type constants. The C11 thread_local convenience macro is removed from the C23 interface, though the active glibc header still exposes it as a compatibility macro for this Clang configuration.

The fixture uses a condition-variable handshake for deterministic cnd_wait/cnd_signal behavior, an expired absolute deadline for cnd_timedwait, an immediately available timed mutex for mtx_timedlock, a recursive mutex for repeated locking, joined workers for TSS destructor and thrd_exit behavior, and an atomic completion flag for the detached worker. The C fixture prints stable statuses and completes without scheduler-dependent ordering.

No unsupported lowering was found. Slate already emits target-correct opaque mtx_t/cnd_t layouts, thrd_t/tss_t aliases, extern declarations, C-ABI callbacks, noreturn thrd_exit, and direct FFI calls for the entire header. The consolidated fixture translates, compiles, links, and differentially matches C, so no implementation child ticket was filed; creating one would not represent an observed gap. Validation: cargo nextest r --release --test stdlib_coverage --nocapture passes with threads/functions enabled, cargo fmt and cargo clippy pass, cargo nextest r --release passes 201 tests with 2 skipped, and git diff --check passes.
close_reason: Completed exhaustive C23 threads.h coverage; all interfaces already pass baseline FFI lowering, so no implementation gap was filed.

notes:
Inventoried the mandatory C23 <complex.h> surface: 22 function families in float, double, and long double forms (66 functions), CMPLXF/CMPLX/CMPLXL, the complex/_Complex_I/I and version macros, and CX_LIMITED_RANGE. Per user direction, replaced the prior cabs-only probe with one consolidated tests/stdlib/complex/functions.c fixture that prints a labeled result for all 66 functions and all three constructors (69 lines total). The complete fixture exposes one shared lowering failure: generated alloca frames initialize Complex<LongDouble> members with untyped integer zeros, so Rust compilation fails before long-double complex ABI behavior can be checked. This is tracked by slate-nk3.25.2, and complex/functions is registered in KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED against that bead. The standard CX_LIMITED_RANGE pragma is independently rejected by the directive layer; its minimal reproduction is preserved at tests/fixtures.unsupported/stdlib_complex_cx_limited_range.c and tracked by slate-nk3.25.1.

title: Fixup runner batch 11: unused params and final cleanup
description: Migrate this five-pass batch to the explicit Fixup runner architecture tracked by slate-04q.63. Covered scheduled passes: UnusedParams, FinalReturns, MainZeroExit. Each pass call site must visibly choose run-once or to-fixpoint execution. Eligible body passes should implement the common Fixup trait with all logger, facts, function identity, phase, and configuration dependencies stored on the pass struct; fixup itself takes only the function body and reports whether that round changed it. Facts-invalidating fixpoint passes must explicitly reanalyze between rounds. Program-wide or FnDef-level passes that cannot honestly use the body trait remain explicit exceptions. This final partial batch covers the remaining three scheduled passes and completes the Pass::ALL inventory.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exactly these scheduled pass boundaries are migrated or documented as explicit non-body exceptions: UnusedParams, FinalReturns, MainZeroExit.
- Eligible pass structs implement the shared body Fixup interface and no longer rely on thin module-level NoopLogger wrappers.
- apply_with_logger visibly selects run_once_items or to_fixpoint_items and the required fact-refresh policy for every covered pass.
- No covered pass hides a completion loop inside one Fixup invocation.
- Pass order, repeated pipeline occurrences, skip/debug behavior, trace events, and generated Rust remain unchanged.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Implemented the final three-pass runner batch. UnusedParams is an explicit program-wide exception scheduled to fixpoint across the whole Program, with one removal per round. FinalReturns and MainZeroExit now implement the shared body Fixup trait, store their function metadata/configuration on the pass struct, and are instantiated inline before run_once. Removed the covered modules' obsolete NoopLogger wrapper functions. Preserved the pre-existing StructFieldInit wrapper deletion. Validation: cargo fmt; cargo clippy --all-targets; cargo nextest r --release (176 passed, 2 skipped); git diff --check.

title: Unify body rewrite passes behind explicit Fixup runners
description:
Why: fixup orchestration in src/fixups/mod.rs obscures whether a rewrite runs once or to convergence. Most rewrite modules expose a thin module::fixup function that creates a NoopLogger-backed pass struct and immediately calls its method, while the production pipeline separately constructs the same struct and repeats item/function traversal and fixpoint loops. Facts-backed fixpoint passes also duplicate analyze-visit-repeat logic.

Refactor the body-oriented rewrite passes around one Fixup trait whose only method input is &mut Vec<IndentStmt> and whose boolean result reports whether that invocation changed the body. Each pass struct should own or borrow every other dependency it needs, including the logger, FunctionId, FixupFacts, pass phase, and configuration. Remove convergence loops from individual pass implementations so orchestration, not the pass, states whether it runs once or to a fixpoint.

Add explicit shared runners for run-once and to-fixpoint execution over function items. The call site in apply_with_logger must instantiate the concrete pass and select the runner, making convergence behavior obvious. Facts-backed passes must use the same runner model with an explicit fact-refresh policy that reanalyzes the program between fixpoint rounds when required. Prefer a parameter or small policy enum on the common runner family over a parallel helper if that remains clear and borrow-checker-friendly; otherwise use a clearly named to_fixpoint_items_with_facts helper.

Start from the existing Fixup implementations for struct_field_init and var_aliases. Audit body-oriented passes and migrate their thin module::fixup wrappers and hand-written loops. Program-wide or FnDef-shape rewrites that cannot honestly implement the body trait should remain explicit and be documented as exceptions rather than forced through a misleading adapter.
design:
Target shape:
- Fixup::fixup(&mut self, body: &mut Vec<IndentStmt>) -> bool performs one invocation/round.
- run_once_items makes a single pass over eligible function bodies.
- to_fixpoint_items repeats until a full program round reports no change.
- Facts-aware execution analyzes at the required boundary and constructs a pass with FunctionId plus FixupFacts already stored in the struct. For fixpoint passes that can invalidate facts, reanalyze before every round.
- apply_with_logger explicitly constructs each concrete pass and visibly chooses run_once_items or to_fixpoint_items plus the fact-refresh policy.
- Preserve special bounded convergence such as inline temp round limits through an explicit runner option or documented specialized runner.

Likely facts-refresh migrations include zero_init, dead_locals, call_args, final_return_temps, and atomic_compare_exchange. Plain body fixpoint migrations include struct_field_init, var_aliases, constant_conditions, ptr_copy, for_continue, singleton_scopes, and other eligible passes. Confirm the final list by auditing src/fixups/rewrite.
acceptance_criteria:
- Eligible body rewrite structs implement one common Fixup trait and take only &mut Vec<IndentStmt> in fixup; logger, facts, function identity, phase, and pass-specific configuration live on the struct.
- Thin module-level fixup wrappers that only create a NoopLogger and delegate are removed or replaced by direct pass construction in tests and production.
- Shared run_once_items and to_fixpoint_items runners exist, and every migrated call site explicitly selects one.
- Facts-backed runners support explicit reanalysis between fixpoint rounds; zero_init and every other facts-invalidating loop preserve current reanalysis behavior.
- A Fixup invocation performs one round; passes such as var_aliases do not hide their own completion loop beneath the shared fixpoint runner.
- Program-wide/FnDef-level passes that cannot use the body trait are audited and left as clear, documented exceptions.
- Pass ordering, skip/debug boundaries, rewrite logging, generated Rust, and differential behavior remain unchanged.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass; all test commands use nextest.
close_reason: Closed
